complete the lesson.

lessons.title: This one, that one: 这个, 那个, 些, 第
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Lesson 13 put a measure word between a number and a noun: {两|liǎng}{本|běn}{书|shū}. This lesson
uses the same slot after "this", "that" and "which": {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū} (this book),
{那个|nà ge}{人|rén} (that person), {哪个|nǎ ge}？ (which one?). You'll learn {些|xiē} for plurals
(these, those, some), {第|dì} for "first, second, third", and the words you need in a
{超市|chāo shì} (supermarket): fruit, apples, milk and eggs.

## This, that, which + measure word

{这|zhè} (this), {那|nà} (that) and {哪|nǎ} (which) are **[[demonstratives]]**: words that point at
something. In lesson 03 you used {这|zhè} and {那|nà} alone with {是|shì}: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}.
In front of a noun they need a measure word, exactly like a number:

| Number | Demonstrative | |
|---|---|---|
| {一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū} — a book | {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū} — this book | {那|nà}{本|běn}{书|shū} — that book |
| {一|yí}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu} — a piece of clothing | {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu} — this (piece of) clothing | {哪|nǎ}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}？ — which (piece of) clothing? |
| {一|yí}{个|gè}{人|rén} — a person | {这个|zhè ge}{人|rén} — this person | {那个|nà ge}{人|rén} — that person |

{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？ — How much is this book?
{那个|nà ge}{人|rén}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{老师|lǎo shī}。 — That person is my teacher.
{你|nǐ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{哪|nǎ}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}？ — Which piece of clothing would you like to buy?

Leaving the measure word out, ~~{这|zhè}{书|shū}~~, is the classic mistake. (In fast speech you'll
hear {这|zhè} + noun without a measure word now and then, but say it in full.) After a
demonstrative, {个|gè} is usually light: *zhège*, *nàge*.

Demonstrative and number together: the demonstrative comes first.

{这|zhè}{两|liǎng}{本|běn}{书|shū} — these two books
{那|nà}{三|sān}{个|gè}{苹果|píng guǒ} — those three apples

## This one, that one: {这个|zhè ge}, {那个|nà ge}, {哪个|nǎ ge}

With {个|gè} and no noun, the demonstratives mean "this one", "that one", "which one": the word
you use most when pointing in a shop.

{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{这个|zhè ge}。 — I'll have this one.
{那个|nà ge}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？ — How much is that one?
{你|nǐ}{要|yào}{哪个|nǎ ge}？ — Which one do you want?

{哪个|nǎ ge} is a question word like {什么|shén me}: it stays in the place of the answer, and the
sentence needs no {吗|ma}. Ask {哪个|nǎ ge}？ → answer {这个|zhè ge}。

Pronunciation. In everyday northern speech these words are often said *zhèige*, *nèige* and
*něige*. You'll hear both forms; this course writes the dictionary forms, *zhège*, *nàge*, *nǎge*.
Mind the tones of {那|nà} (falling: that) and {哪|nǎ} (dipping: which), written with a different
character too: 哪 has 口 on the left, like the question particles 吗 and 呢.

## Plurals: {这些|zhè xiē}, {那些|nà xiē}, {哪些|nǎ xiē}

{些|xiē} is a measure word for "a number of": with a demonstrative it makes a plural, and it
*replaces* the other measure word.

{这些|zhè xiē}{书|shū} — these books (not ~~{这些|zhè xiē}{本|běn}{书|shū}~~)
{那些|nà xiē}{苹果|píng guǒ} — those apples
{哪些|nǎ xiē}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}？ — which fruits?
{这些|zhè xiē}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}。 — These are mine.

Nouns themselves don't change for plural (lesson 02's -{们|men} is only for people), so {这些|zhè xiē}
and {那些|nà xiē} are often the only sign of a plural in the sentence.

## Some: {一些|yì xiē}

{一些|yì xiē} is "some, a few", for things you could count or not:

{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{一些|yì xiē}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}。 — I'd like to buy some fruit.
{我们|wǒ men}{买|mǎi}{一些|yì xiē}{鸡蛋|jī dàn}{吧|ba}。 — Let's buy some eggs.

Compare {一点儿|yì diǎnr} (lesson 12): "a little", a small amount, often of something you don't
count ({一点儿|yì diǎnr}{水|shuǐ}). {一些|yì xiē} is "some", and needn't be small.

(Lesson 24 brings {有的|yǒu de}, "some (of them)", for statements like "some apples are
expensive, some are cheap".)

## First, second, third: {第|dì} + number

Put {第|dì} before a number to make an ordinal: {第|dì}{一|yī} (first), {第|dì}{二|èr} (second),
{第|dì}{三|sān} (third)… With a noun, the measure word follows as usual:

{第|dì}{一|yī}{天|tiān} — the first day
{第|dì}{二|èr}{个|gè}{人|rén} — the second person
{第|dì}{三|sān}{本|běn}{书|shū} — the third book
{这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{第|dì}{一|yī}{次|cì}{来|lái}{中国|Zhōng guó}。 — This is my first time in China. ({次|cì}, time, occurrence, is HSK 2's.)

Two rules from earlier lessons apply: in an ordinal, {一|yī} keeps its first tone (*dì yī*, not
*dì yí*), and "second" is {第|dì}{二|èr}, never ~~{第|dì}{两|liǎng}~~, because {两|liǎng} counts and
{二|èr} is the number's name.

## At the supermarket

| Word | Meaning | Note |
|---|---|---|
| {超市|chāo shì} | supermarket | {超|chāo} "super" + {市|shì} "market" |
| {水果|shuǐ guǒ} | fruit | {水|shuǐ} water + {果|guǒ} fruit: "juicy fruit" |
| {苹果|píng guǒ} | apple | |
| {牛奶|niú nǎi} | milk | {牛|niú} cow + {奶|nǎi} milk |
| {鸡蛋|jī dàn} | egg | {鸡|jī} chicken + {蛋|dàn} egg: a hen's egg |

Fruit is counted with {个|gè} ({三|sān}{个|gè}{苹果|píng guǒ}). Prices are often given per item or by
weight; {两|liǎng}{块|kuài}{一|yí}{个|gè} means "two kuai each" (literally "two kuai, one"). Weights
such as {斤|jīn} (half a kilo, the market unit) come in a later course.

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 些 | some, a few | xiē | 二 | 8 | {这些|zhè xiē}, {那些|nà xiē}, {一些|yì xiē} |
| 苹 (traditional 蘋) | apple (in 苹果) | píng | 艹 | 8 | {苹果|píng guǒ} |
| 果 | fruit; result | guǒ | 木 | 8 | {苹果|píng guǒ}, {水果|shuǐ guǒ} |
| 第 | (ordinal prefix) | dì | ⺮ | 11 | {第|dì}{一|yī}, {第|dì}{二|èr} |
| 牛 | cow, ox | niú | 牛 | 4 | {牛奶|niú nǎi} |
| 奶 | milk | nǎi | 女 | 5 | {牛奶|niú nǎi}, {奶奶|nǎi nai} (grandma, HSK 2) |
| 鸡 (traditional 雞) | chicken | jī | 鸟 | 7 | {鸡蛋|jī dàn} |
| 蛋 | egg | dàn | 虫 | 11 | {鸡蛋|jī dàn} |
| 超 | exceed; super | chāo | 走 | 12 | {超市|chāo shì} |
| 市 | market; city | shì | 巾 | 5 | {超市|chāo shì} |

- 果 is a tree (木) with fruit on top: one of the pictographs you can still see.
- 牛 started as an ox's head with horns. Its last stroke, the vertical, goes through everything.
- 第 is ⺮ (bamboo) + 弟, which you know from {弟弟|dì di}: the sound part, and it's the same
  syllable, *dì*. A memory aid for the meaning "order": bamboo strips, tied together in order,
  were early books.
- 奶 is 女 (woman) + 乃 (*nǎi*), meaning plus sound again.
- 超 has 走 (walk) from lesson 08 (in 起): going past, "exceed". 市 is a market; {超市|chāo shì} is a
  word-for-word "super market".
- In traditional characters some of these look very different: 苹 is 蘋 and 鸡 is 雞 (the 鸟 "bird"
  radical becomes 隹, another bird). The switch shows them.

### New radicals

⺮, "bamboo on top" ({竹字头|zhú zì tóu}). The character 竹 (bamboo) squeezed onto the top of a
character: six short strokes. Characters with it are often things made of bamboo or done with
bamboo: brushes, slips, baskets, chopsticks. You have 第; later come 笔 (pen, HSK 2) and 筷
in {筷子|kuài zi} (chopsticks, HSK 3). Don't confuse it with 艹 (grass), three strokes.

欠, "yawn" ({欠|qiàn}). A person with the mouth wide open; as a character it now means "to
owe". It's the right side of 欢 in {喜欢|xǐ huan} (lesson 11), and you'll meet it in 歌 (song,
lesson 22) and 次 (time, HSK 2).

牛, "cow, ox" ({牛|niú}). As a whole character it's the 牛 of {牛奶|niú nǎi}. On the left of a
character it becomes 牜, narrower, with the last horizontal rising: you'll see that form in 物 and
特 in later courses.

### Stroke order

- 牛: the short left-falling stroke, the upper horizontal, the long lower horizontal, and
  last the vertical straight through.
- 鸡: 又 first (two strokes), then 鸟: the short left-falling stroke, the horizontal that turns
  down with a hook, the dot inside, the long vertical that turns twice and hooks, and the bottom
  horizontal last.
- 果: 日 first (four strokes), then the long horizontal, then the vertical, which starts at the
  top of 日 and runs down through everything, and last the two falling strokes (left, then right).
- 第: ⺮ first, then 弟 below it.

```trace
些苹果第牛
```

```trace
奶鸡蛋超市
```

=}

## Dialogue: in the supermarket

{安娜|Ān nà} (安娜) and {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (王芳) are shopping.

```dialogue
# In the supermarket
安娜: {王芳|Wáng Fāng}，{你|nǐ}{看|kàn}，{这些|zhè xiē}{苹果|píng guǒ}{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}！
= Wang Fang, look, these apples are cheap!
王芳: {对|duì}，{两|liǎng}{块|kuài}{一|yí}{个|gè}。{我们|wǒ men}{买|mǎi}{一些|yì xiē}{吧|ba}。
= Yes, two kuai each. Let's buy some.
安娜: {好|hǎo}。{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{这个|zhè ge}、{这个|zhè ge}{和|hé}{那个|nà ge}。
= OK. I'll have this one, this one and that one.
王芳: {那个|nà ge}{不|bú}{太|tài}{好|hǎo}，{你|nǐ}{要|yào}{这个|zhè ge}{吧|ba}。
= That one's not very good; take this one.
安娜: {好|hǎo}。{你|nǐ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{什么|shén me}？
= OK. What would you like to buy?
王芳: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{牛奶|niú nǎi}{和|hé}{鸡蛋|jī dàn}。{哪些|nǎ xiē}{牛奶|niú nǎi}{便宜|pián yi}？
= I want milk and eggs. Which milk is cheap?
安娜: {这些|zhè xiē}{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}，{那些|nà xiē}{很|hěn}{贵|guì}。
= These are cheap; those are expensive.
王芳: {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{这些|zhè xiē}{吧|ba}。
= I'll get these, then.
安娜: {那|nà}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}？{很|hěn}{大|dà}！
= What fruit is that? It's huge!
王芳: {那|nà}{是|shì}{西瓜|xī guā}，{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}！
= That's a watermelon. It's delicious!
```

{西瓜|xī guā} (watermelon, "western melon") is an HSK 3 word. The 、 in Anna's line is the
enumeration comma, used between items in a list. And notice {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{这些|zhè xiē}{吧|ba}: with
{我|wǒ}, {吧|ba} sounds like "I'll go with these, then".

## Reading: David's first Saturday

> {我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{大卫|Dà wèi}，{今天|jīn tiān}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{的|de}{第|dì}{一|yī}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}。{上午|shàng wǔ}{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{李明|Lǐ Míng}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}。{超市|chāo shì}{很|hěn}{大|dà}，{东西|dōng xi}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{多|duō}。{李明|Lǐ Míng}{买|mǎi}{牛奶|niú nǎi}{和|hé}{鸡蛋|jī dàn}，{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{一些|yì xiē}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}。{那些|nà xiē}{苹果|píng guǒ}{不|bú}{贵|guì}，{三|sān}{块|kuài}{一|yí}{个|gè}，{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{五|wǔ}{个|gè}。{苹果|píng guǒ}{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}，{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}。

1. What is special about today for David?
2. What does Li Ming buy?
3. How much is one apple, and how many does David buy?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. It's his first Saturday in Beijing ({第|dì}{一|yī}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù}).
2. Milk and eggs.
3. Three kuai each; he buys five.

"My name is David. Today is my first Saturday in Beijing. In the morning Li Ming and I go to the
supermarket to buy some things. The supermarket is big, and there's lots of stuff. Li Ming buys
milk and eggs; I buy some fruit. Those apples aren't expensive, three kuai each, and I buy five.
The apples are tasty; I really like them."
</details>

{第|dì}{一|yī}{个|gè}{星期|xīng qī}{六|liù} shows the full ordinal pattern: {第|dì} + number + measure word +
noun.

## Say it

```speak
{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{这个|zhè ge}。
= I'll have this one.
{那个|nà ge}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？
= How much is that one?
{你|nǐ}{要|yào}{哪个|nǎ ge}？
= Which one do you want?
{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{一些|yì xiē}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}。
= I'd like to buy some fruit.
{这|zhè}{是|shì}{第|dì}{一|yī}{天|tiān}。
= This is the first day.
```

## Pronunciation

- {那|nà} (that) falls; {哪|nǎ} (which) dips. {那个|nà ge}？ and {哪个|nǎ ge}？ ask different things.
- {些|xiē}: *x* + *ie*, level: "syeh". After {一|yī} it makes {一|yì} fall: *yì xiē*.
- {水果|shuǐ guǒ}: two third tones, so the first rises: said *shuí guǒ*. {牛奶|niú nǎi} is 2 + 3, no
  change.
- {苹果|píng guǒ}: *píng* rises, then a low *guǒ*.
- {第|dì}{一|yī}: {一|yī} stays first tone in ordinals.
- {鸡蛋|jī dàn}: *j* is like the English "j" in "jeep" with the tongue tip down; level, then falling.

## Common mistakes

- No measure word after a demonstrative: ~~{这|zhè}{书|shū}~~, ~~{那|nà}{衣服|yī fu}~~. Say
  {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}, {那|nà}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}.
- Two measure words: ~~{这些|zhè xiē}{本|běn}{书|shū}~~. {些|xiē} is the measure word: {这些|zhè xiē}{书|shū}.
- ~~{第|dì}{两|liǎng}~~ for "second": the ordinal is {第|dì}{二|èr}.
- Reading the ordinal {第|dì}{一|yī} as *dì yí*: {一|yī} doesn't change in ordinals.
- {吗|ma} after a {哪个|nǎ ge} question: ~~{你|nǐ}{要|yào}{哪个|nǎ ge}{吗|ma}？~~ The question word already
  asks.
- English order with numbers: ~~{两|liǎng}{这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}~~. The demonstrative comes first:
  {这|zhè}{两|liǎng}{本|běn}{书|shū}.

## Key points

- Demonstrative + measure word + noun: {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}, {那|nà}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu},
  {哪个|nǎ ge}{人|rén}？ With a number: {这|zhè}{两|liǎng}{本|běn}{书|shū}.
- {这个|zhè ge} / {那个|nà ge} / {哪个|nǎ ge}: this one / that one / which one.
- {这些|zhè xiē} / {那些|nà xiē} / {哪些|nǎ xiē}: {些|xiē} replaces the measure word. {一些|yì xiē}: some.
- {第|dì} + number (+ measure word + noun): {第|dì}{一|yī}, {第|dì}{二|èr}{个|gè}{人|rén}; {一|yī} stays yī.
- Supermarket words: {超市|chāo shì}, {水果|shuǐ guǒ}, {苹果|píng guǒ}, {牛奶|niú nǎi}, {鸡蛋|jī dàn}.
- New radicals: ⺮ (bamboo), 欠 (yawn), 牛 (cow).

The words from this lesson are listed below; they join your vocabulary reviews when you
complete the lesson.

lessons.title: Clothes and describing: 很, 非常, 真 and A-not-A questions
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

You've been saying {很|hěn}{贵|guì} and {很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi} for two lessons. This lesson explains how
these describing sentences work, and adds stronger words than {很|hěn}: {非常|fēi cháng} (extremely)
and {真|zhēn} (really!). You'll learn a second way to ask yes/no questions, {贵|guì}{不|bu}{贵|guì}？
("expensive or not?"), the all-purpose {怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ (how is it?), and {对|duì} (right).
The topic is clothes: {衣服|yī fu}, {穿|chuān} (to wear), {新|xīn} (new), {漂亮|piào liang} (pretty).
And there's {一半|yí bàn}, half, for sharing.

## Adjectives as the predicate: no {是|shì}

In English, "is" joins a subject and an adjective: "The coat *is* pretty." In Chinese the
adjective itself is the predicate, the part that says something about the subject. There's no
verb "to be":

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。 — This piece of clothing is (very) pretty.
{书|shū}{很|hěn}{贵|guì}。 — Books are expensive.
{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 — I'm fine. (lesson 01)

A sentence like this is an **[[adjective predicate]]** sentence. Its rule is short:

| Subject | (degree word) | Adjective |
|---|---|---|
| {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu} | {很|hěn} | {漂亮|piào liang} |
| {饺子|jiǎo zi} | {非常|fēi cháng} | {好吃|hǎo chī} |
| {苹果|píng guǒ} | {不|bú} | {贵|guì} |

Putting {是|shì} in, ~~{衣服|yī fu}{是|shì}{漂亮|piào liang}~~, is the most common mistake English
speakers make in Chinese. {是|shì} links two nouns ({他|tā}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}); an adjective doesn't
need it.

Why {很|hěn}? A bare adjective sounds like a comparison: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì} on its own
suggests "this one is the expensive one (and that one isn't)". That's useful for contrasts:

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì}，{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{便宜|pián yi}。 — This one is expensive, that one is cheap.

For a plain statement, people add {很|hěn}, which then often means no more than "is". When you
really mean "very", stress it, or choose a stronger word.

## Degree adverbs: {很|hěn}, {非常|fēi cháng}, {真|zhēn}, {太|tài}

Words that say *how much* go right before the adjective. They're called **[[degree adverbs]]**:

| Word | Strength | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| {很|hěn} | plain (often weak) | {很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang} | (very) pretty |
| {非常|fēi cháng} | strong | {非常|fēi cháng}{漂亮|piào liang} | extremely pretty |
| {真|zhēn} | exclamation | {真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}！ | it's really pretty! |
| {太|tài}…{了|le} | exclamation, often "too" | {太|tài}{贵|guì}{了|le}！ | too expensive! / so expensive! |
| {不|bú}{太|tài} | weak negative | {不|bú}{太|tài}{贵|guì} | not very expensive |

- {非常|fēi cháng} is a strong "very, extremely". It's common in speech and in writing.
- {真|zhēn} expresses your own surprise or feeling, like "really!" or "so!": {你|nǐ}{真|zhēn}{好|hǎo}！
  (You're so kind!) {真|zhēn} also means "real, true". Use it in statements, not in questions.
- {太|tài}…{了|le} you know from lesson 12.

Negatives put {不|bù} before the adjective: {不|bú}{贵|guì}, {不|bù}{好看|hǎo kàn}, {不|bú}{漂亮|piào liang}.
Never {没|méi}: ~~{没|méi}{贵|guì}~~.

## A-not-A questions: {贵|guì}{不|bu}{贵|guì}？

Besides {吗|ma}, Chinese can ask a yes/no question by saying the adjective or verb twice, with
{不|bu} between: "expensive not expensive?" This is an **[[A-not-A question]]**:

{贵|guì}{不|bu}{贵|guì}？ — Is it expensive?
{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{漂亮|piào liang}{不|bu}{漂亮|piào liang}？ — Is this pretty?
{你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{不|bu}{喜欢|xǐ huan}？ — Do you like it?
{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{不|bu}{去|qù}？ — Are you going?

Three rules:

1. No {吗|ma}: the A-not-A form is already the question. ~~{贵|guì}{不|bu}{贵|guì}{吗|ma}？~~
2. {不|bu} is light (neutral tone) in the middle: *guì bu guì*. This course writes it *bu*.
3. Answer with A or not-A: {贵|guì}。/ {不|bú}{贵|guì}。 With {有|yǒu}, the "not" is {没|méi}:
   {有|yǒu}{没有|méi yǒu}？ (Is there…? / Do you have…?)

With a two-syllable word, speakers often shorten the first half: {漂|piào}{不|bu}{漂亮|piào liang}？,
{喜|xǐ}{不|bu}{喜欢|xǐ huan}？ Both are correct.

A-not-A questions sound a little more direct than {吗|ma} questions, as if you really want the
answer; both are everyday Chinese.

## How is it? {怎么样|zěn me yàng}

{怎么样|zěn me yàng} asks for an opinion: "How is it? What do you think of it?" It goes where the
adjective would go:

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ — What do you think of this top?
— {很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}！ — It looks great!
{你|nǐ}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ — How are you doing?

After a suggestion, it means "how about it?":

{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}，{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ — Let's go to the supermarket. How about it?

## Right: {对|duì}

{对|duì} is "right, correct". On its own it's the usual way to say "yes, that's right":

A: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{大卫|Dà wèi}{吗|ma}？ — Are you David?
B: {对|duì}。 — That's right.
{不|bú}{对|duì}。 — That's not right. / That's wrong.

You know it already from {对不起|duì bu qǐ} (sorry). {对|duì} is also a preposition, "to,
towards" ({他|tā}{对|duì}{我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}, he's good to me), which a later lesson uses.

## Half: {一半|yí bàn}

{一半|yí bàn} is "half (of something)": a share or a part, unlike {半|bàn} in {八|bā}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}
(half past eight) or {半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí} (half an hour), from lesson 07.

{一半|yí bàn}{是|shì}{你|nǐ}{的|de}。 — Half is yours.
{我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{一半|yí bàn}，{你|nǐ}{吃|chī}{一半|yí bàn}。 — I'll eat half, you eat half.
{我们|wǒ men}{一|yì}{人|rén}{一半|yí bàn}。 — Half each. (literally "one person, one half")

## Clothes: {衣服|yī fu}, {穿|chuān}, {新|xīn}

{衣服|yī fu} is clothes in general, or one garment, counted with {件|jiàn}: {一|yí}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}.
English has many words for garments; at HSK 1 this one word does the job. ({裤子|kù zi}, trousers,
and others come in HSK 2.)

{穿|chuān} is "to wear" and "to put on":

{今天|jīn tiān}{你|nǐ}{穿|chuān}{什么|shén me}？ — What are you wearing today?
{她|tā}{穿|chuān}{新|xīn}{衣服|yī fu}。 — She's wearing new clothes.

A one-syllable adjective such as {新|xīn} can go straight before its noun: {新|xīn}{衣服|yī fu}
(new clothes), {新|xīn}{书|shū} (a new book). With {很|hěn} or a two-syllable adjective, put {的|de}
in between: {很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}{的|de}{衣服|yī fu} (very pretty clothes).

## {漂亮|piào liang} and {好看|hǎo kàn}

Both describe how something looks:

- {漂亮|piào liang}: pretty, beautiful, smart. For people (of any gender, though more often women
  and children), clothes, places and things.
- {好看|hǎo kàn}: good-looking, nice to look at ({好|hǎo} + {看|kàn}, like {好吃|hǎo chī}). It also
  describes films and books that are good to watch or read.

{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}。 and {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。 are
both natural.

## Characters
{=

| Character | Meaning | Pinyin | Radical | Strokes | Words |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 衣 | clothing | yī | 衣 | 6 | {衣服|yī fu} |
| 服 | clothes; to serve | fu (fú) | 月 | 8 | {衣服|yī fu} |
| 穿 | wear; pierce | chuān | 穴 | 9 | {穿|chuān} |
| 新 | new | xīn | 斤 | 13 | {新|xīn}, {新年|xīn nián} (New Year, HSK 3) |
| 漂 | (in 漂亮) | piào | 氵 | 14 | {漂亮|piào liang} |
| 亮 | bright | liang (liàng) | 亠 | 9 | {漂亮|piào liang}, {月亮|yuè liang} (moon, HSK 3) |
| 非 | not; wrong | fēi | 非 | 8 | {非常|fēi cháng} |
| 常 | often; usual | cháng | 巾 | 11 | {非常|fēi cháng}, {常常|cháng cháng} (often, HSK 3) |
| 真 | real; really | zhēn | 目 | 10 | {真|zhēn} |
| 对 ✎ (traditional 對) | right, correct; towards | duì | 寸 | 5 | {对|duì}, {对不起|duì bu qǐ} |
| 怎 | how | zěn | 心 | 9 | {怎么样|zěn me yàng}, {怎么|zěn me} (how, lesson 18) |
| 样 (traditional 樣) | shape, appearance | yàng | 木 | 10 | {怎么样|zěn me yàng}, {一样|yí yàng} (the same, HSK 3) |

The other ten are written the same in traditional script; in Traditional the tracing pads show
對 and 樣.

- 衣 started as a picture of a jacket: the collar at the top, the sleeves and the hem. On the
  left of a character it becomes the narrow form 衤, as in 裤 (trousers, HSK 2).
- 新 is 亲 + 斤, an axe. In 亲, 木 (wood) sits under a shortened 辛 (xīn), which gives the
  sound. The usual explanation of the origin: chopping wood with an axe, and from that "fresh,
  new".
- 穿 is 穴 (a hole) + 牙 (tooth). The old explanation is a tooth piercing through: "to go
  through", then "to put on" (arms through sleeves). Take it as a memory aid.
- 漂 is 氵 + 票 (*piào*), and 样 is 木 + 羊 (*yáng*): sound parts again. 怎 has 心 (heart) at the
  bottom, as in 您.
- 非 is two rows of strokes facing away from each other, like wings back to back: "against, not".
- 对 is 又 (a hand) + 寸; its traditional form is 對.
- 服 is under 月 here; in old forms this "moon" was a boat, so the radical doesn't mean moon in 服.

### New radical

穴, "cave, hole" ({穴宝盖|xué bǎo gài}). A roof (宀) with 八 under it: the opening of a cave.
You have it in 穿. Later you'll see it in 空 (empty, free) and 突 (sudden), both in HSK 3.

### Stroke order

- 对: 又 first (two strokes: the horizontal that turns into a left-falling stroke, then the
  dot), then 寸: the horizontal, the vertical with a hook, and the dot last.
- 非: the left half first: its vertical, then its three short horizontals from top to bottom;
  then the right half the same way.
- 真: 十 on top, then 目 (five strokes), then the long horizontal, then the two short strokes at
  the bottom (left, then right).
- 衣: the dot, the horizontal, then the long left-falling stroke, the short vertical that
  rises, the short left-falling stroke on the right, and the long right-falling stroke last.

```trace
衣服穿新漂亮
```

```trace
非常真对怎样
```

Write it: 对 is one of the characters to know by hand. Write it three times from memory, then
check it on the pad.

=}

## Dialogue: in a clothes shop

{安娜|Ān nà} (安娜) and {王芳|Wáng Fāng} (王芳) are shopping; the third speaker is a shop assistant,
{店员|diàn yuán} (店员).

```dialogue
# In a clothes shop
安娜: {王芳|Wáng Fāng}，{你|nǐ}{看|kàn}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}，{漂亮|piào liang}{不|bu}{漂亮|piào liang}？
= Wang Fang, look at this top. Is it pretty?
王芳: {非常|fēi cháng}{漂亮|piào liang}！{你|nǐ}{穿|chuān}{一下|yí xià}{吧|ba}。
= Very pretty! Put it on and see.
安娜: {怎么样|zěn me yàng}？{好看|hǎo kàn}{吗|ma}？
= How is it? Does it look good?
王芳: {真|zhēn}{好看|hǎo kàn}！{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？
= It looks really good! How much is it?
安娜: {你好|nǐ hǎo}，{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？
= Excuse me, how much is this?
店员: {四百|sì bǎi}{块|kuài}。
= Four hundred kuai.
安娜: {四百|sì bǎi}{块|kuài}？{太|tài}{贵|guì}{了|le}！
= Four hundred? That's too expensive!
店员: {今天|jīn tiān}{半价|bàn jià}，{两百|liǎng bǎi}{块|kuài}。
= It's half price today: two hundred.
安娜: {两百|liǎng bǎi}{块|kuài}？{太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}！
= Two hundred? Great! I'll take it!
王芳: {对|duì}，{买|mǎi}{吧|ba}！{你|nǐ}{穿|chuān}{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}。
= Yes, buy it! You look really pretty in it.
```

{半价|bàn jià} (half price) is a word outside the course, made of {半|bàn} (half) and {价|jià}
(price). Notice how Anna opens with {你好|nǐ hǎo} to get the assistant's attention: it works like
"excuse me". The last line, literally "you wear this clothing really pretty", is how Chinese says
"you look pretty in it".

## Reading: half each

> {今天|jīn tiān}{是|shì}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}，{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{姐姐|jiě jie}{去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}{买|mǎi}{衣服|yī fu}。{姐姐|jiě jie}{穿|chuān}{一|yí}{件|jiàn}{新|xīn}{衣服|yī fu}，{说|shuō}：“{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？{漂亮|piào liang}{不|bu}{漂亮|piào liang}？”{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}：“{非常|fēi cháng}{漂亮|piào liang}！”{衣服|yī fu}{三百|sān bǎi}{块|kuài}。{姐姐|jiě jie}{说|shuō}：“{太|tài}{贵|guì}{了|le}，{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{买|mǎi}。”{我|wǒ}{说|shuō}：“{我们|wǒ men}{一|yì}{人|rén}{一半|yí bàn}{吧|ba}！”{姐姐|jiě jie}{说|shuō}：“{你|nǐ}{真|zhēn}{好|hǎo}！”

1. Where do the writer and the older sister go, and why?
2. What does the writer think of the clothes?
3. How much does each of them pay, if the sister accepts?

<details>
<summary>Answers and translation</summary>

1. To a shop, to buy clothes.
2. They're extremely pretty ({非常|fēi cháng}{漂亮|piào liang}).
3. 150 kuai each: half of 300 ({一|yì}{人|rén}{一半|yí bàn}).

"Today is Sunday, and my older sister and I go to the shops to buy clothes. My sister tries on a
new top and says, 'How is it? Is it pretty?' I say, 'It's gorgeous!' It's three hundred kuai. My
sister says, 'Too expensive, I won't buy it.' I say, 'Let's go half each!' My sister says,
'You're so sweet!'"
</details>

## Say it

```speak
{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
= What do you think of this?
{真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}！
= It's really pretty!
{贵|guì}{不|bu}{贵|guì}？
= Is it expensive?
{不|bú}{太|tài}{贵|guì}。
= Not too expensive.
{对|duì}，{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}！
= Right, I'll take it!
{我们|wǒ men}{一|yì}{人|rén}{一半|yí bàn}{吧|ba}。
= Let's go half each.
```

## Pronunciation

- {不|bu} in A-not-A questions is light and quick: *guì bu guì*, *hǎo bu hǎo*. Before a 4th tone
  elsewhere it's *bú* ({不|bú}{贵|guì}); in the middle of the question it's neutral.
- {漂亮|piào liang}: *piào* falls with a puff on the *p*; *liang* is light.
- {衣服|yī fu}: level *yī*, then a short *fu*.
- {穿|chuān}: *ch* curled back, then *uan*; level.
- {真|zhēn}: *zh* (no puff), *-en*; level. Don't confuse it with {怎|zěn} (dipping, *z* with the
  tongue flat).
- {非常|fēi cháng}: level, then rising.
- {一半|yí bàn}: {一|yī} rises before the 4th tone of {半|bàn}.

## Common mistakes

- {是|shì} + adjective: ~~{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{是|shì}{漂亮|piào liang}~~. Say
  {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}.
- {吗|ma} on an A-not-A question: ~~{贵|guì}{不|bu}{贵|guì}{吗|ma}？~~ Use one or the other:
  {贵|guì}{不|bu}{贵|guì}？ or {贵|guì}{吗|ma}？
- Degree adverb after the adjective: ~~{漂亮|piào liang}{非常|fēi cháng}~~. It goes before:
  {非常|fēi cháng}{漂亮|piào liang}.
- {真|zhēn} in a question: ~~{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{真|zhēn}{漂亮|piào liang}{吗|ma}？~~ Ask with {很|hěn}
  or A-not-A; keep {真|zhēn} for exclaiming.
- {半|bàn} for "half of it": ~~{我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{半|bàn}~~. Say {我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{一半|yí bàn}.
- Forgetting {件|jiàn}: ~~{这|zhè}{衣服|yī fu}~~ → {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}.

## Key points

- Adjective predicates: subject + degree adverb + adjective, no {是|shì}:
  {衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}. A bare adjective contrasts: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{贵|guì}，{那|nà}{件|jiàn}{便宜|pián yi}.
- Degree adverbs: {很|hěn} (plain), {非常|fēi cháng} (extremely), {真|zhēn}…！ (really!), {太|tài}…{了|le}
  (so / too), {不|bú}{太|tài} (not very).
- A-not-A: {贵|guì}{不|bu}{贵|guì}？, {喜|xǐ}{不|bu}{喜欢|xǐ huan}？; no {吗|ma}; {有|yǒu}{没有|méi yǒu}？
- {怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ How is it? How about it?
- {对|duì} right; {不|bú}{对|duì} wrong. {一半|yí bàn} half (of something).
- {穿|chuān} + clothes; {新|xīn}{衣服|yī fu}; {漂亮|piào liang} / {好看|hǎo kàn}.
- New radical: 穴 (cave).
