| also, all | {也|yě} / {都|dōu} + verb | {我们|wǒ men}{也|yě}{都|dōu}{去|qù}。 | 2 |
| and you? | … {呢|ne}？ | {你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？ | 2 |
| having | {有|yǒu} / {没有|méi yǒu} | {我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{妹妹|mèi mei}。 | 3 |
| possession | noun {的|de} noun | {老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{书|shū} | 3 |
| two | {两|liǎng} + measure word | {两个|liǎng gè}{孩子|hái zi} | 4 |
| age | (person) + number + {岁|suì} | {她|tā}{八岁|bā suì}。 | 4 |
| place of an action | {在|zài} + place + verb | {他|tā}{在|zài}{医院|yī yuàn}{工作|gōng zuò}。 | 5 |
| date | year, month, day | 2026{年|nián}11{月|yuè}16{号|hào} | 6 |
| clock time | {点|diǎn}, {分|fēn}, {半|bàn} | {八点半|bā diǎn bàn} | 7 |
| when before the verb | time + verb | {我|wǒ}{七点|qī diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。 | 8 |
| serial verbs | {去|qù} + place + verb | {去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi} | 9 |
| in progress | {在|zài} / {正在|zhèng zài} + verb + {呢|ne} | {他|tā}{在|zài}{睡觉|shuì jiào}{呢|ne}。 | 10 |
| liking | {喜欢|xǐ huan} + noun / verb | {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}。 | 11 |
| suggestion | … {吧|ba} | {我们|wǒ men}{吃饭|chī fàn}{吧|ba}。 | 12 |
| price | {多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？ number + {块|kuài} | {十五块|shí wǔ kuài} | 13 |
| this, that | {这|zhè} / {那|nà} + measure word + noun | {这本|zhè běn}{书|shū} | 14 |
| adjectives | ({很|hěn}) + adjective, no {是|shì} | {这件|zhè jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}。 | 15 |
| A-not-A | verb {不|bu} verb？ | {贵不贵|guì bu guì}？ | 15 |
| where it is | thing {在|zài} place + locative | {书|shū}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}。 | 16 |
| there is | place {有|yǒu} thing | {房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{一个|yí gè}{人|rén}。 | 17 |
| how you travel | {坐|zuò} + vehicle + {去|qù} | {坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}{去|qù} | 18 |
| can | {会|huì} / {能|néng} / {可以|kě yǐ} + verb | {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{写|xiě}{汉字|hàn zì}。 | 19 |
| change | sentence + {了|le} | {天|tiān}{冷|lěng}{了|le}。 | 20 |
| a bit (too) | {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr} + adjective | {我|wǒ}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{忙|máng}。 | 21 |
| double object | verb + person + thing | {给|gěi}{他|tā}{一本|yì běn}{书|shū} | 23 |
| also, in addition | …，{还|hái} + verb | {还有|hái yǒu}{一只|yì zhī}{狗|gǒu} | 24 |
| completed action | verb + {了|le}; {没|méi} + verb | {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{了|le}。 {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{买|mǎi}。 | 25 |
| when… | … {的时候|de shí hou} | {我|wǒ}{小|xiǎo}{的时候|de shí hou} | 25 |

## Common mistakes

- *{是|shì} before an adjective*: {她|tā}{是|shì}{很|hěn}{忙|máng} → {她|tā}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}。
- *Time and place at the end*: {我|wǒ}{工作|gōng zuò}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī} → {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。
- *A number without a measure word*: {三|sān}{书|shū} → {三本|sān běn}{书|shū}; {二个|èr gè} → {两个|liǎng gè}.
- *{不|bù} for the past or with {有|yǒu}*: {昨天|zuó tiān}{我|wǒ}{不去|bú qù} → {昨天|zuó tiān}{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}。
- *{了|le} as a past tense*: {去年|qù nián}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}{了|le} → {去年|qù nián}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。
- *{和|hé} between sentences*: use {也|yě} or {还|hái} before the second verb.

## Key points

- Predicates: verbs; adjectives with {很|hěn} (no {是|shì}); nouns for dates, times, ages and prices.
- Statements, questions, imperatives ({请|qǐng}…, {不要|bú yào}…) and exclamations ({太|tài}…{了|le}！ {真|zhēn}…！).
- Word order: (time) subject (time) adverb ({在|zài} place) verb object. How long goes after the verb.
- A number or {这|zhè} / {那|nà} needs a measure word; {两|liǎng} before measure words.
- {不|bù} for now, habits, the future and adjectives; {没|méi} for {有|yǒu} and for what didn't happen.
- {了|le}: change at the end of a sentence, completion after the verb; {在|zài} / {正在|zhèng zài} for now.
- Coordination: {和|hé} for nouns, {也|yě} and {还|hái} before the second verb.

This lesson has no new words.

lessons.title: The HSK 1 exam
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

This course covers the words and characters of the new HSK 1. This lesson explains what the exam
is and how it's built, gives you strategies for each part, and ends with a short practice set
written for this course, in the style of the exam's tasks. The questions at the end of the
lesson are more practice of the same kind.

You don't have to take the exam to use this course. But the exam is a good goal: a date in the
calendar makes regular study easier, and passing it shows what you can do.

## The HSK and the new levels

The **[[HSK]]** ({汉语|Hàn yǔ}{水平|shuǐ píng}{考试|kǎo shì}, "Chinese proficiency test") is the official
test of Chinese for people whose first language isn't Chinese. It's run by an organisation under
China's Ministry of Education, and it's taken at test centres around the world, on paper or on a
computer depending on the centre.

The HSK is changing. A new version, often called **[[HSK 3.0]]**, uses a new syllabus published in
November 2025 and in force from July 2026; its first official sitting was announced for 13
December 2026. It has nine levels in three bands. This course follows the new syllabus for level
1: 300 words and 246 characters, and the topics and tasks it lists for the level, such as
personal information, daily routine, food, shopping, transport and the weather, and reading
signs, menus, name cards and timetables.

Earlier courses and many websites describe the old HSK 1 (150 words) or the 2021 standard's
level 1 (500 words). Both differ from the new exam, so check which one a book or app means.

> Exam details change, and the organisers publish them on the official HSK website
> (chinesetest.cn), including sample papers. Before you register, check the format, the dates,
> the fee and the pass mark there. The figures in this lesson come from the syllabus and from
> reports on the first sample papers, and some had not been officially confirmed when this lesson
> was written.

## How the new HSK 1 is built

As far as was known when this lesson was written (from reports on the official sample paper and
on the organisers' outline of the exam), the new HSK 1 has:

| | |
|---|---|
| Parts | listening (20 questions) and reading (20 questions) |
| Questions | 40, all to choose or match (no writing) |
| Time | about 40 minutes in all, including time to fill in your details and to copy your listening answers onto the answer sheet |
| Speaking | none at level 1 |
| Writing | none at level 1 (writing starts at a later level) |

The old HSK 1 had the same shape: a listening part and a reading part with 20 questions each,
about 40 minutes in all, and the questions printed in pinyin as well as characters. One report on
the new sample paper says it prints pinyin with the Chinese too, but that hadn't been officially
confirmed; this course practises reading with pinyin turned off so that it doesn't matter.

### Listening

You hear each item twice on the old exam (check whether the new one does the same). Reports on the
new sample paper describe four kinds of task, five questions of each:

- *Words and pictures.* You hear a word or short phrase ({看书|kàn shū}, {打电话|dǎ diàn huà})
  and choose the photo that shows it.
- *What did you hear?* You hear a short sentence and choose the written words that match it.
- *Dialogues and pictures.* You hear a short dialogue and choose the photo that fits it.
- *A short text and a question.* You hear a few sentences and a question about them, and choose
  the answer: a time, a place, a person, a price.

What makes these hard is speed, not grammar. Lesson 28's listening strategies are exactly what
you need: the question word, numbers, {不|bù} / {没|méi}, time words.

### Reading

- *Sentences and pictures.* Match each sentence to a photo.
- *Questions and answers.* Match each question to its answer: {你|nǐ}{几点|jǐ diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}？
  goes with {七点|qī diǎn}, {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}？ with {去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}.
- *Fill the gap.* Choose the word that completes a sentence: a measure word, a question word, a
  verb.
- *Short texts.* Read a sign, a note, a menu or a few sentences and answer a question about them
  (lesson 27).

## Scoring

The old HSK 1 gave up to 100 points for listening and 100 for reading, and you passed with 120 of
200. For the new HSK, sample papers reported so far didn't include score scales or pass marks, so
don't assume the old figures still apply: check the official site. Results come as a score
report; the old reports were valid for applications for two years.

## Strategies

### Before the test

- *Know the formats.* Do the official sample paper once, untimed, to learn what each task looks
  like. Then do this lesson's practice set and the module quiz.
- *Review every word.* Your vocabulary reviews have all 300 words. Bring every word to at least
  Advanced in the last weeks; spend more time on the ones you keep missing.
- *Read with pinyin off.* Turn the pinyin switch off in the reviews and in lesson texts for the
  last month, so the characters carry the meaning.
- *Listen every day.* Play the dialogues of lessons 26–29 with the words hidden.

### During the test

1. *Read the choices before the audio starts.* If the choices are times, you know to listen for
   {点|diǎn}; if they're people, for {谁|shéi} and names.
2. *Answer every question.* There's no penalty for a wrong answer on the old exam; never leave a
   blank. Cross out the choices you know are wrong, then choose.
3. *Don't stop on one question.* If you miss an item in listening, let it go and get ready for
   the next: the audio doesn't wait.
4. *Match by meaning, not by one word.* A picture of a cup doesn't always go with the sentence
   that says {杯子|bēi zi}: {我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{杯子|bēi zi} says the opposite. Read to the end.
5. *Check the numbers.* {四|sì} and {十|shí}, {两|liǎng} and {八|bā}: write the number you hear in
   the margin.
6. *Manage the time.* In reading, do the items you find easy first and come back to the others.


## A short practice set

Try these, then check your answers below. They're written for this course in the style of the
exam's tasks, not copied from any paper.

### A. Listening

Play each phrase without looking at the words, and choose its meaning.

```speak
{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{看书|kàn shū}。
= 1. a) I'm reading. b) I'm watching TV. c) I'm sleeping.
{现在|xiàn zài}{十点|shí diǎn}。
= 2. a) It's four now. b) It's ten now. c) It's seven now.
{他|tā}{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}{去|qù}{上海|Shàng hǎi}。
= 3. a) by train b) by taxi c) by plane
```

### B. Questions and answers

Match each question to an answer.

| Question | Answers |
|---|---|
| 4. {你|nǐ}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}{名字|míng zi}？ | a) {三口人|sān kǒu rén}。 |
| 5. {你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{几口人|jǐ kǒu rén}？ | b) {十五块|shí wǔ kuài}。 |
| 6. {这个|zhè ge}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？ | c) {我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{李明|Lǐ Míng}。 |
| 7. {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}？ | d) {去|qù}{医院|yī yuàn}。 |

### C. Fill the gap

Choose {本|běn}, {吗|ma}, {没|méi} or {在|zài}.

8. {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}___？
9. {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{两|liǎng}___ {书|shū}。
10. {他|tā}{昨天|zuó tiān}___ {来|lái}。
11. {妈妈|mā ma}___ {医院|yī yuàn}{工作|gōng zuò}。

### D. A short text

Read and answer.

> {今天|jīn tiān}{星期六|xīng qī liù}，{天气|tiān qì}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{姐姐|jiě jie}{上午|shàng wǔ}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{买|mǎi}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}，{下午|xià wǔ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}。

12. When do they go to the supermarket? 13. What do they do in the afternoon?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1 a. 2 b ({十|shí} rises; {四|sì} 4 would fall). 3 c. 4 c. 5 a. 6 b. 7 d. 8 {吗|ma}. 9 {本|běn}.
10 {没|méi}. 11 {在|zài}. 12 On Saturday morning ({上午|shàng wǔ}). 13 They watch TV at home.

Translation of D: Today is Saturday, and the weather is lovely. My older sister and I go to the
supermarket in the morning to buy fruit, and in the afternoon we watch TV at home. (Without {了|le}
the text doesn't say whether this has happened yet: it could be a plan or a diary.)

</details>

## A study plan for the last month

| Week | Do |
|---|---|
| 1 | One official sample paper, untimed. List the task types you found hard. Review words every day. |
| 2 | Lessons 26–27 again (questions, signs). Module quizzes of modules 1–3. |
| 3 | Lessons 28–29 again (listening, grammar). Module quizzes of modules 4–6. Pinyin off. |
| 4 | A second sample paper, timed. Review only the words and points you missed. Sleep well the night before. |

## Dialogue: after the exam

```dialogue
# After the exam
安娜: {你|nǐ}{觉得|jué de}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
= What did you think?
大卫: {听力|tīng lì}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{难|nán}，{阅读|yuè dú}{不|bù}{难|nán}。
= The listening questions were a bit hard; the reading ones weren't.
安娜: {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{觉得|jué de}。{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听见|tīng jiàn}{第二个|dì èr gè}{问题|wèn tí}。
= I think so too. I didn't catch the second question.
大卫: {没关系|méi guān xi}。{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{吃饭|chī fàn}{吧|ba}！
= Never mind. Let's go and eat!
安娜: {好|hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{饺子|jiǎo zi}。
= OK! I'd like dumplings.
```

{难|nán} (difficult) is an HSK 2 word. {听力|tīng lì} (listening) and {阅读|yuè dú} (reading) are the names of
the exam parts; they are words for later levels.

## Can you do this?

When you can do all of these, you're ready for HSK 1:

- introduce yourself: name, country, age, job, family, likes (lesson 28);
- ask and answer the questions of lesson 26, with the right particle or question word;
- say and understand numbers to 9,999, prices, phone numbers, times and dates;
- read a sign, a menu, a name card, a price label, a timetable and a note (lesson 27);
- use measure words, {不|bù} and {没|méi}, the two {了|le} and {在|zài} / {正在|zhèng zài} (lesson 29);
- recognise all 246 characters (the character list in the Study tools box) and write the
  handwriting characters marked ✎.

## Common mistakes

- *Studying the wrong list.* The new HSK 1 has 300 words; older lists have 150 or 500.
- *Learning only with pinyin.* The characters carry the meaning; practise with pinyin off.
- *Leaving answers blank.* Choose something every time.
- *Reading the picture, not the sentence.* {不|bù}, {没|méi} and the last words of a sentence can
  reverse what the picture suggests.

## Key points

- The new HSK 1 (HSK 3.0) tests listening and reading: about 40 questions in about 40 minutes, no
  writing or speaking. It covers 300 words and 246 characters.
- Check the official site for the current format, dates, fee and pass mark.
- Listening: read the choices first, listen for the key word, never leave a blank.
- Reading: match by meaning, read to the end, scan for numbers and characters you know.
- Practise with pinyin off and with real timing in the last weeks.

This lesson has no new words. Congratulations on reaching the end of HSK 1!

lessons.title: A longer story
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

Everything you've read so far has been short: a sentence, a note, a menu. This lesson is a story
of about 300 characters, written for this course, in four parts. Almost every word is from HSK 1;
three new words are glossed below. Reading a longer text is a different skill: you keep the story
in your head, follow who is doing what, and let a few unknown words go by.

Read each part once without stopping, even if you miss something. Then read it again more slowly,
and open the translation only to check. When you've finished, read the whole story once more with
pinyin turned off.

## Before you read

The story is about {婷婷|Tíng tíng} (Tingting), a student, her cat {小白|Xiǎo Bái}
("Little White") and her friend {李明|Lǐ Míng}. Three words you haven't learned:

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| {喵|miāo} | miaow (the sound a cat makes) |
| {哭|kū} | to cry |
| {黑|hēi} | black (an HSK 2 word) |

Pet names with {小|xiǎo} + a colour or a feature are very common: {小白|Xiǎo Bái}, {小黑|Xiǎo Hēi}.

## The story: {小白|Xiǎo Bái}

### Part 1

> {婷婷|Tíng tíng}{有|yǒu}{一只|yì zhī}{猫|māo}，{它|tā}{叫|jiào}{小白|Xiǎo Bái}。{小白|Xiǎo Bái}{两岁|liǎng suì}{了|le}，{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}，{也|yě}{很|hěn}{好玩儿|hǎo wánr}，{婷婷|Tíng tíng}{很|hěn}{爱|ài}{它|tā}。{白天|bái tiān}{婷婷|Tíng tíng}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}{上课|shàng kè}，{小白|Xiǎo Bái}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{里|lǐ}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。{每天|měi tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{婷婷|Tíng tíng}{回家|huí jiā}{的时候|de shí hou}，{小白|Xiǎo Bái}{都|dōu}{叫|jiào}：“{喵|miāo}！{喵|miāo}！”

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

Tingting has a cat called Little White. Little White is two years old, very pretty and great fun, and Tingting loves it. In
the daytime Tingting goes to classes at school, and Little White sleeps at home. Every evening, when
Tingting comes home, Little White calls: "Miaow! Miaow!"

</details>

{每天|měi tiān} is "every day" (an HSK 2 word), and {都|dōu} goes with it: "every time", on all the evenings. {叫|jiào} is "to call" in the sense of an
animal's cry as well as "to be called".

### Part 2

> {星期五|xīng qī wǔ}{晚上|wǎn shang}，{天气|tiān qì}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}。{婷婷|Tíng tíng}{回家|huí jiā}{了|le}，{她|tā}{没|méi}{听见|tīng jiàn}“{喵|miāo}”。“{小白|Xiǎo Bái}，{你|nǐ}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？”{小白|Xiǎo Bái}{不在|bú zài}{椅子|yǐ zi}{上|shàng}，{也|yě}{不在|bú zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{下|xià}。{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{的|de}{床|chuáng}{下|xià}{也|yě}{没有|méi yǒu}。{婷婷|Tíng tíng}{找|zhǎo}{了|le}{一个|yí gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}，{没|méi}{看见|kàn jiàn}{小白|Xiǎo Bái}。

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

On Friday evening it was cold and it started to rain. Tingting came home, but she didn't hear a
"miaow". "Little White, where are you?" Little White wasn't on the chair, and wasn't under the
table. It wasn't under the bed in her room either. Tingting looked for an hour, but didn't see Little White.

</details>

Chinese often joins two facts with just a comma where English says "but". Notice the two kinds of
{了|le}: {下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le} (it started to rain: a change) and {找|zhǎo}{了|le}{一个|yí gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}
(she looked for an hour: a completed action with its duration after the verb).

### Part 3

> {婷婷|Tíng tíng}{给|gěi}{李明|Lǐ Míng}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}：“{喂|wèi}，{李明|Lǐ Míng}，{小白|Xiǎo Bái}{不在|bú zài}{家|jiā}{了|le}！”{李明|Lǐ Míng}{说|shuō}：“{你|nǐ}{不要|bú yào}{哭|kū}，{我|wǒ}{现在|xiàn zài}{去|qù}{你|nǐ}{家|jiā}。”{二十分钟|èr shí fēn zhōng}{后|hòu}，{李明|Lǐ Míng}{来|lái}{了|le}，{他们|tā men}{去|qù}{外边|wài bian}{找|zhǎo}。{雨|yǔ}{很|hěn}{大|dà}。{他们|tā men}{问|wèn}{了|le}{超市|chāo shì}{和|hé}{饭店|fàn diàn}{的|de}{人|rén}：“{你们|nǐ men}{看见|kàn jiàn}{一只|yì zhī}{白|bái}{猫|māo}{了|le}{吗|ma}？”{大家|dà jiā}{都|dōu}{说|shuō}：“{没|méi}{看见|kàn jiàn}。”

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

Tingting phoned Li Ming. "Hello, Li Ming, Little White's gone (isn't at home any more)!" Li Ming said,
"Don't cry. I'm coming over now." Twenty minutes later Li Ming arrived, and they went outside to look. It
was raining hard. They asked the people at the supermarket and the restaurant: "Have you seen a white cat?" Everyone said, "No, I haven't."

</details>

{雨|yǔ}{很|hěn}{大|dà} ("the rain is big") is how Chinese says "it's raining hard". The answer
{没|méi}{看见|kàn jiàn} has no {了|le}, like every {没|méi} answer.

### Part 4

> {十点|shí diǎn}{了|le}，{他们|tā men}{回|huí}{婷婷|Tíng tíng}{家|jiā}。{在|zài}{外边|wài bian}，{李明|Lǐ Míng}{听见|tīng jiàn}：“{喵|miāo}——”“{你|nǐ}{听|tīng}！”{他|tā}{说|shuō}。{他们|tā men}{看见|kàn jiàn}{车|chē}{下|xià}{有|yǒu}{两只|liǎng zhī}{猫|māo}：{小白|Xiǎo Bái}{和|hé}{一只|yì zhī}{小|xiǎo}{黑|hēi}{猫|māo}。{婷婷|Tíng tíng}{非常|fēi cháng}{高兴|gāo xìng}：“{小白|Xiǎo Bái}，{你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{朋友|péng you}{了|le}！”{现在|xiàn zài}，{婷婷|Tíng tíng}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{两只|liǎng zhī}{猫|māo}{了|le}：{小白|Xiǎo Bái}{和|hé}{小黑|Xiǎo Hēi}。{李明|Lǐ Míng}{说|shuō}：“{小黑|Xiǎo Hēi}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{漂亮|piào liang}！{明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{再|zài}{来|lái}{看|kàn}{它们|tā men}。”

<details>
<summary>Translation</summary>

It was ten o'clock, and they went back to Tingting's home. Outside, Li Ming heard "Miaow…". "Listen!"
he said. They saw two cats under a car: Little White and a little black cat. Tingting was
delighted. "Little White, you've got a friend!" Now Tingting has two cats: Little White and Little
Black. Li Ming said, "Little Black is pretty too! I'll come and see them again tomorrow."

</details>

{车|chē}{下|xià} is "under a car", with the position word {下|xià}. {十点|shí diǎn}{了|le} ("it's
ten now") and {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{朋友|péng you}{了|le} ("you've got a friend now") are both the
change-of-state {了|le}; so is the last one: there are two cats *now*.

## Reading it again

Now read the four parts again with pinyin off, and see if you can answer these without looking:

1. How old is Little White?
2. Why did Tingting call Li Ming?
3. Where did they find Little White?
4. What changed at the end of the story?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Two ({两岁|liǎng suì}{了|le}). 2. Because Little White wasn't at home. 3. Under a car outside
Tingting's home. 4. Tingting has two cats now: Little White has a friend, Little Black.

</details>

Then try retelling the story aloud in short sentences: {婷婷|Tíng tíng}{有|yǒu}{一只|yì zhī}{猫|māo}……
{星期五|xīng qī wǔ}{晚上|wǎn shang}……

## Key points

- Read a longer text once for the story, then again for the details; check the translation last.
- Follow the people: {她|tā}, {他|tā}, {他们|tā men} and {它|tā} point back to the names.
- Time words ({星期五|xīng qī wǔ}{晚上|wǎn shang}, {十点|shí diǎn}{了|le}) mark the steps of a story.
- Both kinds of {了|le} carry a story forward: what happened, and what changed.

lessons.title: Writing by hand
lessons.body:
## What this lesson is for

HSK 1 doesn't ask you to write, but HSK 2 does: short answers in characters, from a list of 100
characters that the syllabus expects you to write by hand at levels 1 and 2. You've learned 95 of
them in this course (marked ✎ in the character sections and the character list); HSK 2 adds the
last five. This lesson is about writing them well: in the square, in proportion, with the strokes
in order, and recognising the same character in the different shapes it takes in print.

You need paper with squares (or the tracing pads in this lesson) and a pen or pencil.

This lesson describes the simplified forms this course teaches, so with the script switch on
Traditional its text stays in simplified characters; the tracing pads follow your script.

{=

## The square

Every Chinese character takes the same amount of space, a square, however many strokes it has:
{一|yī} (one stroke) and {谢|xiè} (12 strokes) are the same size. Children in China learn on
practice paper with a grid in each square:

- **[[tianzige]]** ({田字格|tián zì gé}, "the 田 grid"): a square divided into four by a dashed cross, like
  the character {田|tián} (field);
- {米字格|mǐ zì gé} ("the 米 grid"): the same with the two diagonals added, like {米|mǐ} (rice).

The dashed lines aren't part of the character: they help you place it. Centre the character on
the cross, and fill most of the square, leaving a little space on every side. A character with few
strokes ({人|rén}, {大|dà}, {口|kǒu}) is drawn a little smaller than the square, never stretched to the
edges.

The tracing pads in this course use the same square with a dashed cross.

On squared writing paper for compositions, every character and every punctuation mark (。，？！)
takes one square, and a new paragraph starts two squares in.

## Proportions

Most characters are built from two or three parts. The parts share the square, and they're not
equal:

| Layout | Examples | How to share the square |
|---|---|---|
| left–right | {你|nǐ}, {好|hǎo}, {妈|mā}, {说|shuō}, {们|men}, {时|shí} | the radical on the left is usually narrow (about a third); the right part is wider |
| top–bottom | {字|zì}, {是|shì}, {早|zǎo}, {茶|chá}, {学|xué}, {爸|bà} | the top part is flatter and often wider; the bottom part carries the weight |
| enclosure | {国|guó}, {四|sì}, {回|huí} | the frame fills the square; the inside is small and centred |
| half enclosure | {这|zhè}, {边|biān}, {还|hái}; {医|yī} | 辶 runs along the bottom under the part it carries; 匚 in {医|yī} opens to the right |

In a left–right character, the left part often changes shape to make room: {女|nǚ} on its own is
wide, but in {好|hǎo} and {妈|mā} it's narrow and its last stroke rises to the right. {子|zǐ} in {好|hǎo}
keeps its normal shape, but in {孩|hái} it becomes a narrow radical with a rising last stroke. The
same thing happens to 土 in {块|kuài} and 王 in {现|xiàn}: on the left, their last stroke rises.

## Stroke order: the rules you use most

The pinyin course taught the rules; here they are with the characters where people slip:

1. *Top before bottom, left before right*: {三|sān}, {你|nǐ}.
2. *Horizontal before vertical when they cross*: {十|shí}, then {午|wǔ}: after the short falling
   stroke at the top, the two horizontals, then the long vertical last.
3. *Outside first, close the door last*: {国|guó} and {四|sì}: left vertical, then the top and right
   in one stroke, then the inside, then the bottom stroke that closes the box.
4. *辶 last*: in {这|zhè}, {边|biān}, {还|hái} you write the part on top first and the walking
   radical under it at the end.
5. *The dot at the end*: in {我|wǒ} (7 strokes) the dot at the top right is the very last stroke.
6. *Count the strokes*: {女|nǚ} has 3 (a stroke that falls to the left and then turns to the
   right, a long stroke falling to the left, then the horizontal), {九|jiǔ} 2 (the falling stroke first, then
   one turning stroke for the rest), {口|kǒu} 3.

## Common mistakes

- *Wrong stroke direction.* Horizontals go left to right, verticals top to bottom, and falling strokes
  always go downwards: from the top right down to the left, or from the top left down to the right. A reversed stroke may look right on paper, but the
  tracing pads will catch it, and it makes fast handwriting harder to read.
- *Joining strokes.* {口|kǒu} is three strokes: the left side; the top and right side in one stroke;
  the bottom. Drawing it as one loop makes it hard to tell from {日|rì} or a circle.
- *{口|kǒu} or {日|rì}?* {日|rì} is taller than wide and has a stroke across the middle; {口|kǒu} is
  square and empty. As radicals they're both narrow: compare {吃|chī} and {时|shí}.
- *{土|tǔ} or {士|shì}?* In {土|tǔ} (earth) the bottom horizontal is longer; in {士|shì} (in
  {女士|nǚ shì}) the top one is.
- *{午|wǔ} or {牛|niú}?* In {牛|niú} the vertical goes through the top; in {午|wǔ} it doesn't.
- *{人|rén}, {入|rù} or {八|bā}?* {人|rén}: the long stroke on the left; {入|rù}: the long stroke on
  the right; {八|bā}: two strokes that don't touch.
- *{买|mǎi} or {卖|mài}?* {卖|mài} (sell) has {十|shí} on top: you give something "more" away. (A
  memory aid, not the history of the character.)
- *{几|jǐ} or {九|jiǔ}?* {九|jiǔ} has a stroke that crosses; {几|jǐ} doesn't.

In traditional characters some of these look different: {买|mǎi} and {卖|mài} are 買 and 賣 (told
apart by 士 on top of 賣), {几|jǐ} is 幾, and {谢|xiè} has 17 strokes (謝).

=}

## Print and handwriting

The same character looks a little different in different typefaces, and handwriting is different
again. The three styles you'll meet most:

| Style | Looks like | Where you see it |
|---|---|---|
| Song ({宋体|sòng tǐ}) | thin horizontals, thick verticals, small "serifs" at the ends of strokes | most printed books and newspapers |
| Hei ({黑体|hēi tǐ}) | strokes of even thickness, no decoration, like a sans-serif font | screens, signs, headings |
| Kai ({楷体|kǎi tǐ}) | shaped like brush writing in the regular style; closest to handwriting | textbooks and children's books |

Kai is the best model for your own writing, because it shows how each stroke starts and ends.
Some details change between styles, so don't be surprised when a dot looks like a short line, or
a hook is missing in Hei. The structure of the character doesn't change.

{=

### The shapes of 心 and 言

Two components change shape depending on where they are, and these are not font differences:
they're part of the character.

- 心 (heart, {心|xīn}) keeps its shape at the bottom of a character: {想|xiǎng}, {您|nín},
  {怎|zěn}, {息|xī}. On the left it becomes 忄 (three strokes: two dots and a vertical):
  {忙|máng}.
- 言 (speech, {言|yán}) on the left is written 讠 in simplified characters: a dot and one
  turning stroke, two strokes in all: {说|shuō}, {话|huà}, {语|yǔ}, {请|qǐng}, {谁|shéi}, {谢|xiè}. If you
  switch the course to traditional characters you'll see the full {言|yán} (7 strokes) in its place:
  說, 話, 語, 請, 誰, 謝.

=}

## Practice page: the 95 handwriting characters

Trace each character, then write it three times from memory on squared paper. Printing the lesson
gives you the tracing pads as a worksheet. The character list in the Study tools box has the
pinyin, meaning and stroke count of each.


strokes against the pad.

## Key points

{=

- Each character fills one square, centred on the cross of the grid ({田字格|tián zì gé}).
- Parts share the square unequally: narrow radicals on the left, flatter parts on top.
- Stroke order: top to bottom, left to right, horizontal before vertical, outside then inside then
  close, 辶 last.
- Watch the look-alikes: {口|kǒu} / {日|rì}, {土|tǔ} / {士|shì}, {午|wǔ} / {牛|niú}, {人|rén} / {入|rù} / {八|bā},
  {买|mǎi} / {卖|mài}, {几|jǐ} / {九|jiǔ}.
- Song, Hei and Kai print the same characters in different styles; Kai is the model for writing.
  忄 and 讠 are the side forms of 心 and 言.

=}

sections.name: Health, free time and the past

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm not a teacher."?
questions.explanation: {不|bù} goes right before the verb it negates: {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}. Before the fourth tone of {是|shì} it's said bú. Putting {不|bù} after {是|shì} or at the start copies no Chinese pattern, and the verb can't move to the end.

questions.stem: Turn "{你|nǐ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。" (You're a student.) into a yes-or-no question.
questions.explanation: {吗|ma} goes at the very end, and nothing else moves: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}{吗|ma}？ It can't go at the start or after the subject, and a question that already has {什么|shén me} never takes {吗|ma}.

questions.stem: How do you ask "What's your name?"
questions.explanation: The question word stays where the answer will go: {你|nǐ}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}{名字|míng zi}？ — {我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{安娜|Ān nà}。 Moving {什么|shén me} to the front copies English. Adding {吗|ma} to a question with {什么|shén me} is a mistake, and {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{名字|míng zi}{吗|ma} means "Are you a name?"

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct for "I'm fine."?
questions.explanation: {好|hǎo} is an adjective, and Chinese adjectives work without {是|shì}. In a plain statement they take an unstressed {很|hěn}: {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。 Every choice with {是|shì} copies English "am".

questions.stem: You meet a friend's grandmother for the first time. Which greeting is the most respectful?
questions.explanation: {您|nín} is the polite "you", for older people, teachers and strangers, so {您好|nín hǎo} is the respectful greeting. {你好|nǐ hǎo} is fine with people your age. {你|nǐ}{好|hǎo}{吗|ma}？ asks whether someone is well, which you'd ask someone you already know, and {再见|zài jiàn} is "goodbye".

questions.stem: Which is the pinyin of 什么 (what)?
questions.explanation: {什么|shén me}: a second (rising) tone, then a neutral tone, which has no mark. The second syllable is light and short, never a full tone.

questions.stem: Two third tones meet in 你好, written nǐ hǎo. How is the first syllable said?
choices: nǐ, a full low third tone
ní, rising like a second tone
nì, falling like a fourth tone
questions.explanation: When two third tones meet, the first is said as a second tone: {你好|nǐ hǎo} sounds like ní hǎo. Pinyin still writes the third tone. The same happens in {很好|hěn hǎo}, said hén hǎo.

questions.stem: Which character means "she"?
questions.explanation: 她 has the radical 女 "woman" on the left. 他 (he) has 亻 "person"; both are read tā. 你 is "you" and 您 the polite "you", with 心 "heart" underneath.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word 名__ (míng zi, name)?
questions.explanation: 名字 is written with 字 (character, word): a roof 宀 over 子. 子 alone is "child", also read zi, so it's the tempting one. 学 is the first character of {学生|xué sheng}, and 宇 is another character with a roof.

questions.stem: Which radical do 你, 他 and 什 share?
questions.explanation: All three have 亻 on the left, the form 人 (person) takes at the side of a character. 女 is in 她 and 好, 口 in 叫, 吗 and 名, and 心 at the bottom of 您.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking?
questions.explanation: You heard {你|nǐ}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}{名字|míng zi}？ "What's your name?" The question word {什么|shén me} (what) asked for a name; "Are you a student?" would end in {吗|ma}, and "How are you?" is {你|nǐ}{好|hǎo}{吗|ma}？

questions.stem: Listen. Which sentence did you hear?
questions.explanation: {她|tā}{不|bú}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}: "She isn't a teacher." Listen for bú before shì: without it the sentence is positive. The last word was lǎo shī (teacher), not xué sheng (student), and there was no ma at the end.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.
questions.explanation: The question was {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}{吗|ma}？ "Are you a student?" A yes-or-no question is answered with its verb: {是|shì}, {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。 The others answer "What's your name?", "How are you?" and "Thank you".

questions.stem: Listen. Who is the speaker greeting?
choices: a teacher whose family name is Wang
questions.explanation: {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}，{您好|nín hǎo}！ greets Teacher Wang: the family name, then the title {老师|lǎo shī}, and the polite {您|nín}. A classmate or a child would get {你|nǐ}, and a group {你们|nǐ men}.

questions.stem: Read: "{你好|nǐ hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{李明|Lǐ Míng}。{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}，{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。" What is true?
choices: Li Ming's family name is Wang.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}，{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}: "I'm not a teacher, I'm a student." Watch {不|bú}: it reverses the first half. The family name is {李|Lǐ}, written first, and nothing is said about how Li Ming is.

questions.stem: Read: A: "{她|tā}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}{名字|míng zi}？" B: "{她|tā}{叫|jiào}{刘华|Liú Huá}，{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。" A: "{她|tā}{好|hǎo}{吗|ma}？" B: "{她|tā}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。" What is true?
choices: Liu Hua is a teacher, and she is well.
questions.explanation: B says {她|tā}{叫|jiào}{刘华|Liú Huá}，{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī} (she's called Liu Hua and is a teacher) and {她|tā}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} (she's fine). The pronoun {她|tā} shows they are talking about a woman, not about B.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I'm not a teacher.
questions.explanation: Subject, then {不|bú} right before the verb {是|shì}, then the noun: {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。 {很|hěn} goes before adjectives, not nouns.

questions.stem: Build the question in Chinese.
questions.prompt: What's her name?
questions.explanation: {她|tā}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}{名字|míng zi}？ keeps the order of the answer ({她|tā}{叫|jiào}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}). A question with {什么|shén me} takes no {吗|ma}.

questions.stem: Type the word for "teacher" (pinyin with tone numbers, for example ni3 hao3, or characters): ___
questions.explanation: Teacher is {老师|lǎo shī}: a third tone, then a first tone (type lao3 shi1). After a family name it's a title: {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {他|tā} he, {她|tā} she, {您|nín} the polite you, {老师|lǎo shī} teacher, {名字|míng zi} name. A student would be {学生|xué sheng}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {您|nín}, the polite "you": a rising second tone, ending in -n.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {老师|lǎo shī}: a low third tone, then a high first tone (3+1).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm a student too."?
questions.explanation: {也|yě} is an adverb, so it goes after the subject and before the verb: {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。 Putting it at the end copies English "too"; it can't start the sentence or come between the verb and its object.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "We're all students too."?
questions.explanation: With both adverbs the order is fixed: {也|yě} first, then {都|dōu}, both after the subject and before the verb. {都|dōu}{也|yě} is a common mistake, and neither adverb can go at the start or the end.

questions.stem: How do you ask someone where they're from?
questions.explanation: {哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}, "a person of which country", stands where the answer goes: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{美国人|Měi guó rén}。 {那|nà} (fourth tone) means "that", not "which". A question with a question word takes no {吗|ma}, and {是|shì} comes before the whole phrase.

questions.stem: You want to say you're British and ask the other person the same question back. Which is best?
questions.explanation: {呢|ne} after a pronoun turns the same question back: {你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？ "And you?" {吗|ma} can't stand after a bare pronoun; {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{英国人|Yīng guó rén}{吗|ma}？ asks "Am I British?", and {呢|ne} doesn't go in the middle of a sentence.

questions.stem: Which word means "they" for a group of two men and one woman?
questions.explanation: {他们|tā men} covers men and any mixed group; {她们|tā men} is only for a group of women. Both are said tā men. {我们|wǒ men} is "we" and {你们|nǐ men} "you" (plural).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "He can't speak Chinese."?
questions.explanation: The negative goes before {会|huì}: {不|bú}{会|huì}{说|shuō}, "can't speak" (bú before the fourth tone of huì). {会|huì}{不|bù}{说|shuō} would mean "can not-speak", and {不|bú}{是|shì} is the negative of {是|shì}, which has no place here.

questions.stem: Which tone does 哪 (which) have?
questions.explanation: {哪|nǎ}, "which", has the third tone. With the fourth tone, nà, it's {那|nà}, "that", so the tone decides between a question and an answer.

questions.stem: Which is the pinyin of 汉语 (Chinese)?
questions.explanation: {汉语|Hàn yǔ}: a fourth tone, then a third. yu is the ü sound; after y the dots aren't written. The name is capitalised in pinyin because it's a proper noun.

questions.stem: Which radical do 语 and 说 share?
questions.explanation: {=讠=} is the simplified side form of 言, "speech" ({+讠+} in traditional characters): it marks words about speaking and language, such as {语|yǔ} (language) and {说|shuō} (to speak). 氵 is in 汉, 亻 in 们, and 口 in 哪 and 呢.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word 汉__ (Hàn yǔ, Chinese)?
questions.explanation: 汉语 is written with 语 (language): 讠 + 吾. 吾 alone is only its right-hand part, and 说 (to speak) and 话 (speech, lesson 10) have the same radical but other meanings.

questions.stem: Which character means "country"?
questions.explanation: {=国=} (guó) is 玉 (jade) inside an enclosure; the traditional form {+国+} has 或 inside. 回 (to return) has a small box inside a big one, 四 is four, and 图 (picture, map) has a different inside.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the sentence mean?
questions.explanation: You heard {我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{中国人|Zhōng guó rén}: {都|dōu} is "all". "Too" would be {也|yě}, "Americans" {美国人|Měi guó rén}, and there was no {吗|ma} to make a question.

questions.stem: Listen. Which sentence did you hear?
questions.explanation: {她|tā}{也|yě}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{英语|Yīng yǔ}: "She can speak English too." Listen for yě after tā, and for Yīng yǔ (English) at the end rather than Hàn yǔ (Chinese).

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.
choices: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{加拿大人|Jiā ná dà rén}。
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}？ asks where you're from, so the answer puts a nationality where {哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén} was: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{加拿大人|Jiā ná dà rén} (I'm Canadian). The others give a name, a language and a job.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker want to know?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{英国人|Yīng guó rén}，{你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？ "I'm British. And you?" {呢|ne} repeats the question that the first sentence answered, here "where are you from?"

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{大卫|Dà wèi}，{是|shì}{英国人|Yīng guó rén}。{我|wǒ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{英语|Yīng yǔ}，{也|yě}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。" Which languages does David speak?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{英语|Yīng yǔ}，{也|yě}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}: "I speak English, and Chinese too." {也|yě} adds the second language; French ({法语|Fǎ yǔ}) isn't mentioned.

questions.stem: Read: A: "{你们|nǐ men}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}{吗|ma}？" B: "{不|bú}{是|shì}。{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}，{她|tā}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。" What is true about B and the woman with B?
choices: Neither of them is a teacher.
One is a teacher and one is a student.
questions.explanation: A asks whether they are both teachers ({都|dōu} = both). B says no: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}， {她|tā}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}, "I'm a teacher, she's a student."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: They can all speak Chinese.
questions.explanation: Subject, then the adverb {都|dōu}, then {会|huì} + verb + language: {他们|tā men}{都|dōu}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。 {也|yě} would add "too", which isn't in the English.

questions.stem: Build the question in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Where are you from? (Which country are you from?)
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}？ follows the answer's order ({我|wǒ}{是|shì}{中国人|Zhōng guó rén}), with {哪|nǎ} in front of {国|guó}. A question word needs no {吗|ma}.

questions.stem: Type the word for "we, us" (pinyin with tone numbers or characters): ___
questions.explanation: {我们|wǒ men} is {我|wǒ} + the plural suffix {们|men}, in the neutral tone (type wo3 men or wo3 men5).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {中文|Zhōng wén}: a high first tone, then a rising second (1+2).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {我们|wǒ men}: a third tone, then the light neutral tone of {们|men} (3+neutral).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I don't have an older sister."?
questions.explanation: {有|yǒu} is the one verb that {不|bù} can't negate: its negative is {没有|méi yǒu}. 不有 is the classic mistake, {没|méi} can't come after {有|yǒu}, and {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{是|shì}{姐姐|jiě jie} means "I'm not an older sister".

questions.stem: Which is correct for "three older sisters"?
questions.explanation: Number + measure word + noun: {三|sān}{个|gè}{姐姐|jiě jie}. A number can't stand right before a noun as in English, {的|de} doesn't count anything, and the measure word comes after the number, not before it.

questions.stem: How do you ask "How many older brothers do you have?"
questions.explanation: {几|jǐ} + measure word stands where the number in the answer goes: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{哥哥|gē ge}。 Without {个|gè} it's wrong, a question word takes no {吗|ma}, and the number phrase comes before the noun.

questions.stem: How do you say "the teacher's name"?
questions.explanation: Owner + {的|de} + thing: {老师|lǎo shī}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}. {名字|míng zi}{的|de}{老师|lǎo shī} would be "the name's teacher", and {的|de} never comes first or last in the phrase.

questions.stem: Which is the most natural way to say "my mum"?
questions.explanation: With family members {的|de} is usually dropped: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}. ({我|wǒ}{的|de}{妈妈|mā ma} is possible but sounds emphatic.) The owner still comes first; {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{妈妈|mā ma} is "I'm a mum".

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct for "I'm a student and my brother is a teacher."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}{和|hé}{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}，{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}，{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。
{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}，{和|hé}{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{老师|lǎo shī}。
questions.explanation: {和|hé} joins nouns, not sentences. Two sentences are simply put side by side with a comma: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}，{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。 Each other choice uses {和|hé} as English uses "and".

questions.stem: You point at a photo across the room: "That's my older sister." Which sentence fits?
questions.explanation: {那|nà} (fourth tone) is "that", for something further away; {这|zhè} is "this", close by. {哪|nǎ} (third tone) asks "which", and the last choice scrambles the order.

questions.stem: Which tone does 那 (that) have?
questions.explanation: {那|nà}, "that", has a short falling fourth tone. Said with the third tone, nǎ, it becomes {哪|nǎ}, "which".

questions.stem: How is 一个 (one, with the measure word) written in this course's pinyin?
questions.explanation: {一|yī} changes to yí before a fourth tone, and {个|gè} is fourth: {一|yí}{个|gè}. This course writes the change. yī is kept for counting and in numbers; yì comes before tones 1 to 3.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word __妈 (mā ma, mum)?
questions.explanation: 妈妈 is written with 妈: 女 (woman) + 马 (horse), which gives the sound ma. 吗 has 口 instead (the question particle), 马 alone is "horse", and 她 is "she".

questions.stem: In {=这=} (this), which part is written last?
choices: the dot at the very top
questions.explanation: {=辶 is always written last, after the part it carries: first 文 (dot, horizontal, left-falling, right-falling), then 辶 (dot, zigzag, sweep).=} The traditional form, {+这+}, has 言 in place of 文, and 辶 still comes last.

questions.stem: Read: A: "{这|zhè}{是|shì}{你|nǐ}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}{吗|ma}？" B: "{不|bú}{是|shì}，{这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}。" Whose name is it?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{的|de}{名字|míng zi}: "my older brother's name". {我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge} has no {的|de} (family), and the {的|de} after it marks the brother as the owner of the name.

questions.stem: Listen. What is true about the speaker?

audio.text: 我有一个哥哥和一个姐姐。

choices: has an older brother and an older sister
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{哥哥|gē ge}{和|hé}{一|yí}{个|gè}{姐姐|jiě jie}: one older brother ({哥哥|gē ge}) and one older sister ({姐姐|jiě jie}), joined by {和|hé}. There was no {没有|méi yǒu}.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{人|rén}？ asks how many people are in your family. {五|wǔ}{个|gè}{人|rén} (five people) puts a number where {几|jǐ} was. One older sister doesn't answer the question.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?

audio.text: 这是我爸爸，那是我妈妈。

choices: showing Dad close by and Mum further away
showing Mum close by and Dad further away
saying that Dad and Mum are both here
showing an older brother and an older sister
questions.explanation: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba} (this is my dad), {那|nà}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma} (that is my mum): {这|zhè} is near, {那|nà} further away.

questions.stem: Listen. Which sentence did you hear?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}{姐姐|jiě jie}: "I don't have an older sister." Listen for méi before yǒu, and for jiě jie (sister) rather than gē ge (brother).

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{张小红|Zhāng Xiǎo hóng}。{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{四|sì}{个|gè}{人|rén}：{爸爸|bà ba}、{妈妈|mā ma}、{姐姐|jiě jie}{和|hé}{我|wǒ}。{我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{和|hé}{妈妈|mā ma}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。{我|wǒ}{姐姐|jiě jie}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。" How many people are in Zhang Xiaohong's family, and who are the teachers?
choices: four; her sister and her mother
questions.explanation: {四|sì}{个|gè}{人|rén}: four people, including Zhang Xiaohong herself. {爸爸|bà ba}{和|hé}{妈妈|mā ma}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}: both parents are teachers; her older sister is a student.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: This is my older brother.
questions.explanation: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}。 "This" is {这|zhè}; {那|nà} would be "that". With family, no {的|de} is needed after {我|wǒ}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: My dad and mum are both teachers.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{和|hé}{妈妈|mā ma} is the subject; {都|dōu} (both) sums it up before the verb: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{和|hé}{妈妈|mā ma}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。 The pair can also go without {和|hé}: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{妈妈|mā ma}{都|dōu}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {爸爸|bà ba} dad, {妈妈|mā ma} mum, {哥哥|gē ge} older brother, {姐姐|jiě jie} older sister, {家|jiā} home or family. A younger brother is {弟弟|dì di}, in the next lesson.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {没有|méi yǒu}: a rising second tone, then a dipping third (2+3).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {姐姐|jiě jie}: a third tone, then a neutral tone, as in every doubled family word (3+neutral).

questions.stem: How do you say "two people"?
questions.explanation: Before a measure word, "two" is {两|liǎng}: {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{人|rén}. {二|èr} is for counting and inside numbers, {十二|shí èr} is twelve, and {们|men} is never used after a number.

questions.stem: Which is 105?
questions.explanation: {一百零五|yì bǎi líng wǔ}: one hundred, zero (for the empty tens), five. {一百五|yì bǎi wǔ} is the spoken short form of 150, {一零五|yāo líng wǔ} reads digits one by one like a room number, and the "one" before {百|bǎi} can't be dropped.

questions.stem: Which is 2,026?
choices: {二千二十六|èr qiān èr shí liù}
{两千二十六|liǎng qiān èr shí liù}
{两千二百六|liǎng qiān èr bǎi liù}
{两千零二十六|liǎng qiān líng èr shí liù}
questions.explanation: 2,026 has no hundreds, so {零|líng} fills the gap: {两千零二十六|liǎng qiān líng èr shí liù}. Without {零|líng} the number is incomplete, and {两千二百六|liǎng qiān èr bǎi liù} means 2,260. Before {千|qiān}, {两|liǎng} is the usual word for two.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "My younger sister is eight."?
questions.explanation: Age is a number + {岁|suì} after the subject, with no {是|shì}: {我|wǒ}{妹妹|mèi mei}{八|bā}{岁|suì}。 {岁|suì} is itself a measure word, so {个|gè} isn't added, and the number comes before {岁|suì}.

questions.stem: Which is the natural way to ask a five-year-old child their age?
questions.explanation: {几岁|jǐ suì} expects a small number, so it suits a child, and the friendly {了|le} is often added. {岁|suì} takes no {个|gè}, {几|jǐ}{口|kǒu}{人|rén} asks about family size, and a question word takes no {吗|ma}.

questions.stem: Which word fits the blank? {你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ} ___ {人|rén}？ (How many people are there in your family?)
questions.explanation: {口|kǒu} (mouth) is the measure word for the people in a family: {几|jǐ}{口|kǒu}{人|rén}. {个|gè} would also work, more casually. {岁|suì} is for age, and {两|liǎng} and {多|duō} aren't measure words.

questions.stem: Which word fits the blank? {中国|Zhōng guó}{有|yǒu} ___ {人|rén}？ (How many people does China have?)
questions.explanation: The answer is a huge number, so use {多少|duō shao}, which suits any number and needs no measure word. {几|jǐ} expects a small number (and always a measure word), and {两|liǎng} is "two".

questions.stem: How do you say "twelve years old"?
questions.explanation: The last digit of a number is always {二|èr}, even before a measure word: {十二|shí èr}{岁|suì}. {两|liǎng} replaces {二|èr} only when "two" stands alone before the measure word: {两|liǎng}{岁|suì}. Twenty would be {二十|èr shí}, and ten needs no "one" in front.

questions.stem: How is 一百 (100) written in this course's pinyin?
questions.explanation: {一|yī} becomes yì before a first, second or third tone, and {百|bǎi} is third: {一百|yì bǎi}. Before a fourth tone it would be yí ({一|yí}{个|gè}), and yī stays at the end of a number ({十一|shí yī}).

questions.stem: Which is the pinyin of 女儿 (daughter)?
questions.explanation: {女儿|nǚ ér}: a third tone, then a second. After n, ü keeps its dots (nǔ would be a different syllable, as in 努), and both syllables keep a full tone, unlike {儿子|ér zi}.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word 多__ (duō shao, how many)?
questions.explanation: 多少 is written with 少 (few): 小 with an extra left-falling stroke. 小 is "small", and 沙 (sand) and 步 (step) are look-alikes you'll meet later.

questions.stem: Which character means "hundred"?
questions.explanation: 百 (bǎi) is 白 with a horizontal stroke on top. 白 alone is "white", 千 (qiān) is "thousand", and 日 is "sun, day".

questions.stem: 那 and 都 have 阝 on the right. What does the right-hand 阝 come from?
questions.explanation: On the right, 阝 comes from 邑, "town"; on the left (as in 院, lesson 21) it comes from 阜, "mound, hill". The two look the same, and people call them "right ear" and "left ear" from their shape, but neither comes from 耳.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the speaker say?
choices: There are five people in my family.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{五|wǔ}{口|kǒu}{人|rén}: {口|kǒu} counts the members of a family. Children would be {孩子|hái zi}, and an age would end in {岁|suì}.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the speaker say?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{弟弟|dì di}{十五|shí wǔ}{岁|suì}: dì di is a younger brother (an older one is gē ge, a younger sister mèi mei), and shí wǔ is fifteen.

questions.stem: Listen. Which number did you hear?
questions.explanation: {三千四百零八|sān qiān sì bǎi líng bā}: three thousand, four hundred, zero (no tens), eight = 3,408. 3,480 would end {八十|bā shí}, and 3,048 would be {三千零四十八|sān qiān líng sì shí bā}.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{多大|duō dà}？ asks a young adult's age, so the answer is a number + {岁|suì}: {我|wǒ}{二十|èr shí}{岁|suì}。 The others answer questions about family and how you are.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{五|wǔ}{口|kǒu}{人|rén}：{爸爸|bà ba}、{妈妈|mā ma}、{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{妹妹|mèi mei}{和|hé}{我|wǒ}。{我|wǒ}{二十|èr shí}{岁|suì}，{我|wǒ}{妹妹|mèi mei}{一|yí}{个|gè}{十二|shí èr}{岁|suì}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{九|jiǔ}{岁|suì}。" How old is the younger sister?
questions.explanation: {一|yí}{个|gè}{十二|shí èr}{岁|suì}，{一|yí}{个|gè}{九|jiǔ}{岁|suì}: one is twelve, the other nine, so the younger one is nine. Twenty is the writer's own age, and {两|liǎng} counts the sisters.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I have two younger sisters.
questions.explanation: Number + measure word + noun after {有|yǒu}: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{妹妹|mèi mei}。 Before {个|gè} "two" is {两|liǎng}, not {二|èr}.

questions.stem: Type the word for "son" (pinyin with tone numbers or characters): ___
questions.explanation: Son is {儿子|ér zi} (type er2 zi5 or er2 zi). Daughter is {女儿|nǚ ér}, and a child of either sex is {孩子|hái zi}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {岁|suì}, years old: a falling fourth tone.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {孩子|hái zi}: a rising second tone, then the light ending {子|zi} (2+neutral).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I work at a company."?
questions.explanation: {在|zài} + place comes before the verb: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。 Putting the place after {工作|gōng zuò} copies English. {在|zài} can't come before the subject, and {是|shì} doesn't say where.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "My mum is at home."?
questions.explanation: {在|zài} + place says where someone is: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。 {是|shì} would make her "a home", {有|yǒu}{家|jiā} is "has a home", and {在|zài} must come before the place.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "My mum works at a company too."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{也|yě}{工作|gōng zuò}。
{也|yě}{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。
{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{也|yě}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。
{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{也|yě}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。
questions.explanation: The order is subject, adverb, {在|zài} + place, verb: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{也|yě}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。 {也|yě} goes before the whole {在|zài} phrase, not after it, and never before the subject.

questions.stem: How do you ask "What do you do (for a living)?"
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{做|zuò}{什么|shén me}{工作|gōng zuò}？ "What work do you do?" {工作|gōng zuò}{什么|shén me} isn't a Chinese pattern, a question with {什么|shén me} takes no {吗|ma}, and {你|nǐ}{做|zuò}{工作|gōng zuò}{吗|ma} only asks whether you work.

questions.stem: Which means "a teacher of Chinese" (someone who teaches the language)?
questions.explanation: The modifier comes first and says what kind: {汉语|Hàn yǔ}{老师|lǎo shī} teaches Chinese. {中国|Zhōng guó}{老师|lǎo shī} is a teacher from China, whatever they teach. The modifier can't go after the noun, and {中国人|Zhōng guó rén}{老师|lǎo shī} isn't said.

questions.stem: A: "{你|nǐ}{爸爸|bà ba}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吗|ma}？" (Is your dad at home?) B: "No." Which word does B say?
questions.explanation: Answer with the verb of the question: {在|zài}, so {不|bú}{在|zài}. {不|bú}{是|shì} answers {是|shì} questions, {没有|méi yǒu} answers {有|yǒu} questions, and {不|bú}{会|huì} answers {会|huì} questions.

questions.stem: In which sentence is 工作 a noun ("a job")?
choices: {他们|tā men}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{工作|gōng zuò}。
questions.explanation: After {有|yǒu} (to have), {工作|gōng zuò} is the thing you have: a job. In the other sentences it follows {在|zài} + place and is the verb, "to work".

questions.stem: How are 学生 (student) and 大学生 (university student) written in pinyin?
questions.explanation: {学生|xué sheng} has a light second syllable in mainland speech, but in {大学生|dà xué shēng} (and {医生|yī shēng}) 生 keeps its first tone. 学 is always xué, second tone.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {在|zài} has a falling fourth tone, so {不|bù} before it becomes bú: {不|bú}{在|zài}. {再|zài} (again) sounds exactly the same.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word 工__ (gōng zuò, to work)?
questions.explanation: 工作 is written with 作: 亻 + 乍. 做 (to do, lesson 9) is also read zuò, so it's easy to mix up, but 工作 always takes 作. 昨 (yesterday) has 日 on the left, and 怎 (how) has 心 underneath.

questions.stem: Which two parts make up 男 (male)?
questions.explanation: 男 is 田 (field) over 力 (strength, a plough in the oldest forms). 日 has one line inside, not a cross; 刀 has no stroke crossing through it, and 口 is empty inside.

questions.stem: Which character means "to be at"?
questions.explanation: 在 (zài) has 土 at the bottom right. 有 (to have) has 月 there, and 左 (left) and 右 (right), which you'll meet in HSK 2, have 工 and 口.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the sentence mean?
questions.explanation: {他|tā}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{工作|gōng zuò}: {在|zài} + place + {工作|gōng zuò}, "works at a university". A student would be {大学生|dà xué shēng}, a school {学校|xué xiào}, and there was no {不|bù}.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker's mother do?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{是|shì}{医生|yī shēng}: yī shēng is a doctor. A teacher is lǎo shī and a student xué sheng; a company would be gōng sī.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{爸爸|bà ba}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吗|ma}？ asks whether your dad is at home, so answer with {在|zài} (or {不|bú}{在|zài}). The other replies answer different questions.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the sentence mean?
choices: We all work at a company.
questions.explanation: {我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}: {都|dōu} (all) + {在|zài} (to be at) + {学校|xué xiào} (school). "Too" would be {也|yě}, and "students" {学生|xué sheng}.

questions.stem: Read the name badge: "{刘华|Liú Huá} · {北京大学|Běi jīng Dà xué} · {汉语|Hàn yǔ}{老师|lǎo shī}" ({北京大学|Běi jīng Dà xué}: Peking University). What does Liu Hua do?
choices: works for a company in Beijing
is a doctor at a hospital
questions.explanation: {汉语|Hàn yǔ}{老师|lǎo shī} is a teacher of Chinese, and {北京大学|Běi jīng Dà xué} is the university. A student would be {学生|xué sheng} or {大学生|dà xué shēng}.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{王静|Wáng Jìng}。{我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{是|shì}{医生|yī shēng}，{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{是|shì}{大学生|dà xué shēng}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}。" Who works for a company?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}: her mother works for a company. Her father is a doctor, her brother is a university student, and Wang Jing is a student too.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: My older sister works at a university.
questions.explanation: Subject ({我|wǒ}{姐姐|jiě jie}), then {在|zài} + place, then the verb: {我|wǒ}{姐姐|jiě jie}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{工作|gōng zuò}。 No {是|shì}: the verb is {工作|gōng zuò}.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {医生|yī shēng} doctor, {老师|lǎo shī} teacher, {大学生|dà xué shēng} university student, {公司|gōng sī} company, {学校|xué xiào} school. A hospital is {医院|yī yuàn} (lesson 21).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {学校|xué xiào}: a rising second tone, then a falling fourth (2+4).

questions.stem: In the name {张小红|Zhāng Xiǎo hóng}, which part is the family name?
questions.explanation: Chinese names put the family name first: {张|Zhāng}, then the given name {小红|Xiǎo hóng}. Most family names are one character, and given names one or two.

questions.stem: How do you politely ask an older person's family name?
questions.explanation: {您|nín}{贵姓|guì xìng}？ "Your honourable family name?" is the polite set question. {你|nǐ}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me} is for people your age, and the other two mix patterns ({姓|xìng} takes a name, not {名字|míng zi}).

questions.stem: Someone asks you "{您|nín}{贵姓|guì xìng}？" and your family name is Li. What do you answer?
questions.explanation: {贵|guì} (honourable) is only for the other person. About yourself say {我|wǒ}{姓|xìng}{李|Lǐ}, and you can add your full name: {叫|jiào}{李明|Lǐ Míng}.

questions.stem: According to the 2020 national name report, which five family names were the most common in mainland China?
choices: {欧阳|Ōu yáng}, {司马|Sī mǎ}, {诸葛|Zhū gě}, {王|Wáng}, {李|Lǐ}
questions.explanation: {王|Wáng}, {李|Lǐ}, {张|Zhāng}, {刘|Liú} and {陈|Chén}: together about three in ten registered people. Two-character family names such as {欧阳|Ōu yáng} are rare, and {明|míng}, {芳|fāng} and {文|wén} are typical given-name characters.

questions.stem: Which way of addressing someone is friendly but only for an older colleague or friend you know well?
questions.explanation: {老|lǎo} + family name is friendly and respectful between people who know each other, for someone older. {小王|Xiǎo Wáng} is for someone younger, {王老师|Wáng lǎo shī} is a title that's always safe, and the full name suits classmates and colleagues.

questions.stem: You visit a Chinese friend's home and meet their mother. What is a natural greeting?
questions.explanation: Young people call a friend's mother {阿姨|ā yí} (auntie), and a friend's father {叔叔|shū shu} (uncle). {妈妈|mā ma} is for your own mother, and {你好吗|nǐ hǎo ma} isn't a first greeting.

questions.stem: Which statement about family names and marriage in mainland China is true?
choices: A wife must take her husband's family name.
Children always take the mother's family name.
Married couples join their two family names into one.
Each spouse keeps their own name, and a child takes the father's or the mother's family name.
questions.explanation: The Civil Code gives each spouse the right to use their own name (Article 1056), and a child takes the father's or the mother's family name (Article 1015); the father's is the more common choice.

questions.stem: How is the name 王芳 written in pinyin, following the spelling rules?
questions.explanation: The family name and the given name are two words, each with a capital: Wáng Fāng. In English some people swap the order to Fang Wang, but in pinyin the Chinese order stays.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's family name?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{姓|xìng}{陈|Chén}，{叫|jiào}{陈文|Chén Wén}: the family name is {陈|Chén}, said after {姓|xìng}; {文|Wén} is the given name.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking for?
questions.explanation: {您贵姓|nín guì xìng}？ is the polite way to ask for someone's family name. Age would be {多大|duō dà}, a job {做|zuò}{什么|shén me}{工作|gōng zuò}, and where someone is from {哪|nǎ}{国|guó}{人|rén}.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{大卫|Dà wèi}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{中文|Zhōng wén}{名字|míng zi}{叫|jiào}{王文|Wáng Wén}。{王|Wáng}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{中国|Zhōng guó}{姓|xìng}。" What kind of Chinese name does David have?
choices: only a sound loan of his English name
a Chinese-style name with the family name Wang
questions.explanation: {大卫|Dà wèi} is a sound loan of David, but he also has a Chinese-style name, {王文|Wáng Wén}: the family name {王|Wáng} plus a given name. {姓|xìng} here is a noun, "family name".

questions.stem: Read the name card: "{李|Lǐ} {华|Huá} · {医生|yī shēng}". How would you greet this person at work?
questions.explanation: Family name + title, then the polite greeting: {李医生|Lǐ yī shēng}，{您好|nín hǎo}！ The title goes after the family name (not the given name {华|Huá}), and {小李|Xiǎo Lǐ} is for a younger person you know well.

questions.stem: About how old are the oracle-bone inscriptions, the oldest large body of Chinese writing?
questions.explanation: They date from the late Shang dynasty, roughly 1250–1050 BCE: over 3,000 years ago. Bronze inscriptions followed, and the simplified characters of this course were standardised in 1956 and 1964.

questions.stem: What were the oracle bones used for?
choices: asking the ancestors questions, read from cracks in heated bone or shell
questions.explanation: Shang kings had ox shoulder blades and turtle shells heated until they cracked, read the answer from the cracks, and had the question carved beside them: divination.

questions.stem: Which character began as a drawing of three peaks rising from one line?
questions.explanation: {山|shān}, mountain. {水|shuǐ} was a winding stream with drops, {木|mù} a tree with branches and roots, and {门|mén} (門) the two wings of a door.

questions.stem: In 妈 (mā, mother), what does the part 马 (mǎ, horse) contribute?
questions.explanation: 妈 is phonetic-semantic: 女 (woman) gives the meaning and {马|mǎ} the sound ma. The horse has nothing to do with the meaning.

questions.stem: Which two characters share a sound part?
questions.explanation: {妈|mā} and {吗|ma} both take 马 as the sound part, with different meaning parts (女 and 口). 妈 and 她 share the meaning part 女, and 们 and 他 share 亻.

questions.stem: Which kind of character is 上 (shàng, up, above)?
choices: an indicative: a mark points at the idea
questions.explanation: In its oldest form, {上|shàng} was a short mark above a longer line: a pointer at "above". {下|xià} was the same with the mark below. "Up" can't be drawn as a thing, so it isn't a pictograph.

questions.stem: How is 休 (xiū, to rest) usually explained?
questions.explanation: {休|xiū} is 亻 (person) + {木|mù} (tree): someone resting against a tree, a compound of two meanings. A woman with a child is the traditional story of {好|hǎo}, and sun and moon of {明|míng}.

questions.stem: By common estimates, how many characters are phonetic-semantic (a meaning part plus a sound part)?
choices: about eight or nine in ten
questions.explanation: Most characters, roughly 80 to 90 percent by common estimates, combine a meaning part with a sound part. Pictographs, the best-known kind, number only a few hundred.

questions.stem: Listen. Which character did you hear? Listen for the tone.
questions.explanation: You heard {马|mǎ} (horse), a low, dipping third tone. {妈|mā} is high and level, {骂|mà} (to scold) falls, and {吗|ma} is light and neutral. The same sound part, four different syllables.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker naming?
questions.explanation: {甲骨文|jiǎ gǔ wén}, "shell and bone writing": the oracle-bone inscriptions. Bronze inscriptions are {金文|jīn wén}.

questions.stem: Read: "{林|lín}{是|shì}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{木|mù}，{森|sēn}{是|shì}{三|sān}{个|gè}{木|mù}。" ({林|lín}: woods; {森|sēn}: forest) What kind of characters are 林 and 森?
questions.explanation: "林 is two 木 (trees), 森 is three": the meaning comes from putting trees together, so they are compounds. Neither part gives a sound, and neither is a single picture.

questions.stem: Read: "{这|zhè}{个|gè}{字|zì}{是|shì}{女|nǚ}{和|hé}{子|zǐ}。" Which character is it?
questions.explanation: "This character is 女 and 子": {好|hǎo}, good. {妈|mā} is 女 + 马, {字|zì} is 宀 + 子, and {她|tā} is 女 + 也.

questions.stem: Which is the Chinese order for "Monday, 16 November 2026"?
questions.explanation: Chinese dates go from the biggest unit to the smallest: year, month, day, then the weekday. The other orders copy English or European habits (day first, or month and day before the year).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Today isn't Monday."?
choices: {今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{星期一|xīng qī yī}。
{今天|jīn tiān}{星期一|xīng qī yī}{不|bù}。
{今天|jīn tiān}{不是|bú shì}{星期一|xīng qī yī}。
{不|bù}{今天|jīn tiān}{星期一|xīng qī yī}。
questions.explanation: {今天|jīn tiān}{星期一|xīng qī yī} needs no verb, but the negative does: {不|bù} must stand before a verb, so {是|shì} comes back: {今天|jīn tiān}{不是|bú shì}{星期一|xīng qī yī}. {不|bù} directly before a noun, or at the end or the start, is not Chinese.

questions.stem: Which means "two months" (an amount of time)?
questions.explanation: An amount of months needs the measure word {个|gè}, and "two" before a measure word is {两|liǎng}: {两个月|liǎng gè yuè}. {二月|èr yuè} is February, a month name. {两月|liǎng yuè} leaves out {个|gè}, and {二个|èr gè} uses the wrong "two".

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I don't work on Saturdays."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{工作|gōng zuò}{星期六|xīng qī liù}。
{我|wǒ}{工作|gōng zuò}{不|bù}{星期六|xīng qī liù}。
{我|wǒ}{星期六|xīng qī liù}{不|bù}{工作|gōng zuò}。
{星期六|xīng qī liù}{不|bù}{我|wǒ}{工作|gōng zuò}。
questions.explanation: A time word goes before the verb (after the subject or at the front), and {不|bù} goes right before the verb: {我|wǒ}{星期六|xīng qī liù}{不|bù}{工作|gōng zuò}. Putting the day at the end is English order; {不|bù} can't stand before the subject.

questions.stem: In 一月 (January), how is 一 said?
questions.explanation: In dates, months, weekdays and years {一|yī} is a number in a series, so it keeps its first tone: {一月|yī yuè}, {一号|yī hào}, {星期一|xīng qī yī}. It changes only when it counts something: {一个月|yí gè yuè} (one month), {一天|yì tiān} (one day).

questions.stem: Which character completes the word 今__ (jīn tiān, today)?
questions.explanation: 今天 ends in 天 (day): 大 with a line on top. 大 (big) has no top line, 太 (too) has a dot, and 夫 (man, husband) has its top line crossing the vertical.

questions.stem: Which radical do 明, 昨 and 星 share?
questions.explanation: All three have 日 (sun, day): on the left in 明 and 昨, on top in 星. 月 is the right side of 明 and the radical of 期; 口 is in 号; 目 has one more inner stroke than 日.

questions.stem: Match each day to its English name.
questions.explanation: The weekdays are numbered from Monday: {星期一|xīng qī yī} is day one, {星期三|xīng qī sān} day three, {星期五|xīng qī wǔ} day five. Sunday has no number: {星期天|xīng qī tiān} (or {星期日|xīng qī rì} in writing). Tuesday would be {星期二|xīng qī èr} and Saturday {星期六|xīng qī liù}.

questions.stem: Listen. What's the date today?
questions.explanation: You heard {今天|jīn tiān}{十一月|shí yī yuè}{十二号|shí èr hào}: the month comes first ({十一月|shí yī yuè}, November), then the day ({十二号|shí èr hào}, the 12th). 11 December would be {十二月|shí èr yuè}{十一号|shí yī hào}.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?
questions.explanation: {明天|míng tiān}{星期四|xīng qī sì}: tomorrow (míng tiān) is Thursday (day four, sì). Today would be {今天|jīn tiān}, Tuesday {星期二|xīng qī èr}, and "the 4th" {四号|sì hào}.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.
choices: {是|shì}，{今天|jīn tiān}{星期五|xīng qī wǔ}。
questions.explanation: {星期几|xīng qī jǐ} asks which day of the week, so the answer puts the day where {几|jǐ} was: {今天|jīn tiān}{星期五|xīng qī wǔ}. {十号|shí hào} answers {几号|jǐ hào} (the date), {五月|wǔ yuè} is a month, and {是|shì} answers a yes/no question, not a question with {几|jǐ}.

questions.stem: Listen. True or false: tomorrow is Saturday.

audio.text: 明天是星期六吗？不是，明天星期五。

questions.explanation: The question was {明天|míng tiān}{是|shì}{星期六|xīng qī liù}{吗|ma}？ and the answer {不是|bú shì}，{明天|míng tiān}{星期五|xīng qī wǔ}: no, tomorrow is Friday.

questions.stem: Read the desk calendar page: "2026{年|nián}5{月|yuè}　1　{星期五|xīng qī wǔ}". What day is it?
questions.explanation: Big to small: 2026{年|nián} (the year), 5{月|yuè} (May, month five), the big 1 (the day), and {星期五|xīng qī wǔ} (Friday, day five of the week). Don't take the 5 of {星期五|xīng qī wǔ} for the date, or 5{月|yuè} for January.

questions.stem: How is the year 1998年 read?
choices: yì qiān jiǔ bǎi jiǔ shí bā nián
shí jiǔ jiǔ shí bā nián
questions.explanation: Years are read digit by digit, then {年|nián}: yī jiǔ jiǔ bā nián. Not as a big number (one thousand nine hundred…), and not split in two as in English (nineteen ninety-eight). {一|yī} is a digit here, so it keeps its first tone.

questions.stem: Read: "{今天|jīn tiān}{是|shì}{十二月|shí èr yuè}{三十一号|sān shí yī hào}。" What's the date tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Today is 31 December ({十二月|shí èr yuè}{三十一号|sān shí yī hào}), so tomorrow is {一月|yī yuè}{一号|yī hào}, 1 January. 30 December was yesterday ({昨天|zuó tiān}).

questions.stem: Type the word for "tomorrow" (pinyin with tone numbers, for example ni3 hao3, or characters): ___
questions.explanation: Tomorrow is {明天|míng tiān}: a second tone, then a first tone (type ming2 tian1). Yesterday is {昨天|zuó tiān} and today {今天|jīn tiān}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Today is Wednesday, 20 May.
questions.explanation: The time word {今天|jīn tiān} is the subject, and the date follows big to small: month, day, weekday. No verb is needed: {今天|jīn tiān}{五月|wǔ yuè}{二十号|èr shí hào}{星期三|xīng qī sān}。

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I'm at home on Sunday.
questions.explanation: The time word goes before the verb, either after the subject ({我|wǒ}{星期天|xīng qī tiān}{在|zài}{家|jiā}) or at the front ({星期天|xīng qī tiān}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}). Both are correct.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {昨天|zuó tiān}, yesterday: a rising 2nd tone, then a high level 1st.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the three syllables?
questions.explanation: {星期日|xīng qī rì}, Sunday: two high level 1st tones, then a falling 4th.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {年|nián}, year: the 2nd tone, rising.

questions.stem: How do you say "two o'clock"?
questions.explanation: {点|diǎn} counts like a measure word, and before a measure word "two" is {两|liǎng}: {两点|liǎng diǎn}. {二点|èr diǎn} is the classic mistake; {两个点|liǎng gè diǎn} adds an extra measure word, and {时|shí} isn't the spoken word for o'clock.

questions.stem: Which means "two hours" (an amount of time)?
questions.explanation: An amount of hours is {小时|xiǎo shí}, usually with {个|gè}: {两个小时|liǎng gè xiǎo shí}. {两点|liǎng diǎn} is two o'clock, a point on the clock; {二小时|èr xiǎo shí} uses the wrong "two"; {两分钟|liǎng fēn zhōng} is two minutes.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I have class at eight."? ({上课|shàng kè}: to have class)
choices: {我|wǒ}{上课|shàng kè}{八个小时|bā gè xiǎo shí}。
questions.explanation: A time when something happens goes before the verb: {我|wǒ}{八点|bā diǎn}{上课|shàng kè}. After the verb is English order, and {八个小时|bā gè xiǎo shí} after the verb is a duration: "I have eight hours of class".

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I work eight hours a day."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{一天|yì tiān}{八个小时|bā gè xiǎo shí}{工作|gōng zuò}。
{我|wǒ}{一天|yì tiān}{工作|gōng zuò}{八点|bā diǎn}。
{我|wǒ}{八点|bā diǎn}{一天|yì tiān}{工作|gōng zuò}。
{我|wǒ}{一天|yì tiān}{工作|gōng zuò}{八个小时|bā gè xiǎo shí}。
questions.explanation: A duration goes after the verb: {工作|gōng zuò}{八个小时|bā gè xiǎo shí}. Before the verb it reads like a time when, and {八点|bā diǎn} is eight o'clock, not eight hours.

questions.stem: How do you say "3:30 p.m."?
questions.explanation: The part of the day comes before the clock time (big to small), and {半|bàn} follows the hour: {下午|xià wǔ}{三点半|sān diǎn bàn}. {上午|shàng wǔ} is the morning.

questions.stem: Which means "one and a half hours"?
choices: {一个半小时|yí gè bàn xiǎo shí}
{一个小时半|yí gè xiǎo shí bàn}
questions.explanation: {半|bàn} goes straight after the measure word: {一个半小时|yí gè bàn xiǎo shí}. Putting it at the end copies English. {一点半|yī diǎn bàn} is 1:30 on the clock, and {半个小时|bàn gè xiǎo shí} is half an hour.

questions.stem: 几点 (what time?) is written jǐ diǎn. How is it said?
choices: jǐ dián: the second syllable rises
jì diǎn: the first syllable falls
jí diǎn: the first syllable rises
questions.explanation: Two third tones in a row: the first is said like a second tone, jí diǎn. Pinyin keeps the dictionary tones. The same happens in {两点|liǎng diǎn} (liáng diǎn) and {九点|jiǔ diǎn} (jiú diǎn).

questions.stem: Which character completes the word 下__ (xià wǔ, afternoon)?
questions.explanation: 下午 is written with 午 (noon). 牛 (ox) looks almost the same, but its vertical stroke pokes up through the top; 年 (year) has more strokes, and 千 (thousand, lesson 4) has only one horizontal.

questions.stem: Which character means "half"?
questions.explanation: 半 (bàn, half): two short strokes on top, two horizontals and a vertical through the middle. 分 is minute, 午 noon and 点 o'clock.

questions.stem: Listen. What time is it?
questions.explanation: {九点十分|jiǔ diǎn shí fēn}: the hour (nine) comes first, then the minutes (ten). 10:09 would be {十点零九分|shí diǎn líng jiǔ fēn}.

questions.stem: Listen. What time is it?
questions.explanation: {两点半|liǎng diǎn bàn}: two o'clock and a half. Listen for bàn at the end; 12:30 would be {十二点半|shí èr diǎn bàn}.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about her?
choices: She works ten hours a day.
questions.explanation: {十个小时|shí gè xiǎo shí} after the verb is a duration: ten hours. {一天|yì tiān} (a day) before the verb says how often. "At ten" would be {十点|shí diǎn} before the verb.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.
choices: {有|yǒu}，{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{半个小时|bàn gè xiǎo shí}。
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{现在|xiàn zài}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}{吗|ma}？ asks "Do you have time now?", so answer with {有|yǒu} (or {没有|méi yǒu}). {现在|xiàn zài}{三点|sān diǎn} answers "What time is it?" instead.

questions.stem: Read the sign: "{上课|shàng kè}{时间|shí jiān}　{上午|shàng wǔ} 8:00—12:00　{下午|xià wǔ} 2:00—5:00". How many hours of class are there a day? ({上课|shàng kè}{时间|shí jiān}: class times)
questions.explanation: Four hours in the morning (8 to 12) and three in the afternoon (2 to 5): seven hours, {七个小时|qī gè xiǎo shí}. There are no classes from noon to two.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{上午|shàng wǔ}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}{四个小时|sì gè xiǎo shí}，{下午|xià wǔ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。" Which is true?
choices: The writer works four hours in the morning.
The writer starts work at four in the morning.
The writer is at the office in the afternoon.
The writer works at home for four hours.
questions.explanation: {四个小时|sì gè xiǎo shí} after {工作|gōng zuò} is a duration: four hours of work, in the morning ({上午|shàng wǔ}) at the office ({在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}). In the afternoon the writer is at home.

questions.stem: Type the word for "hour" (an amount of time; pinyin with tone numbers or characters): ___
questions.explanation: An hour is {小时|xiǎo shí}: a third tone, then a second (type xiao3 shi2). {点|diǎn} is "o'clock", a point on the clock.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese. ({上课|shàng kè}: to have class)
questions.prompt: I have class at nine in the morning.
questions.explanation: The time goes before the verb, big to small: {上午|shàng wǔ}{九点|jiǔ diǎn}. It can follow the subject ({我|wǒ}{上午|shàng wǔ}{九点|jiǔ diǎn}{上课|shàng kè}) or stand at the front, and the part of the day can open the sentence with the clock time after the subject.

questions.stem: Match each time to the clock.
left: {八点零五分|bā diǎn líng wǔ fēn}
questions.explanation: {半|bàn} is half past: 8:30. {零五分|líng wǔ fēn} is five minutes with a zero before it: 8:05 (8:50 would be {八点五十|bā diǎn wǔ shí}). Two o'clock is {两点|liǎng diǎn}, and twelve o'clock {十二点|shí èr diǎn}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {小时|xiǎo shí}, hour: a low 3rd tone, then a rising 2nd.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {现在|xiàn zài}, now: two falling 4th tones.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {半|bàn}, half: the 4th tone, falling. Not {班|bān} (shift), which is high and level.

questions.stem: Which is "tomorrow at seven in the morning"?
choices: {明天|míng tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{七点|qī diǎn}
{七点|qī diǎn}{明天|míng tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}
{早上|zǎo shang}{七点|qī diǎn}{明天|míng tiān}
{明天|míng tiān}{七点|qī diǎn}{早上|zǎo shang}
questions.explanation: Time words line up from the biggest unit to the smallest: the day ({明天|míng tiān}), the part of the day ({早上|zǎo shang}), the clock time ({七点|qī diǎn}). English goes the other way round.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I have dinner at home in the evening."?
