choices: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{晚上|wǎn shang}{吃|chī}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}。
{我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{吃|chī}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
{我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}。
{我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}{晚上|wǎn shang}{在|zài}{家|jiā}。
questions.explanation: The normal order is subject, time, place, verb, object: {我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{晚饭|wǎn fàn}. Time comes before place, and both come before the verb, never after it.

questions.stem: Why is "睡觉八个小时" (for "sleep eight hours") wrong?
choices: A duration always goes before the verb
睡觉 already has its object (觉) inside, so no object can follow it
睡觉 is only used for the evening
八个小时 needs another measure word
questions.explanation: {睡觉|shuì jiào} is a separable verb: {睡|shuì} (sleep) + {觉|jiào} (a sleep). The duration either goes inside it ({睡|shuì}{八个小时|bā gè xiǎo shí}{的|de}{觉|jiào}) or follows {睡|shuì} alone (lesson 21). A duration does follow the verb, so "A duration always goes before the verb" is wrong too.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: "___ {十点|shí diǎn}，{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}。" (At ten in the morning I'm at the office.)
questions.explanation: Ten in the morning is {上午|shàng wǔ}{十点|shí diǎn}: {上午|shàng wǔ} is the whole morning until noon. {早上|zǎo shang} is the early part of the morning, and {晚上|wǎn shang}{十点|shí diǎn} would be 10 p.m.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "You're early!"?
questions.explanation: {早|zǎo} is an adjective, so it takes {很|hěn} and no {是|shì}: {你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{早|zǎo}！ {早上|zǎo shang} is a noun, "morning", and can't be the predicate here. ({你早|nǐ zǎo}！ without {很|hěn} is the greeting "Morning!")

questions.stem: Which is the pinyin of 睡觉 (to go to bed)?
questions.explanation: {睡觉|shuì jiào}: two fourth tones. 觉 is jiào in this word but jué in {觉得|jué de} (to feel), so learn it inside the word. Shuì starts with a curled-back sh, not s.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word 起__ (qǐ chuáng, to get up)?
questions.explanation: {=起床 is written with 床 (bed): the shelter 广 with wood 木 inside. 广 and 木 are only its parts, and 店 (shop) has 广 with 占 inside.=}

questions.stem: Which radical is on the left of {=饭=} (meal) in simplified characters?
questions.explanation: {=饭 has 饣, the side form of 食 (food): {早饭|zǎo fàn}, {午饭|wǔ fàn}, {晚饭|wǎn fàn}. 钅 (metal) is in 钟, 讠 (speech) in 说 and 语, 亻 (person) in 他 and 你.=}

questions.stem: Which character means "early"?
questions.explanation: {=早 (zǎo, early) is 日 over 十. 旱 (drought) has 干 under the sun instead, 草 (grass) has 艹 on top, and 晚 is the opposite, "late".=}

questions.stem: Listen. What time does the speaker get up?
questions.explanation: {六点半|liù diǎn bàn}: six o'clock and a half, 6:30. {起床|qǐ chuáng} is to get up.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about him?
questions.explanation: {下午|xià wǔ}{五点|wǔ diǎn} is 5 p.m., and {下班|xià bān} is to finish work ({上班|shàng bān} would be to start).

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.
choices: {我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{十一点|shí yī diǎn}{睡觉|shuì jiào}。
{我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{七点|qī diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}。
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{几点|jǐ diǎn}{睡觉|shuì jiào}？ asks what time you go to bed: answer with the time before {睡觉|shuì jiào}. The second reply answers "What time do you get up?".

questions.stem: Listen. When are these two people most likely talking?
questions.explanation: {早|zǎo}！ is the morning greeting, "Morning!", and {你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{早|zǎo}！ is "You're early!".

questions.stem: Read the note: "6:30 {起床|qǐ chuáng}　7:00 {吃|chī}{早饭|zǎo fàn}　7:30 {上班|shàng bān}　12:00 {吃|chī}{午饭|wǔ fàn}　4:30 {下班|xià bān}". What does the writer do at 7:30?
questions.explanation: 7:30 is {上班|shàng bān}, to start work. Breakfast ({吃|chī}{早饭|zǎo fàn}) is at 7:00, getting up ({起床|qǐ chuáng}) at 6:30 and finishing work ({下班|xià bān}) at 4:30.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{七点|qī diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}，{八点|bā diǎn}{上班|shàng bān}，{下午|xià wǔ}{五点|wǔ diǎn}{下班|xià bān}。" How long is the writer's working day?
questions.explanation: From 8 a.m. ({八点|bā diǎn}{上班|shàng bān}) to 5 p.m. ({下午|xià wǔ}{五点|wǔ diǎn}{下班|xià bān}) is nine hours, {九个小时|jiǔ gè xiǎo shí}. Getting up at seven isn't part of the working day.

questions.stem: Type the word for "breakfast" (pinyin with tone numbers or characters): ___
questions.explanation: Breakfast is {早饭|zǎo fàn}, "early meal": a third tone, then a fourth (type zao3 fan4). Lunch is {午饭|wǔ fàn} and dinner {晚饭|wǎn fàn}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I get up at six in the morning.
questions.explanation: Time before the verb, big to small: {早上|zǎo shang}{六点|liù diǎn}. The subject can come first ({我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{六点|liù diǎn}{起床|qǐ chuáng}) or after the time phrase or part of it.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {饭|fàn} is a meal: {早|zǎo} (early) + {饭|fàn} is breakfast, {午|wǔ} (noon) + {饭|fàn} lunch, {晚|wǎn} (late) + {饭|fàn} dinner. {晚上|wǎn shang} is the evening; noon is {中午|zhōng wǔ} and early morning {早上|zǎo shang}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {起床|qǐ chuáng}, to get up: a low 3rd tone, then a rising 2nd.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {晚上|wǎn shang}, evening: a 3rd tone, then the neutral tone. {上|shàng} loses its tone in this word.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {早饭|zǎo fàn}, breakfast: a low 3rd tone, then a falling 4th.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm going to the shop to buy some things."? ({商店|shāng diàn}: shop)
questions.explanation: In a serial verb sentence the actions come in the order they happen: first go to the shop ({去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}), then buy things ({买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}). The place follows {去|qù} directly; it can't come at the end or before {去|qù}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I don't want to go."?
questions.explanation: "Don't want to" is {不想|bù xiǎng} before the verb. {不要|bú yào} + verb usually means "don't (do it)!", so {我|wǒ}{不要|bú yào}{去|qù} sounds like a refusal. {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{不|bú}{去|qù} is "I'm thinking of not going", a different idea.

questions.stem: You're at home, on the phone to a friend. How do you ask "Are you coming to my place?"
questions.explanation: You're at home, so your friend would come towards you: {来|lái}. {去|qù} is movement away from the speaker, {回|huí} is going back to where someone belongs, and {在|zài} asks whether they are at your place now.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: "{你|nǐ}{去|qù}___？" (Where are you going?)
questions.explanation: {哪儿|nǎr} (where) goes where the place would be: {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}？ — {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}。 {那儿|nàr} with a fourth tone means "there". {什么|shén me} asks "what" and {几|jǐ} "how many", not about places.

questions.stem: Which sentence sounds the most decided: "I'm going to China (I've made up my mind)."?
questions.explanation: {要|yào} + verb is a decision or a plan: {我|wǒ}{要|yào}{去|qù}{中国|Zhōng guó}. {想|xiǎng} + verb is a wish, "I'd like to go". Both go before the verb, so {去|qù}{要|yào} is the wrong order.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm not going shopping today."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bú}{去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}。
{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}{不|bù}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}。
{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}。
{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}。
questions.explanation: Time words and {不|bù} go before the first verb, because they cover the whole chain: {今天|jīn tiān}{不|bú}{去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}. With {不|bù} before {买|mǎi} the sentence says "I'm going to the shop today but not buying anything"; {今天|jīn tiān} can't follow the place, and {不|bù} can't go before the subject.

questions.stem: Which character completes the sentence {我|wǒ} __ {学校|xué xiào}。 (wǒ qù xué xiào, I'm going to school)?
questions.explanation: 去 (qù, go): 土 on top of 厶. 至 (to, as on signs) has 土 at the bottom instead, 法 (method) is 去 with 氵 on the left, and 公 (as in {公司|gōng sī}) has 八 over 厶.

questions.stem: Which character means "to look, watch, read"?
questions.explanation: 看 (kàn) is a hand 手 held over an eye 目. 省 has 目 too, under 少, 者 has no eye, and 手 alone is "hand".

questions.stem: Match each verb to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {去|qù} is to go (away from here), {来|lái} to come (towards here), {回|huí} to go back and {买|mǎi} to buy. To sell is {卖|mài} and to look {看|kàn}.

questions.stem: Listen. Where is the speaker going, and why?
choices: to school, to see the teacher
to the shop, to buy things
to a friend's place, for a meal
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}: first the place ({商店|shāng diàn}, shop), then what for ({买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}, buy things).

questions.stem: Listen. What would the speaker like to do on Saturday?

audio.text: 星期六我想回家看妈妈。

questions.explanation: {星期六|xīng qī liù}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{回|huí}{家|jiā}{看|kàn}{妈妈|mā ma}: on Saturday I'd like to go home ({回|huí}{家|jiā}) and see Mum ({看|kàn}{妈妈|mā ma}). If Mum were coming, the verb would be {来|lái} with Mum as the subject.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.
questions.explanation: {有事|yǒu shì} is "to have something on", so the question is "Are you busy tomorrow?". Answer with {有|yǒu} or {没有|méi yǒu}. {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{东西|dōng xi} means "I have stuff", objects, not plans.

questions.stem: Listen. True or false: the speaker wants to go to school.

audio.text: 我不想去学校，我想回家。

questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{不想|bù xiǎng}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{回|huí}{家|jiā}: I don't want to go to school, I want to go home.

questions.stem: Read the note: "{妈妈|mā ma}：{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}{看|kàn}{王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}，{五点|wǔ diǎn}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。{小明|Xiǎo míng}" Why has Xiaoming gone out?
choices: to see Teacher Wang at school
questions.explanation: {去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}{看|kàn}{王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}: to go to school to see Teacher Wang. The second part says Xiaoming will be home at five ({五点|wǔ diǎn}{回|huí}{家|jiā}).

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{星期六|xīng qī liù}{要|yào}{上班|shàng bān}，{星期天|xīng qī tiān}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}。" What would the writer like to do on Sunday?
questions.explanation: {星期天|xīng qī tiān}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}: on Sunday, go to the shop to buy things. Work ({上班|shàng bān}) is on Saturday.

questions.stem: Type the word for "to come" (pinyin with tone numbers or characters): ___
questions.explanation: To come is {来|lái}, a second tone (type lai2). To go is {去|qù} and to go back {回|huí}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: He goes home for lunch at noon.
questions.explanation: Time before the verbs, then the actions in order: go home ({回家|huí jiā}), then eat lunch ({吃|chī}{午饭|wǔ fàn}): {他|tā}{中午|zhōng wǔ}{回家|huí jiā}{吃|chī}{午饭|wǔ fàn}。

questions.stem: Build the question in Chinese.
questions.prompt: What would you like to do on Saturday?
questions.explanation: {想|xiǎng} goes before the verb, and the question word {什么|shén me} stays where the answer goes, after {做|zuò}. A question with {什么|shén me} takes no {吗|ma}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {买|mǎi}, to buy: the 3rd tone, low and dipping. {卖|mài} (to sell, lesson 13) is the 4th.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {来|lái}, to come: the 2nd tone, rising.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {回家|huí jiā}, to go home: a rising 2nd tone, then a high level 1st.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "He's sleeping."?
questions.explanation: The progressive {在|zài} goes straight before the verb: {他|tā}{在|zài}{睡觉|shuì jiào}. It can't follow the verb, {是|shì} doesn't make a progressive, and the last one is a question ("Is he sleeping?").

questions.stem: Which is the negative of "{他|tā}{在|zài}{工作|gōng zuò}。" (He's working.)?
questions.explanation: The progressive is negated with {没|méi} before {在|zài}: {他|tā}{没在|méi zài}{工作|gōng zuò}. {不在|bú zài} means "isn't here", and the negative word can't come between {在|zài} and the verb.

questions.stem: What does {在|zài} do in "{她|tā}{在|zài}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。"?
choices: It shows the action is going on: "is (doing)".
questions.explanation: Here {在|zài} is followed by a verb phrase, {打电话|dǎ diàn huà}, so it's the progressive: "She's on the phone." Followed by a place ({在|zài}{家|jiā}) it means "at" or "be at". "Again" is a different word, {再|zài} (lesson 23), with the same sound.

questions.stem: How do people usually read room number 101 aloud?
questions.explanation: Room and phone numbers are read digit by digit, and 1 is said yāo, so it can't be mistaken for qī (7): yāo líng yāo. Both 1s change, and the number isn't read as "one hundred and one".

questions.stem: Your phone rings. What do you usually say first?
questions.explanation: {喂|wéi}？ (or {喂|wéi}，{你好|nǐ hǎo}！) answers the phone. {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{谁|shéi}？ as the first words would be blunt, {我|wǒ}{找|zhǎo}… is what the caller says, and {再见|zài jiàn} ends the call.

questions.stem: On the phone, how do you say "I'd like to speak to Teacher Wang."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{知道|zhī dào}{王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}。
questions.explanation: {找|zhǎo} + person, "I'm looking for", is how you ask for someone on the phone or at a door. {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{王老师|Wáng lǎo shī} says you are Teacher Wang, and the last one reverses who is looking for whom.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: "{你|nǐ}{的|de}{手机号|shǒu jī hào}{是|shì}___？" (What's your mobile number?)
questions.explanation: A phone number is a long number, so ask with {多少|duō shao}. {几|jǐ} only asks about small numbers (usually under ten), {谁|shéi} is "who" and {哪儿|nǎr} "where".

questions.stem: When people answer the phone, how is 喂 usually said?
questions.explanation: On the phone almost everyone says {喂|wéi} with a rising, questioning tone. The dictionary tone is wèi, falling, which sounds like a sharp "Hey!".

questions.stem: Which character completes the word __电话 (dǎ diàn huà, to make a phone call)?
questions.explanation: 打电话 starts with 打 (dǎ, strike): 扌 + 丁. 找 (look for) has 戈 on the right, 扣 has 口, and 订 has the speech radical 讠.

questions.stem: Which character means "who"?
questions.explanation: 谁 (shéi) is 讠 + 隹. 话 (words) and 说 (speak) share its radical 讠, and 推 (push) has the same right side, 隹, with 扌 (hand) instead.

questions.stem: Listen. What is Li Ming doing?
questions.explanation: {李明|Lǐ Míng}{在|zài}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}{呢|ne}: {在|zài} … {呢|ne} around {打电话|dǎ diàn huà}, "is on the phone".

questions.stem: Listen. Who does the caller want to speak to?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{找|zhǎo}{王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}: "I'm looking for Teacher Wang", the way you ask for someone on the phone.

questions.stem: Listen and choose the best reply.
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{做|zuò}{什么|shén me}{呢|ne}？ asks what you're doing right now, so answer with {在|zài} + an activity: "I'm listening to the teacher." {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng} answers who you are.

questions.stem: Listen. True or false: he's sleeping.
questions.explanation: {他|tā}{没在|méi zài}{睡觉|shuì jiào}，{他|tā}{在|zài}{工作|gōng zuò}: he isn't sleeping, he's working. {没在|méi zài} is the negative of the progressive.

questions.stem: Read the name card: "{陈刚|Chén Gāng}　{大学|dà xué}{老师|lǎo shī}　{手机|shǒu jī}：126 1011 0101". How are the first three digits of the mobile number read?
questions.explanation: Phone numbers are read digit by digit, with 1 said yāo: 126 is yāo èr liù. Reading it as a number (one hundred and eighty-six) is wrong for phone numbers, and liù keeps its fourth tone.

questions.stem: Read: "{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{在|zài}{找|zhǎo}{她|tā}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}。{她|tā}{不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{手机|shǒu jī}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}。" What's the problem?
choices: Wang Fang doesn't know where her phone is.
Wang Fang doesn't know who called her.
Wang Fang doesn't know her own number.
questions.explanation: {在|zài}{找|zhǎo}{她|tā}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}: she's looking for her phone, and {不|bù}{知道|zhī dào}{手机|shǒu jī}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}: she doesn't know where it is.

questions.stem: Build the question in Chinese.
questions.prompt: What is he doing right now?
questions.explanation: {正在|zhèng zài} goes before the verb, the question word {什么|shén me} after {做|zuò}, and {呢|ne} at the end: {他|tā}{正在|zhèng zài}{做|zuò}{什么|shén me}{呢|ne}？ {吗|ma} isn't used with a question word.

questions.stem: Type the word for "to know (a fact)" (pinyin with tone numbers or characters): ___
questions.explanation: {知道|zhī dào}: a first tone, then a fourth (type zhi1 dao4). In speech the second syllable is often light. Knowing a person is {认识|rèn shi}, lesson 23.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {手机|shǒu jī}, mobile phone: a low 3rd tone, then a high level 1st.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the three syllables?
questions.explanation: {打电话|dǎ diàn huà}, to make a phone call: a 3rd tone, then two falling 4th tones.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {听|tīng}, to listen: the 1st tone, high and level.

questions.stem: What is {公历|gōng lì}?
choices: the Gregorian calendar, used for everyday dates
a calendar of the twelve animals
a list of the twenty-four solar terms
questions.explanation: {公历|gōng lì}, the "public calendar", is the Gregorian calendar of work, school and phones. The traditional one is {农历|nóng lì}, which sets the festival dates.

questions.stem: Why does the Spring Festival fall on a different Gregorian date every year?
choices: A new date is chosen every year.
It's always the first Monday in February.
It's the first day of the traditional calendar, whose months follow the moon.
questions.explanation: {春节|Chūn jié} is {正月初一|zhēng yuè chū yī}, the first day of the first month of {农历|nóng lì}. Its months follow the moon, so the day moves, always landing between 21 January and 20 February.

questions.stem: Which traditional date is the Mid-Autumn Festival?
questions.explanation: {中秋节|Zhōng qiū jié} is the fifteenth day of the eighth month, at the full moon. {正月初一|zhēng yuè chū yī} is the Spring Festival, {正月十五|zhēng yuè shí wǔ} the Lantern Festival and {五月初五|wǔ yuè chū wǔ} the Dragon Boat Festival.

questions.stem: Someone was born on 10 January 1998. The 1998 Spring Festival was on 28 January. Which year's animal do they have?
choices: the animal of the year after
the animal of the year before
questions.explanation: The animal year changes at the Spring Festival, not on 1 January. 10 January 1998 is still in the old year, so it's the animal of 1997.

questions.stem: Which animal comes right after the horse, {马|mǎ}?
questions.explanation: The order is rat, ox, tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, goat, monkey, rooster, dog, pig. After {马|mǎ} comes {羊|yáng}, then {猴|hóu}; {蛇|shé} comes before the horse.

questions.stem: How do you ask someone "What's your zodiac animal?"
questions.explanation: The verb is {属|shǔ}, "to belong to (a sign)": {你|nǐ}{属|shǔ}{什么|shén me}？ — {我|wǒ}{属|shǔ}{马|mǎ}。 {你|nǐ}{几|jǐ}{岁|suì}？ asks a child's age directly.

questions.stem: Read the sign: "{周一|zhōu yī}{至|zhì}{周五|zhōu wǔ}　9:00—17:00". When is it open? ({至|zhì}: to)
questions.explanation: {周|zhōu} is the written word for "week" on signs: {周一|zhōu yī} is Monday and {周五|zhōu wǔ} Friday, numbered like {星期一|xīng qī yī} and {星期五|xīng qī wǔ}. 17:00 is 5 p.m.

questions.stem: Read the form: "{出生日期|chū shēng rì qī}：2001{年|nián}3{月|yuè}8{日|rì}". What is the date of birth?
questions.explanation: Big to small: 2001 is the year, 3{月|yuè} March, 8{日|rì} the 8th. {出生日期|chū shēng rì qī} means "date of birth".

questions.stem: Which way of writing 20 May 1998 is standard on a Chinese form?
questions.explanation: Dates run year, month, day, like 1998{年|nián}5{月|yuè}20{日|rì}; the hyphen form keeps the same order. Day-first and month-first forms copy European and American habits and would confuse a reader.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true?
choices: The speaker is a tiger and the mother a horse.
The speaker is a horse and the mother a tiger.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{属|shǔ}{马|mǎ}，{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{属|shǔ}{虎|hǔ}: I was born in a horse year, my mum in a tiger year.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?
choices: The Spring Festival is on the fifteenth day of the first month.
The Spring Festival is on the first day of the first month.
The Lantern Festival is on the first day of the first month.
The Spring Festival is on 1 January.
questions.explanation: {春节|Chūn jié}{是|shì}{正月初一|zhēng yuè chū yī}: {正月|zhēng yuè} is the first month of the traditional calendar and {初一|chū yī} its first day. That's not 1 January ({一月|yī yuè}{一号|yī hào}).

questions.stem: Which word for "week" belongs to informal speech, especially in the south?
questions.explanation: {礼拜|lǐ bài}, originally "worship", is the informal one: {礼拜天|lǐ bài tiān}. {星期|xīng qī} is the standard word and {周|zhōu} the short written one; {月|yuè} is a month.

questions.stem: On the mainland, what does an L-shaped hand (thumb and index finger stretched out) usually mean?
questions.explanation: The L-shape is the usual mainland sign for 8. In parts of the south and among some Chinese speakers elsewhere in Asia it can mean 7, so say the number too when it matters.

questions.stem: Which gesture usually means 6?
choices: the index finger bent into a hook
the thumb, index and middle fingertips pinched together
the thumb and little finger stretched out
questions.explanation: Six is the thumb and the little finger. The hook is 9, the pinched fingertips 7, and the fist 10.

questions.stem: Why do many people like the number 8?
choices: {八|bā} sounds like the fā of {发财|fā cái} (to become rich).
questions.explanation: {八|bā} sounds like the fā of {发财|fā cái}, "to get rich". {九|jiǔ} is the one that sounds like {久|jiǔ}, and {六|liù} the one like {流|liú}.

questions.stem: Why do some buildings skip the 4th floor?
choices: {四|sì} sounds like the fā of {发财|fā cái} (to get rich).
questions.explanation: {四|sì} and {死|sǐ} differ only in tone, so some people avoid fours in floors, phone numbers and addresses. It's a custom some keep, not a rule.

questions.stem: How is the police number 110 said?
questions.explanation: Phone numbers, short ones included, are read digit by digit with 1 said yāo: yāo yāo líng. Fire is 119 (yāo yāo jiǔ) and ambulance 120 (yāo èr líng).

questions.stem: How is the price 120{元|yuán} said?
choices: {一百二十块|yì bǎi èr shí kuài}
{一百两十块|yì bǎi liǎng shí kuài}
questions.explanation: A price is an amount, so it's read as a number, with {块|kuài} in speech: {一百二十块|yì bǎi èr shí kuài}. Digit by digit (yāo èr líng) is for phone numbers, and twenty is always {二十|èr shí}.

questions.stem: Read the address: "{花园路|Huā yuán Lù} 6{号|hào}，2{号楼|hào lóu}，301". Which floor is flat 301 most likely on?
questions.explanation: Flat numbers often start with the floor: 301 is flat 01 on the 3rd floor. 2{号楼|hào lóu} is Building 2, and 6{号|hào} is the number on Garden Road.

questions.stem: Read the name card: "{手机|shǒu jī}：128 0123 4567". How is the first group read?
questions.explanation: A mobile number is read in groups (3 + 4 + 4), digit by digit, with 1 as yāo: yāo èr bā.

questions.stem: In mainland China, which floor is {一楼|yī lóu}?
questions.explanation: Floors are counted the American way: {一楼|yī lóu} is at street level (the British ground floor), and {二楼|èr lóu} is the one above.

questions.stem: Listen. How much is it?
questions.explanation: {八块|bā kuài}: eight kuai, the spoken word for eight yuan. Eighteen would be {十八块|shí bā kuài} and eighty {八十块|bā shí kuài}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which floor is the speaker's home on?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{在|zài}{五楼|wǔ lóu}: my home is on the fifth floor. Fifteen would be {十五|shí wǔ} and fifty {五十|wǔ shí}.

questions.stem: In online slang, what does 520 stand for?
questions.explanation: Read wǔ èr líng, 520 sounds a little like {我爱你|wǒ ài nǐ}, so people text it for "I love you", and 20 May has become an unofficial day for couples.

questions.stem: Choose the verb: {我|wǒ} ___ {水|shuǐ}。 (I drink water.)
questions.explanation: Drinks take {喝|hē}: {喝|hē}{水|shuǐ}, {喝|hē}{茶|chá}. {吃|chī} is for food, {是|shì} links two nouns ("I am water"), and {有|yǒu} means "have".

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I eat steamed buns in the morning."?
questions.explanation: A time word goes before the verb, after or before the subject: {我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{吃|chī}{包子|bāo zi} (or {早上|zǎo shang}{我|wǒ}{吃|chī}{包子|bāo zi}). Putting {早上|zǎo shang} at the end copies English word order, and the object {包子|bāo zi} always follows the verb.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "He doesn't like (drinking) tea."?
questions.explanation: Liking is a state, so it is negated with {不|bù} right before {喜欢|xǐ huan}. {没|méi} doesn't go with {喜欢|xǐ huan}; {喜欢|xǐ huan}{不|bù}{喝|hē} would mean "likes not drinking"; and {是|shì} isn't needed before a verb.

questions.stem: You'd like some tea. What do you say?
questions.explanation: {想|xiǎng} (would like to) is followed by a verb: {想|xiǎng}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}. Without the verb, {想|xiǎng} + a noun usually means "to miss": {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{茶|chá} sounds like "I miss tea". {是|shì} doesn't go before a verb, and {想|xiǎng} comes before {喝|hē}, not after it.

questions.stem: A friend asks: "{你|nǐ}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{吗|ma}？" What does it mean?
choices: Do you eat rice at home?
questions.explanation: {吃|chī}{饭|fàn} is "to eat, to have a meal", whatever the food is. The rice itself is {米饭|mǐ fàn}; cooking is {做|zuò}{饭|fàn} (lesson 12). {在|zài}{家|jiā} before the verb says where.

questions.stem: What does "{妈妈|mā ma}{去|qù}{买|mǎi}{菜|cài}。" mean?
choices: Mum is going to buy food for meals.
Mum is going to buy tea.
questions.explanation: {菜|cài} is both "dish" and "vegetable", and {买|mǎi}{菜|cài} is the everyday phrase for doing the food shopping. Cooking would be {做|zuò}{饭|fàn}, liking {喜欢|xǐ huan}, and tea {茶|chá}.

questions.stem: What is the pinyin of 茶 (tea)?
questions.explanation: 茶 is chá, second tone (rising). Compare 菜 cài (dish), which falls: {喝|hē}{茶|chá} and {吃|chī}{菜|cài}.

questions.stem: Which pinyin is right for 喜欢 (to like)?
questions.explanation: 喜欢 is xǐ huan: a third tone, then a light neutral syllable. In {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan} the two third tones in a row make 我 rise (said wó xǐhuan), but it is still written wǒ.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word {喝|hē} ___ (hē chá, to drink tea)?
questions.explanation: Tea is 茶: 艹 on top, then 人, then a shape like 木 with a hooked middle stroke. 荼 (a rare character, tú) has an extra stroke under 人; 菜 (dish) has 爫 and 木 under 艹; 苦 (bitter, later) has 古.

questions.stem: Which two characters share the radical 艹 ("grass on top")?
questions.explanation: 茶 (tea) and 菜 (vegetable, dish) both start with 艹, a radical for plants. 吃 and 喝 share 口 (mouth); 米, 面, 喜 and 欢 have different radicals.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the speaker say?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{饺子|jiǎo zi}: a general liking with {喜欢|xǐ huan}. "I'd like to eat" would be {想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}, buns are {包子|bāo zi}, and the negative would have {不|bù}.

questions.stem: Listen. What would the speaker like?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{喝|hē}{水|shuǐ}: I'd like some water. Tea would be {茶|chá}, rice {米饭|mǐ fàn} and noodles {面条儿|miàn tiáor}, and those last two would go with {吃|chī}.

questions.stem: Listen. Where does the speaker eat at noon?
questions.explanation: You heard {中午|zhōng wǔ}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}: at noon I eat rice at school. The place after {在|zài} comes before the verb. At home would be {在|zài}{家|jiā}, at work (at the company) {在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}.

questions.stem: Listen to the question. Which is the best reply?
questions.explanation: The question was {你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{面条儿|miàn tiáor}{吗|ma}？ (Do you like noodles?). Chinese answers a yes/no question by repeating the verb: {喜欢|xǐ huan} (or {不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}). {是|shì} answers a question with {是|shì}, {有|yǒu} one with {有|yǒu}.

questions.stem: Read: "{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{早上|zǎo shang}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}，{不|bù}{喝|hē}{水|shuǐ}。{中午|zhōng wǔ}{她|tā}{吃|chī}{面条儿|miàn tiáor}。{晚上|wǎn shang}{她|tā}{和|hé}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}。" When does Wang Fang eat noodles?
questions.explanation: {中午|zhōng wǔ}{她|tā}{吃|chī}{面条儿|miàn tiáor}: at noon she eats noodles. In the morning ({早上|zǎo shang}) she drinks tea, and in the evening ({晚上|wǎn shang}) she eats at home with her mother.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}。{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{不|bù}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}，{她|tā}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{水|shuǐ}。{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{水|shuǐ}。" Who likes drinking water?
questions.explanation: Mum likes water ({她|tā}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{水|shuǐ}), and {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{水|shuǐ} adds the writer: {也|yě} means "too". Dad likes tea.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I like eating Chinese food.
questions.explanation: Subject, then {喜欢|xǐ huan}, then the action and its object: {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{中国|Zhōng guó}{菜|cài}. No {是|shì}: {喜欢|xǐ huan} is the verb.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: At noon I eat rice at school.
questions.explanation: Time, then place, then the verb: {中午|zhōng wǔ}{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}. The time word may also come after the subject ({我|wǒ}{中午|zhōng wǔ}…), but {在|zài}{学校|xué xiào} always comes before {吃|chī}.

questions.stem: Type the Chinese for "to drink", in pinyin with its tone or in characters: ___
questions.explanation: "To drink" is 喝 hē, first tone (type he1). It goes with every drink: {喝|hē}{水|shuǐ}, {喝|hē}{茶|chá}.

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: 吃 eat and 喝 drink both have 口 (mouth) on the left; 茶 tea and 菜 dish share 艹 on top; 水 is water. Rice (the grain) is 米.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {菜|cài}, dish or vegetable: the fourth tone, falling. Compare {茶|chá} (tea), which rises.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {米饭|mǐ fàn}, cooked rice: tones 3+4. Before a fourth tone the third tone stays low (a "half third").

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Please have some tea."?
questions.explanation: {请|qǐng} goes in front of the verb: {请|qǐng}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}. It is never added at the end like English "please", and it doesn't go between the verb and its object.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Let's go to a restaurant."?
questions.explanation: {吧|ba} at the end of the sentence makes a suggestion: {我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{饭店|fàn diàn}{吧|ba}. With {吗|ma} it's a real question ("Are we going to a restaurant?"), {呢|ne} asks "and…?", and {吧|ba} never goes after the subject.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'd like a little water."?
questions.explanation: {一点儿|yì diǎnr} goes after the verb and before the noun: {喝|hē}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{水|shuǐ}. Putting it before the verb or at the end of the sentence follows English word order.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "The dumplings are so good!"?
questions.explanation: The frame is {太|tài} + adjective + {了|le}: {太|tài}{好吃|hǎo chī}{了|le}. {太|tài} comes before the adjective, no {是|shì} is needed before an adjective, and {不|bú}{太|tài}{好吃|hǎo chī} means "not very tasty".

questions.stem: What does "{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{太|tài}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}。" mean?
choices: I don't drink tea any more.
questions.explanation: {不|bú}{太|tài} + verb or adjective is "not very, not really": a soft way to say you don't like something. Note {不|bú} rises before the fourth tone of {太|tài}, and there is no {了|le} in the negative.

questions.stem: The waiter says "{请|qǐng}{等|děng}{一下|yí xià}。" ({等|děng} = to wait). What does it mean?
questions.explanation: Verb + {一下|yí xià} is "(do it) briefly", a softener: {等|děng}{一下|yí xià} is "wait a moment". Sit down would be {请|qǐng}{坐|zuò}.

questions.stem: At the end of dinner your friend says: "{今天|jīn tiān}{我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ}！" What does your friend mean?
choices: Today I'm asking you a question.
Today I'm inviting you to my home.
questions.explanation: {请|qǐng} + a person is "to invite, to treat": {我|wǒ}{请|qǐng}{你|nǐ} at the end of a meal means "I'm paying". A good reply is {谢谢|xiè xie}！ or {太|tài}{好|hǎo}{了|le}！

questions.stem: How is 一 pronounced in 一下 (yí xià, a moment)?
questions.explanation: 一 changes before the next syllable: before a 4th tone such as 下 xià it rises, yí. Before tones 1, 2 and 3 it falls (一点儿 yì diǎnr); it stays yī when counting.

questions.stem: Which pinyin is right for 先生 (Mr, sir)?
questions.explanation: 先生 is xiān sheng: a first tone, then a light neutral syllable, as in {学生|xué sheng}. In {医生|yī shēng} and {大学生|dà xué shēng}, 生 keeps its first tone.

questions.stem: Which character completes {女|nǚ} ___ (nǚ shì, Ms)?
questions.explanation: 女士 is written with 士, whose top horizontal is the long one. In 土 (earth, as in 在) the bottom horizontal is longer; 王 (king, a common surname) has three horizontals; 工 is "work".

questions.stem: Which character means "too, extremely" (tài)?
questions.explanation: 太 is 大 (big) with a dot inside at the bottom. 大 is big, 天 (day, sky) has a horizontal on top, and 犬 (dog, a character of later levels) has its dot at the top right.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker suggest?
questions.explanation: You heard {我们|wǒ men}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{吧|ba}: "Let's eat." {吧|ba} at the end makes it a suggestion. Cooking would be {做饭|zuò fàn}, going home {回|huí}{家|jiā}, tea {喝|hē}{茶|chá}.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker want?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{喝|hē}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{水|shuǐ}: "I'd like a little water." {一点儿|yì diǎnr} (a little) comes after the verb; tea would be {茶|chá}.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?
questions.explanation: You heard {请|qǐng}{您|nín}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}: "Please have some tea", said politely to a guest ({您|nín}). Asking for tea yourself would be {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}, and praising it {茶|chá}{很|hěn}{好喝|hǎo hē}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the best reply?
questions.explanation: You heard {谢谢|xiè xie}{你|nǐ}！ (Thank you!). The answer to thanks is {不客气|bú kè qi} (you're welcome). {没关系|méi guān xi} answers an apology ({对不起|duì bu qǐ}), and {再见|zài jiàn} is goodbye.

questions.stem: Read: "A：{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{饭店|fàn diàn}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{吧|ba}。B：{好|hǎo}。{你|nǐ}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{什么|shén me}？A：{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{面条儿|miàn tiáor}。B：{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{太|tài}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{面条儿|miàn tiáor}，{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{包子|bāo zi}。" What does B want to eat?
questions.explanation: B says {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{吃|chī}{包子|bāo zi}: steamed buns. A wants noodles, which B doesn't really like ({不|bú}{太|tài}{喜欢|xǐ huan}). Dumplings are {饺子|jiǎo zi}, bread {面包|miàn bāo}.

questions.stem: Read the note: "{妈妈|mā ma}：{今天|jīn tiān}{晚上|wǎn shang}{我|wǒ}{和|hé}{大卫|Dà wèi}{在|zài}{饭店|fàn diàn}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}，{九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。——{小明|Xiǎo Míng}" What is Xiao Ming telling his mother?
choices: He's eating out tonight and will be home at nine.
David is coming home for dinner at nine.
He'll eat at home with David tonight.
questions.explanation: {在|zài}{饭店|fàn diàn}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn} is "eat at a restaurant", and {九|jiǔ}{点|diǎn}{回|huí}{家|jiā} "get home at nine". He's with David ({和|hé}{大卫|Dà wèi}), but not at home, and nobody is cooking ({做饭|zuò fàn}).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Let's have dumplings.
questions.explanation: Subject, verb, object, then {吧|ba} to make the suggestion: {我们|wǒ men}{吃|chī}{饺子|jiǎo zi}{吧|ba}. With {吗|ma} it would be a question.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I can speak a little Chinese.
questions.explanation: {会|huì} (can, a learned skill) goes before the verb, and {一点儿|yì diǎnr} between the verb and its object: {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}.

questions.stem: Type the Chinese for "please" (as in "please have some tea"), in pinyin with its tone or in characters: ___
questions.explanation: "Please" is 请 qǐng, third tone (type qing3), and it goes before the verb: {请|qǐng}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {请|qǐng}, please: the third tone, low and dipping.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {杯子|bēi zi}, cup: a first tone, then the neutral tone ({子|zi} is light, as in {包子|bāo zi}).

questions.stem: Choose the measure word: {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{两|liǎng} ___ {书|shū}。 (I'm buying two books.)
questions.explanation: Books are counted with {本|běn}: {两|liǎng}{本|běn}{书|shū}. {件|jiàn} is for clothes and matters, {块|kuài} for pieces and money, and {个|gè} is the general measure word, not used for books.

questions.stem: How do you say "2 kuai"?
questions.explanation: Before a measure word, two is {两|liǎng}: {两|liǎng}{块|kuài}. {块|kuài} is itself the measure word, so no {个|gè} goes in, and {钱|qián} (money) isn't counted with {个|gè}.

questions.stem: A price tag says 20.50{元|yuán}. How do you say the price?
questions.explanation: Twenty yuan is {二十|èr shí}{块|kuài}, and a number after {块|kuài} gives the tenths (the word {毛|máo} is left off): {二十|èr shí}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ}. {两|liǎng} isn't used inside the number twenty, and {二十五|èr shí wǔ}{块|kuài} would be 25 yuan.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: An adjective follows the subject directly, usually with {很|hěn} before it: {书|shū}{很|hěn}{贵|guì} (books are expensive). {是|shì} doesn't go before an adjective, and {很|hěn} comes right before the adjective, not after it or before the noun.

questions.stem: How do you ask "How much is the bread?"
questions.explanation: The thing comes first and {多少|duō shao}{钱|qián} after it: {面包|miàn bāo}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？ The answer takes the same place: {面包|miàn bāo}{五|wǔ}{块|kuài}.

questions.stem: What does "{他|tā}{卖|mài}{书|shū}。" mean?
questions.explanation: {卖|mài}, fourth tone, is "to sell"; {买|mǎi}, third tone, is "to buy". {=In characters, 卖 has an extra 十 on top of 买.=}

questions.stem: What is the pinyin of 卖 (to sell)?
questions.explanation: 卖 is mài, falling (4th) tone. 买 (to buy) is mǎi, third tone: the same syllable, a different tone.

questions.stem: How is 便 read in 便宜 (cheap)?
questions.explanation: In 便宜 piányi, 便 is pián (2nd tone) and 宜 is light. 便 is read biàn in other words, such as {方便|fāng biàn} (convenient, HSK 3).

questions.stem: Which character completes ___ {店|diàn} (shūdiàn, bookshop)?
questions.explanation: {=Book is 书: four strokes, with the dot at the top right written last. 节 (festival) has 艹 on top, 韦 and 丰 are other characters with crossing strokes, not used in this course.=} (The simplified forms are shown; traditional 书 is 書.)

questions.stem: Which character means "money" (qián)?
questions.explanation: {=钱 has 钅 (metal) on the left: coins were metal. 线 (thread) has 纟 (silk), 浅 (shallow) has 氵 (water) and 践 (to tread) has 足 (foot), all with the same right side.=} (Simplified forms; traditional 钱 is 錢, with 金.)

questions.stem: {=Why do 贵 (expensive) and the traditional forms 買 (buy) and 賣 (sell) contain 贝 / 貝, "shell"?=}
choices: Shellfish were the most expensive food.
Shops were built by the sea.
The shell part gives the sound.
Cowrie shells were once used as money.
questions.explanation: In ancient China cowrie shells served as money, so characters about value, buying and selling often contain 贝. Here it carries meaning, not sound: 贵 guì, 买 mǎi and 卖 mài sound nothing like 贝 bèi.

questions.stem: Listen. How much is the book?
questions.explanation: You heard {一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}{四十五|sì shí wǔ}{块|kuài}: forty-five. 54 would be {五十四|wǔ shí sì}, 4.50 {四|sì}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ}.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the price?
questions.explanation: You heard {面包|miàn bāo}{三|sān}{块|kuài}{五|wǔ}: three yuan fifty. The number after {块|kuài} is tenths of a yuan; 35 would be {三十五|sān shí wǔ}{块|kuài}.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker think of the price?
choices: It's a bit expensive but fine.
questions.explanation: You heard {太|tài}{贵|guì}{了|le}！: "That's too expensive!" Cheap would be {便宜|pián yi}, and {太|tài}…{了|le} is strong, not mild.

questions.stem: Listen. Where is the speaker most likely to be?
questions.explanation: You heard {你们|nǐ men}{卖|mài}{茶|chá}{吗|ma}？: "Do you sell tea?", a question for a shop. {卖|mài} (sell) falls; {买|mǎi} (buy) dips.

questions.stem: Read the price list: "{包子|bāo zi} 2{元|yuán}　{面包|miàn bāo} 4.50{元|yuán}　{茶|chá} 8{元|yuán}" You buy two steamed buns and one tea. How much do you pay?
questions.explanation: Two {包子|bāo zi} at 2{元|yuán} each are 4{元|yuán}, and the tea is 8{元|yuán}: 12{元|yuán}, said {十二|shí èr}{块|kuài}.

questions.stem: Read: "A：{一|yí}{个|gè}{面包|miàn bāo}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？B：{五|wǔ}{块|kuài}。A：{太|tài}{贵|guì}{了|le}！B：{不|bú}{贵|guì}，{很|hěn}{好吃|hǎo chī}。A：{好|hǎo}，{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}。" How much does A pay?
questions.explanation: One roll is {五|wǔ}{块|kuài}, and A buys {两|liǎng}{个|gè} (two, with the noun left out): ten kuai. A complains at first, but B says it's not expensive and tastes good.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I'll buy two books.
questions.explanation: Number + measure word + noun after the verb: {买|mǎi}{两|liǎng}{本|běn}{书|shū}. Two before a measure word is {两|liǎng}, not {二|èr}, and books take {本|běn}, not {个|gè}.

questions.stem: Type the Chinese for "money", in pinyin with its tone or in characters: ___
questions.explanation: Money is 钱 qián, second tone (type qian2). Don't confuse it with 千 qiān (thousand), first tone.

questions.stem: Match each measure word to something it counts.
questions.explanation: {一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}, {一|yí}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}, {一|yí}{个|gè}{包子|bāo zi}, {一|yí}{块|kuài}{钱|qián}. Water isn't counted with a measure word like these; you count cups or glasses of it.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {钱|qián}, money: the second tone, rising. {千|qiān} (thousand) is level.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {商店|shāng diàn}, shop: tones 1+4, high and level, then falling.

questions.stem: Complete: ___ {很|hěn}{贵|guì}。 (This book is expensive.)
questions.explanation: A demonstrative needs a measure word before the noun, and books take {本|běn}: {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}. {这|zhè}{书|shū} leaves the measure word out, {个|gè} is the wrong measure word for books, and the measure word comes after {这|zhè}.

questions.stem: Which means "these books"?
questions.explanation: {些|xiē} is itself the measure word, so it replaces {本|běn}: {这些|zhè xiē}{书|shū}. Two measure words in a row are wrong, and {些|xiē} follows {这|zhè}.

questions.stem: How do you say "the second day"?
questions.explanation: Ordinals are {第|dì} + the number: {第|dì}{二|èr}. "Second" uses {二|èr}, the name of the number, not {两|liǎng}, which counts things. {天|tiān} needs no measure word.

questions.stem: Which question means "Which one do you want?"
questions.explanation: {哪个|nǎ ge} (which one) is a question word: it sits where the answer will go and needs no {吗|ma}. {你|nǐ}{要|yào}{那个|nà ge}{吗|ma}？ asks "Do you want that one?" ({那|nà} falls; {哪|nǎ} dips).

questions.stem: Which means "these two books"?
questions.explanation: The order is demonstrative + number + measure word + noun: {这|zhè}{两|liǎng}{本|běn}{书|shū}. English puts "two" after "these" too, but the measure word must come right before the noun.

questions.stem: What does "{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{一些|yì xiē}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}。" mean?
choices: I'd like to buy some fruit.
I'd like to buy one piece of fruit.
I'd like to buy this fruit.
I'd like to buy all the fruit.
questions.explanation: {一些|yì xiē} is "some, a few". One piece would be {一|yí}{个|gè}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}, this fruit {这个|zhè ge}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}.

questions.stem: How is 一 pronounced in 第一 (first)?
questions.explanation: In ordinals, 一 keeps its first tone: dì yī. Before a measure word it changes: 一个 yí gè, 一些 yì xiē.

questions.stem: Which word is nǎge, "which one"?
questions.explanation: 哪个 nǎge (which one) has 口 on the left and a dipping tone. 那个 nàge (that one) falls, 这个 zhège is "this one" and 那些 nàxiē "those".

questions.stem: Which character completes {苹|píng} ___ (píngguǒ, apple)?
questions.explanation: {=Fruit is 果: a tree (木) with the fruit on top, a 日-like box crossed by a vertical. 里 (inside, lesson 16) has 土 at the bottom, 呆 (dull) has 口 on top, and 东 (east) is a different shape.=}

questions.stem: The lower part of 第 is a character you know, and it gives 第 its sound. Which one?
questions.explanation: 第 is ⺮ (bamboo) on top of 弟, from {弟弟|dì di} (younger brother): both are read dì. The bamboo part is the meaning side; 牛 and 市 are other characters of this lesson.

questions.stem: {牛奶|niú nǎi} is milk. What does 牛 mean on its own?
questions.explanation: 牛 is a cow or ox (it began as a drawing of an ox's head with horns), so {牛奶|niú nǎi} is cow's milk. Chicken is 鸡, as in {鸡蛋|jī dàn}.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the speaker say?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{要|yào}{这个|zhè ge}: "I'll have this one." That one is {那个|nà ge} (nà), which one {哪个|nǎ ge}, and these {这些|zhè xiē}.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the speaker say?
questions.explanation: You heard {这些|zhè xiē}{苹果|píng guǒ}{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}: these (more than one) apples are cheap. "Those" would be {那些|nà xiē}, one apple {这个|zhè ge}{苹果|píng guǒ}, expensive {贵|guì}.

questions.stem: Listen. What will the speaker buy?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{牛奶|niú nǎi}{和|hé}{鸡蛋|jī dàn}: milk and eggs. Apples are {苹果|píng guǒ}, bread {面包|miàn bāo}, tea {茶|chá}.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker telling you?
choices: Today is the first of the month.
questions.explanation: You heard {今天|jīn tiān}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{第|dì}{一|yī}{天|tiān}: "Today is my first day." Monday is {星期|xīng qī}{一|yī}, and the first of the month is {一|yī}{号|hào}.

questions.stem: Read the note: "{大卫|Dà wèi}：{你|nǐ}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{吧|ba}，{买|mǎi}{一些|yì xiē}{苹果|píng guǒ}{和|hé}{鸡蛋|jī dàn}。{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{牛奶|niú nǎi}。——{李明|Lǐ Míng}" What will Li Ming buy?
questions.explanation: Li Ming writes {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{牛奶|niú nǎi}: he will buy the milk. David is asked ({你|nǐ}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{吧|ba}) to buy apples and eggs.

questions.stem: Read: "A：{这些|zhè xiē}{苹果|píng guǒ}{多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}？B：{三|sān}{块|kuài}{一|yí}{个|gè}。A：{那些|nà xiē}{呢|ne}？B：{那些|nà xiē}{两|liǎng}{块|kuài}{一|yí}{个|gè}。A：{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{那些|nà xiē}{吧|ba}，{五|wǔ}{个|gè}。" How much does A pay?
questions.explanation: A buys five of "those" ({那些|nà xiē}) apples at {两|liǎng}{块|kuài}{一|yí}{个|gè}, two kuai each: ten kuai. 15 kuai would be five of "these", at three kuai.

questions.stem: Build the question in Chinese.
questions.prompt: How much is that book?
questions.explanation: Demonstrative + measure word + noun is the topic: {那|nà}{本|běn}{书|shū}; then {多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}. Books take {本|běn}, not {个|gè}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I'd like to buy some fruit.
questions.explanation: {想|xiǎng} before the verb, {一些|yì xiē} before the noun: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{一些|yì xiē}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {这|zhè} near, {那|nà} away, {哪|nǎ} the question; {个|gè} for one, {些|xiē} for more than one. "Which ones" would be {哪些|nǎ xiē}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {苹果|píng guǒ}, apple: tones 2+3, rising, then low.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {牛奶|niú nǎi}, milk: tones 2+3, like {苹果|píng guǒ}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "This piece of clothing is very pretty."?
questions.explanation: An adjective predicate needs no {是|shì}: subject + {很|hěn} + adjective. {是|shì}{漂亮|piào liang} is the typical English-speaker's mistake, {这|zhè}{衣服|yī fu} is missing the measure word {件|jiàn}, and {很|hěn} goes before the adjective.

questions.stem: Which question is correct?
questions.explanation: An A-not-A question is the word, {不|bu}, the word again: {贵|guì}{不|bu}{贵|guì}？ It is already a question, so it takes no {吗|ma}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "The dumplings are extremely tasty."?
choices: {饺子|jiǎo zi}{非常|fēi cháng}{好吃|hǎo chī}。
{饺子|jiǎo zi}{好吃|hǎo chī}{非常|fēi cháng}。
{非常|fēi cháng}{饺子|jiǎo zi}{好吃|hǎo chī}。
{饺子|jiǎo zi}{是|shì}{非常|fēi cháng}{好吃|hǎo chī}。
questions.explanation: A degree adverb such as {非常|fēi cháng} goes right before the adjective: {非常|fēi cháng}{好吃|hǎo chī}. It never follows the adjective, and no {是|shì} is needed.

questions.stem: You want your friend's opinion of the top you're trying on. What do you ask?
choices: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
questions.explanation: {怎么样|zěn me yàng} asks "how is it, what do you think?". {是|shì}{什么|shén me} asks what it is, {多少|duō shao}{钱|qián} the price, and {哪个|nǎ ge} doesn't fit after a noun like this.

questions.stem: You share an apple with a friend. How do you say "Half each."?
questions.explanation: "Half of something" is {一半|yí bàn}: {一|yì}{人|rén}{一半|yí bàn}, "one person, one half". {半|bàn} alone goes with a measure word or a time ({半|bàn}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}, {八|bā}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}), and {一|yí}{个|gè}{半|bàn} means "one and a half".

questions.stem: Which A-not-A question asks "Do you have tea?"
questions.explanation: {有|yǒu} is never negated with {不|bù}, so its A-not-A form is {有|yǒu}{没有|méi yǒu}: {你|nǐ}{有|yǒu}{没有|méi yǒu}{茶|chá}？ The positive comes first.

questions.stem: A: "{你|nǐ}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{吗|ma}？" B: "{对|duì}。" What does B mean?
questions.explanation: {对|duì} is "right, correct", the usual way to confirm. "Sorry" is {对不起|duì bu qǐ}, and "no, that's wrong" would be {不|bú}{对|duì}.

questions.stem: In 贵不贵？ (Is it expensive?), how is 不 said?
questions.explanation: In the middle of an A-not-A question 不 is light: guì bu guì. Before a 4th tone in a statement it rises ({不|bú}{贵|guì}), and elsewhere it is bù.

questions.stem: Which pinyin is right for 漂亮 (pretty)?
questions.explanation: 漂亮 is piào liang: a falling tone, then a light syllable. On its own, 亮 (bright) has its full tone, liàng.

questions.stem: Which character completes ___ {不|bu}{起|qǐ} (duìbuqǐ, sorry)?
questions.explanation: {=对不起 starts with 对: 又 on the left and 寸 on the right. 戏 (play) has 戈 on the right, 双 (pair) is two 又, and 讨 has 讠 instead of 又.=} (Simplified forms; traditional 对 is 對.)

questions.stem: Which character means "new" (xīn)?
questions.explanation: {=新 is 亲 + 斤 (an axe): the usual explanation is chopping wood, and from that "fresh, new". 亲 (relative) and 斤 (a unit of weight) are its two halves on their own; 薪 (salary) adds 艹 on top.=}

questions.stem: Which character has the radical 穴 (cave, hole) on top?
questions.explanation: 穿 (to wear) is 穴 over 牙. 字 and 家 have only the roof 宀 on top, without the 八 under it, and 常 has a different top.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about the clothes?
questions.explanation: You heard {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{非常|fēi cháng}{漂亮|piào liang}: extremely pretty. Cheap is {便宜|pián yi}, too expensive {太|tài}{贵|guì}{了|le}, new {新|xīn}.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking?
questions.explanation: You heard {贵|guì}{不|bu}{贵|guì}？, an A-not-A question: "Is it expensive (or not)?" The price would be asked with {多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}, which one with {哪个|nǎ ge}.

questions.stem: Listen to the question. Which is the best reply?
questions.explanation: The question was {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ (What do you think of this?). It asks for an opinion: {很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}！ A price answers {多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}, and {是|shì}{衣服|yī fu} answers "what is it?".

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker suggest?
choices: Let's buy it at half price.
Let's share it half and half.
questions.explanation: You heard {我们|wǒ men}{一|yì}{人|rén}{一半|yí bàn}{吧|ba}: "Let's go half each." {一半|yí bàn} is half of something, and {吧|ba} makes it a suggestion.

questions.stem: Read: "{王芳|Wáng Fāng}：{大卫|Dà wèi}，{你|nǐ}{看|kàn}，{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？{大卫|Dà wèi}：{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}。{贵|guì}{不|bu}{贵|guì}？{王芳|Wáng Fāng}：{不|bú}{太|tài}{贵|guì}，{一百二十|yì bǎi èr shí}{块|kuài}。{大卫|Dà wèi}：{真|zhēn}{便宜|pián yi}！" What does David think of the price?
questions.explanation: David exclaims {真|zhēn}{便宜|pián yi}！, "really cheap!". "Not very expensive" ({不|bú}{太|tài}{贵|guì}) is what Wang Fang says.

questions.stem: Build the question in Chinese, as an A-not-A question.
questions.prompt: Is this book expensive?
questions.explanation: The topic {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}, then adjective + {不|bu} + adjective: {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}{贵|guì}{不|bu}{贵|guì}？ No {吗|ma} with an A-not-A question.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: This piece of clothing is extremely pretty.
questions.explanation: Demonstrative + measure word + noun, then the degree adverb and the adjective, with no {是|shì}: {这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yī fu}{非常|fēi cháng}{漂亮|piào liang}.

questions.stem: Type the Chinese for "to wear (clothes)", in pinyin with its tone or in characters: ___
questions.explanation: "To wear" is 穿 chuān, first tone (type chuan1): {穿|chuān}{衣服|yī fu}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {穿|chuān}, to wear: the first tone, high and level.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {非常|fēi cháng}, extremely: tones 1+2, level, then rising.

questions.stem: What is English "black tea" called in Chinese?
questions.explanation: Black tea is {红茶|hóng chá}, "red tea". {黑茶|hēi chá} ("black tea" word for word) is a different kind: aged dark tea such as Pu'er. {绿茶|lǜ chá} is green tea, {白茶|bái chá} white tea.

questions.stem: Why is black tea called {红茶|hóng chá}, "red tea", in Chinese?
choices: for the reddish colour of the tea in the cup
because it grows in red soil
because it is drunk at weddings
because it is made from red leaves
questions.explanation: The name describes the colour of the brewed tea (and the reddish edges of the oxidised leaves). The leaves come from the same green tea plant as every other kind.

questions.stem: What decides which of the six kinds of Chinese tea (green, white, yellow, oolong, black, dark) a tea belongs to?
choices: the kind of plant it comes from
how the leaves are processed after picking
the season it is picked in
questions.explanation: All six come from the same plant; what differs is the processing, above all how much the leaves oxidise. Green tea is heated soon after picking, oolong is partly oxidised, black tea all the way.

questions.stem: Longjing ({龙井|Lóng jǐng}, "Dragon Well") is a famous green tea. Where does it come from?
choices: around West Lake in Hangzhou, Zhejiang
questions.explanation: Longjing grows around West Lake in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province. Yunnan is known for Pu'er, Anxi in Fujian for the oolong Tieguanyin, and Qimen in Anhui for Keemun black tea.

questions.stem: Pu'er ({普洱茶|Pǔ ěr chá}) is…
questions.explanation: Pu'er is a dark tea ({黑茶|hēi chá}) named after Pu'er in Yunnan; some Pu'er is stored for years to mature. Biluochun is the green tea from Jiangsu, Tieguanyin the oolong from Fujian.

questions.stem: Who wrote {茶经|Chá jīng}, The Classic of Tea, and when?
choices: Lu Yu, in the 8th century (Tang dynasty)
the Qianlong emperor, in the 18th century
Lu Yu, in the 19th century (Qing dynasty)
questions.explanation: {陆羽|Lù Yǔ} (Lu Yu) wrote The Classic of Tea in the 8th century, under the Tang dynasty: the oldest known book about tea. The Qianlong emperor is the hero of the finger-tapping story.

questions.stem: In a restaurant in Guangdong, someone taps two bent fingers on the table while you fill their cup. What do they mean?
questions.explanation: Tapping with two fingers is a silent thank-you, common in many places in southern China and in Cantonese-speaking communities. A popular story links it to the Qianlong emperor travelling in disguise.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?
questions.explanation: You heard {请|qǐng}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}: "Please have some tea", what a host says to a guest. Asking for tea would be {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}.

questions.stem: Listen. What kind of tea does the speaker like?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{绿茶|lǜ chá}: green tea. Black tea is {红茶|hóng chá}, milk tea {奶茶|nǎi chá}, oolong {乌龙茶|wū lóng chá}.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker order?
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{要|yào}{一|yì}{杯|bēi}{红茶|hóng chá}: one cup ({一|yì}{杯|bēi}) of black tea ({红茶|hóng chá}, "red tea").

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{很|hěn}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}。{早上|zǎo shang}{他|tā}{喝|hē}{绿茶|lǜ chá}，{下午|xià wǔ}{喝|hē}{红茶|hóng chá}。{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{不|bù}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}。" When does the father drink black tea?
questions.explanation: {下午|xià wǔ}{喝|hē}{红茶|hóng chá}: in the afternoon he drinks black ("red") tea. In the morning ({早上|zǎo shang}) he drinks green tea. It's the mother who doesn't drink tea.

questions.stem: Read the teahouse menu: "{绿茶|lǜ chá} 25{元|yuán}　{红茶|hóng chá} 30{元|yuán}　{乌龙茶|wū lóng chá} 35{元|yuán}　{奶茶|nǎi chá} 18{元|yuán}" Which is the cheapest?
questions.explanation: {奶茶|nǎi chá} (milk tea) is 18{元|yuán}, said {十八|shí bā}{块|kuài}. Green tea is 25, black tea 30 and oolong 35.

questions.stem: As a broad tendency, which grain is the main staple in northern China?
questions.explanation: Broadly, the north eats more wheat foods (noodles, dumplings, buns) and the south more rice. It's a tendency, not a rule: both are eaten everywhere today.

questions.stem: What is the difference between {包子|bāo zi} and {馒头|mán tou}?
choices: {包子|bāo zi} are boiled, {馒头|mán tou} are fried.
{包子|bāo zi} are made of rice, {馒头|mán tou} of wheat.
{包子|bāo zi} have a filling, {馒头|mán tou} are plain.
{包子|bāo zi} are eaten in the south only.
questions.explanation: Both are steamed wheat buns. {包子|bāo zi} are wrapped ({包|bāo}) round a filling; {馒头|mán tou} have none and are an everyday staple in the north, eaten with dishes like rice.

questions.stem: When do many families in northern China eat dumplings at the Spring Festival?
choices: around midnight on New Year's Eve
questions.explanation: Families make the {饺子|jiǎo zi} together on New Year's Eve and eat them around midnight, as the old year turns into the new one.

questions.stem: Why are New Year dumplings linked with wealth?
choices: They are very expensive to make.
They are filled with gold leaf.
Their shape looks like an old gold or silver ingot ({元宝|yuán bǎo}).
questions.explanation: The crescent shape is said to look like a {元宝|yuán bǎo}, the boat-shaped ingot once used as money, so eating dumplings is a wish for a prosperous year. Some families also hide a coin in one.

questions.stem: Long-life noodles ({长寿面|cháng shòu miàn}) are eaten on birthdays. What should you try not to do with them?
questions.explanation: Long noodles stand for a long life, so people try not to cut or break them while cooking or eating.

questions.stem: Why shouldn't you stand your chopsticks upright in a bowl of rice?
choices: It makes the rice go cold.
It means you want more rice.
It looks like the incense sticks offered to the dead.
It is a way of asking for the bill.
questions.explanation: Upright sticks in rice recall incense offered to the dead, so the gesture reminds people of funerals and is felt to be unlucky. Lay the chopsticks across the bowl or on a rest.

questions.stem: Where is the rough dividing line between the wheat-eating north and the rice-eating south usually drawn?
choices: along the Qinling mountains and the Huai River
questions.explanation: The Qinling mountains and the Huai River, across the middle of the country, are the usual north–south divide in geography, climate and food.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker suggest?
questions.explanation: You heard {我们|wǒ men}{包|bāo}{饺子|jiǎo zi}{吧|ba}: "Let's make (wrap) dumplings." {包|bāo} is "to wrap", and {吧|ba} makes it a suggestion. Buying would be {买|mǎi}.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?
questions.explanation: You heard {南方人|nán fāng rén}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}: people from the south like rice. Northerners are {北方人|běi fāng rén}.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker have in the morning?
choices: two steamed buns with a filling
questions.explanation: You heard {我|wǒ}{早上|zǎo shang}{吃|chī}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{包子|bāo zi}: two {包子|bāo zi}, the filled steamed buns. Plain ones would be {馒头|mán tou}, dumplings {饺子|jiǎo zi}.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{北京|Běi jīng}{人|rén}，{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{面条儿|miàn tiáor}{和|hé}{饺子|jiǎo zi}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{同学|tóng xué}{是|shì}{上海|Shàng hǎi}{人|rén}，{她|tā}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}。{我们|wǒ men}{都|dōu}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{包子|bāo zi}。" ({同学|tóng xué} = classmate) Who likes rice?
questions.explanation: The classmate from Shanghai likes rice ({她|tā}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{吃|chī}{米饭|mǐ fàn}); the writer from Beijing likes noodles and dumplings. What they both like ({都|dōu}) is steamed buns.

questions.stem: Read the breakfast menu: "{包子|bāo zi} 3{元|yuán}　{馒头|mán tou} 1{元|yuán}　{饺子|jiǎo zi} 15{元|yuán}　{面条儿|miàn tiáor} 12{元|yuán}" You want a plain bun with no filling. How much is it?
questions.explanation: A plain bun is a {馒头|mán tou}: 1{元|yuán}, said {一|yí}{块|kuài}. {包子|bāo zi} (3{元|yuán}) have a filling.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī} ___ {家|jiā}。 (My phone is at home.)
questions.explanation: {在|zài} is the verb "to be at": {我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{在|zài}{家|jiā}. {是|shì} would say the phone is a home, {有|yǒu} means "have", and {里|lǐ} is a locative that follows a noun; it can't be the verb.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "The water is in the cup."?
questions.explanation: The thing, {在|zài}, then the place, and the locative comes after its noun: {杯子|bēi zi}{里|lǐ}, "the cup's inside". {里|lǐ}{杯子|bēi zi} is English order, the second choice puts the cup in the water, and {是|shì} can't stand in for {在|zài}.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: A country is a place word already, so it never takes {里|lǐ}: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{在|zài}{中国|Zhōng guó}, "my dad is in China". {在|zài} comes before the place, not after it.

questions.stem: Which phrase means "on the book"?
questions.explanation: The locative follows the noun: {书|shū}{上|shàng}, "the book's top". {上|shàng}{书|shū} is English order; {书|shū}{里|lǐ} is "in the book" and {书|shū}{下|xià} "under the book".

questions.stem: You've got your friend's book. How do you say "Your book is with me."?
questions.explanation: A person isn't a place, so add {这儿|zhèr}: {我|wǒ}{这儿|zhèr}, "where I am". "{在|zài}{我|wǒ}" alone leaves out the place word, {是|shì} isn't the verb of location, and the last choice turns the sentence round.

questions.stem: You want to ask a stranger where the supermarket is. How do you start?
choices: {不客气|bú kè qi}，{超市|chāo shì}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？
{没关系|méi guān xi}，{超市|chāo shì}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？
questions.explanation: {请问|qǐng wèn}, "may I ask", opens a question to a stranger. {不客气|bú kè qi} answers thanks, {再见|zài jiàn} is goodbye and {没关系|méi guān xi} answers an apology.

questions.stem: Which pinyin is the word that asks "where?"
questions.explanation: {哪儿|nǎr}, third tone, asks "where?". {那儿|nàr}, fourth tone, points: "there". {这儿|zhèr} is "here" and {那里|nà lǐ} is "there" again. Only the tone tells {哪|nǎ} and {那|nà} apart.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {请问|qǐng wèn}, excuse me (may I ask): {请|qǐng} third tone, then {问|wèn} falling fourth. Before a fourth tone the third tone is said low, without its rise.

questions.stem: How is 不 pronounced in "{老师|lǎo shī}不{在|zài}。" (The teacher isn't here.)?
questions.explanation: Before a fourth tone {不|bù} changes to bú: {不|bú}{在|zài}. In the A-not-A question {在|zài}{不|bu}{在|zài} it's light, and before tones 1–3 it stays bù.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? {请|qǐng}___ (excuse me, may I ask)
questions.explanation: {请问|qǐng wèn} is written with {问|wèn}: a mouth {口|kǒu} inside the door {门|mén}. {门|mén} alone is "door", {们|men} is the plural suffix in {我们|wǒ men}, and {间|jiān} (a door with {日|rì} inside) is in {时间|shí jiān}.

questions.stem: {=Which character completes the label? {饭|fàn}___ (after meals)=}
questions.explanation: {={饭|fàn}{后|hòu}, "after meals". {后|hòu} has two left-falling strokes, a horizontal and {口|kǒu}. {名|míng} is the "name" character of {名字|míng zi}, {右|yòu} means "right" (a later word) and {号|hào} is "number, date".=}

questions.stem: What does 外 mean?
questions.explanation: {外|wài} is outside: {学校|xué xiào}{外|wài}, outside the school. Inside is {里|lǐ}, in front {前|qián}, behind {后|hòu}.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the person asking?
questions.explanation: {请问|qǐng wèn}，{超市|chāo shì}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？: "Excuse me, where's the supermarket?" The bookshop would be {书店|shū diàn}, and "over there" {那儿|nàr} (fourth tone), not {哪儿|nǎr}.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the sentence mean?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{在|zài}{你|nǐ}{那儿|nàr}{吗|ma}？: "Is my phone where you are?", that is, "have you got my phone?" {你|nǐ}{那儿|nàr} is the place of the person you're talking to.

questions.stem: Listen. Where is the teacher?

audio.text: 王老师现在不在学校，在家。

questions.explanation: {王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}{现在|xiàn zài}{不|bú}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}，{在|zài}{家|jiā}: Teacher Wang isn't at school now but at home. {不|bú}{在|zài} rules out the school.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the right reply?
questions.explanation: The question is "Excuse me, is Teacher Li here?" The answer repeats the verb: {不|bú}{在|zài}, "he isn't", and says where he is. A teacher isn't in a cup, and the other two answer different questions.

questions.stem: Read the note: "{安娜|Ān nà}：{我|wǒ}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}{里|lǐ}。{你|nǐ}{的|de}{书|shū}{不|bú}{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{这儿|zhèr}，{在|zài}{李明|Lǐ Míng}{那儿|nàr}。{王芳|Wáng Fāng}" Who has Anna's book?
questions.explanation: {在|zài}{李明|Lǐ Míng}{那儿|nàr}: the book is "at Li Ming's place", with Li Ming. {不|bú}{在|zài}{我|wǒ}{这儿|zhèr} says Wang Fang, who wrote the note, doesn't have it.

questions.stem: A label on a bottle of medicine ({药|yào}) says: "{一|yì}{天|tiān}{三|sān}{次|cì}，{饭|fàn}{后|hòu}。" ({次|cì}: times) When do you take it?
questions.explanation: {饭|fàn}{后|hòu} is "after meals", the compact style of labels; before meals would be {饭|fàn}{前|qián}. {一|yì}{天|tiān}{三|sān}{次|cì} is "three times a day".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: My phone is on the book.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{在|zài}{书|shū}{上|shàng}。 The thing first, then {在|zài}, then the place, with the locative after the noun. {是|shì} isn't needed: {在|zài} is the verb.

questions.stem: Type the word for "here" (pinyin with tone marks or characters; either form is fine): ___
questions.explanation: "Here" is {这儿|zhèr} (northern speech) or {这里|zhè lǐ} (everywhere). "There" is {那儿|nàr} / {那里|nà lǐ}, and "where?" {哪儿|nǎr} / {哪里|nǎ lǐ}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {前|qián}, in front; before: the second tone, rising. Don't confuse it with {钱|qián} (money), the same syllable written with another character.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {外|wài}, outside: the fourth tone, falling sharply. In {外边|wài bian} it keeps that tone and {边|bian} is light.

questions.stem: Which is the most natural way to say "There's a book on the table."?
questions.explanation: Place + {有|yǒu} + thing: {桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}. The place is the subject, so it needs no {在|zài} before it (the second choice is heard in speech, but it's less natural). The third choice copies English "there is a book on the table": possible, but not the usual order. In the last, {在|zài} can't introduce a new thing.

questions.stem: Choose the words: {房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ} ___ {电视|diàn shì}。 (There's no TV in the room.)
questions.explanation: The negative of {有|yǒu} is always {没有|méi yǒu}; there's no such word as "{不|bù}{有|yǒu}". {不|bú}{在|zài} is "not at (a place)", which would need the TV first: {电视|diàn shì}{不|bú}{在|zài}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}.

questions.stem: You can't find your phone. How do you ask where it is?
questions.explanation: Your phone is a known thing, so it goes first with {在|zài}: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？ {有|yǒu} introduces something new ("is there a…?"), and the last choice has no verb after the subject.

questions.stem: Choose the verb: {桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng} ___ {一|yí}{个|gè}{杯子|bēi zi}。 (There's a cup on the table.)
questions.explanation: The place comes first and the new thing ({一|yí}{个|gè}{杯子|bēi zi}, "a cup") after it, so the verb is {有|yǒu}. {在|zài} would need the cup first ({杯子|bēi zi}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}), and {住|zhù} is "to live".

questions.stem: Type the missing verb ({在|zài} or {有|yǒu}, in pinyin with tone marks or characters): {你|nǐ}{的|de}{杯子|bēi zi} ___ {桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}。 (Your cup is on the table.)
questions.explanation: Your cup is known, so it comes first and takes {在|zài}: {你|nǐ}{的|de}{杯子|bēi zi}{在|zài}{桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}. With {有|yǒu} the place would come first: {桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{杯子|bēi zi}.

questions.stem: Which is the most natural way to say "There are lots of people outside."?
questions.explanation: {外边|wài bian} can stand alone as a place; one-syllable {外|wài} can't. A {有|yǒu} sentence usually starts with the place, with no {在|zài} before it (the third choice is heard, but it's less natural), and the last choice says the people "have" the outside.

questions.stem: What does "{超市|chāo shì}{在|zài}{那边|nà biān}。" mean?
questions.explanation: {那边|nà biān} is "that side, over there"; over here is {这边|zhè biān}. The supermarket comes first with {在|zài}, so it's a known place being located. "There's a supermarket over there" would be {那边|nà biān}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{超市|chāo shì}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I live in Beijing."? ({北京|Běi jīng}: Beijing)
questions.explanation: {住|zhù}{在|zài} + place: {我|wǒ}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}. With {住|zhù}, {在|zài} and the place usually come after the verb. {在|zài} must stand right before the place, so the other orders don't work ({我|wǒ}{在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng}{住|zhù} would be correct, but it isn't offered).

questions.stem: How is 边 usually said in "外边" (outside)?
questions.explanation: In {外边|wài bian}, {上边|shàng bian}, {前边|qián bian} and the other locatives, {边|biān} is usually light. It keeps its first tone in {这边|zhè biān} and {那边|nà biān}, and alone: {边|biān}, side.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? {电|diàn}___ (television)
questions.explanation: {电视|diàn shì} ends in {视|shì}: 礻 on the left and {见|jiàn} (see) on the right. {现|xiàn} is in {现在|xiàn zài}, {见|jiàn} alone is "see", and {机|jī} is in {手机|shǒu jī}.

questions.stem: {=Which character completes the word? {外|wài}___ (outside)=}
questions.explanation: {={外边|wài bian}: {边|biān} is {力|lì} inside 辶. All four choices have 辶; {这|zhè} has {文|wén} inside, {还|hái} (still, also; later) has {不|bù}, and {过|guò} (HSK 2) has {寸|cùn}.=}

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {桌|zhuō} and {椅|yǐ} both have {木|mù} (wood): {桌子|zhuō zi}, {椅子|yǐ zi}. {房|fáng} has 户 (door) on top, as in {房间|fáng jiān}; {脑|nǎo} has the "meat moon" for the body ({电脑|diàn nǎo}, "electric brain"); {住|zhù} has the person radical. A door would be {门|mén}.

questions.stem: Which component is on the left of 视 (in {电视|diàn shì})?
questions.explanation: {视|shì} has 礻 (from {示|shì}, which also gives the sound) and {见|jiàn} (see). 衤 is the clothing radical, with one stroke more; 亻 is "person" and 讠 "speech".

questions.stem: Listen. What is on the table?
questions.explanation: {桌子|zhuō zi}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{一|yí}{个|gè}{杯子|bēi zi}: there's a cup on the table. A book would be {一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}, a phone {手机|shǒu jī}, and "nothing" {没有|méi yǒu}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true about the room?

audio.text: 我的房间里没有电视，有电脑。

choices: It has a computer but no TV.
It has a TV but no computer.
It has a TV and a computer.
It has neither a TV nor a computer.
questions.explanation: {没有|méi yǒu}{电视|diàn shì}, {有|yǒu}{电脑|diàn nǎo}: no TV, but a computer. Listen for {没有|méi yǒu} before the thing that's missing.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the right reply?
questions.explanation: "Where do you live?" is answered with {住|zhù}{在|zài} + place: "I live on campus." The first choice says where you work, the third how big your home is, and the last where the school is.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the person want to know?
choices: Whether there's a supermarket around here
questions.explanation: {这儿|zhèr}{有|yǒu}{超市|chāo shì}{吗|ma}？: "Is there a supermarket here?" The place comes first and {有|yǒu} asks whether something exists. "Where is the supermarket?" would be {超市|chāo shì}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？, and "Is this a supermarket?" {这|zhè}{是|shì}{超市|chāo shì}{吗|ma}？

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{个|gè}{房间|fáng jiān}。{我|wǒ}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{电脑|diàn nǎo}，{没有|méi yǒu}{电视|diàn shì}。{电视|diàn shì}{在|zài}{爸爸|bà ba}{妈妈|mā ma}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}。" Where is the TV?
questions.explanation: {电视|diàn shì}{在|zài}{爸爸|bà ba}{妈妈|mā ma}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}: the TV is in the parents' room. The writer's room has a computer but no TV, and the home has only two rooms.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: There's a computer in my room.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{电脑|diàn nǎo}。 The place ({我|wǒ}{的|de}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}) comes first, then {有|yǒu} and the thing, with no {在|zài} before the place. {没|méi} would make it "there's no computer".

questions.stem: Build the question in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Where do you live?
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{住|zhù}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}？ is the usual order: {住|zhù}{在|zài} + place. {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}{住|zhù}？ is correct too, but less common.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {房间|fáng jiān}, room: a rising second tone, then a high level first tone.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {电脑|diàn nǎo}, computer: a falling fourth tone, then a third tone (low at the end of a word). All the {电|diàn} words start with that fourth tone.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm going to Beijing by train."? ({北京|Běi jīng}: Beijing)
questions.explanation: The means of travel comes first, then the going: {坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē} + {去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}. {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē} means "I'm going to Beijing to take a train", and the other two break up {坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}.

questions.stem: Choose the verb: {他|tā} ___ {出租车|chū zū chē}。 (He drives a taxi: it's his job.)
questions.explanation: The driver {开|kāi}s a vehicle: {他|tā}{开|kāi}{出租车|chū zū chē}. A passenger {坐|zuò}s it. {做|zuò} is "do, make" (same sound as {坐|zuò}), and {到|dào} is "arrive".

questions.stem: Choose the verb: {我|wǒ} ___ {出租车|chū zū chē}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。 (I'm taking a taxi home.)
questions.explanation: A passenger sits in the taxi: {坐|zuò}{出租车|chū zū chē}{回|huí}{家|jiā}. {开|kāi} would make you the taxi driver, {住|zhù} is "live", and {到|dào} would need a place after it.

questions.stem: How do you ask "How do you get to school?"
choices: {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？
{你|nǐ}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}？
questions.explanation: {怎么|zěn me} goes right before the verb it asks about: {你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}？ {怎么样|zěn me yàng} asks what something is like, so the first choice is "how is going to school?", and {怎么|zěn me} doesn't go before the subject.

questions.stem: Which question means "What time does the train arrive?"
questions.explanation: The time word comes before the verb: {火车|huǒ chē}{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}？ {要|yào}{几|jǐ}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí} asks how long it takes, and {在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr} where it is. The time doesn't go after {到|dào}.

questions.stem: Your friend has a new car. How do you ask what it's like?
questions.explanation: {怎么样|zěn me yàng} at the end asks "what is it like?". {怎么|zěn me} needs a verb after it ({怎么|zěn me}{去|qù}, {怎么|zěn me}{说|shuō}), so it can't end the question or stand before a noun.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm not going by plane."?
questions.explanation: {不|bù} goes before the first verb, the part that's denied: {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}{去|qù} ({不|bú} because {坐|zuò} is fourth tone). {坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}{不|bú}{去|qù} would say you're not going at all, and {不|bù} can't split {坐|zuò} from its vehicle or stand before the subject.

questions.stem: How do you ask "Can you drive?"
questions.explanation: Driving is a learned skill: {会|huì} + {开车|kāi chē}. {会|huì} comes before the verb, not after it; {坐|zuò}{车|chē} is riding as a passenger, and {开会|kāi huì} (a later word) means "have a meeting".

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {飞机|fēi jī}, plane: two high, level first tones. {机|jī} is the same syllable as in {手机|shǒu jī}.

questions.stem: Read the timetable for trips to {北京|Běi jīng} (Beijing; the times are made up for practice): "{飞机|fēi jī} 9:00 → 11:00   {火车|huǒ chē} 8:00 → 13:00" How long does the train take?
questions.explanation: {火车|huǒ chē} leaves at 8:00 and arrives at 13:00 (one in the afternoon): five hours, {五|wǔ}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}. The plane takes two hours. Timetables use the 24-hour clock.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? {火|huǒ}___ (train)
questions.explanation: {火车|huǒ chē}, "fire vehicle": {车|chē}. {东|dōng} (east, in {东西|dōng xi}) and {年|nián} (year) look similar, and {军|jūn} (army, not in this course) is {车|chē} under a cover.

questions.stem: Which character is zuò, "to sit; to travel by"?
questions.explanation: {坐|zuò} is two people on the ground {土|tǔ}. {做|zuò} (do, make) and {作|zuò} (in {工作|gōng zuò}) sound the same but have the person radical; {左|zuǒ} (left) is a later word.

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {火|huǒ} fire ({火车|huǒ chē}), {车|chē} vehicle, {开|kāi} open ({开车|kāi chē}, drive), {出|chū} go out ({出租车|chū zū chē}, "rent-out car"), {到|dào} arrive. "Sit" is {坐|zuò}.

questions.stem: Listen. How is the speaker going to Beijing?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}{去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}: tomorrow by plane. A train is {火车|huǒ chē}, a taxi {出租车|chū zū chē}, and driving {开车|kāi chē}.

questions.stem: Listen. When does the train arrive?
questions.explanation: {下午|xià wǔ}{三|sān}{点|diǎn}{到|dào}: it arrives at three in the afternoon. In three hours would be {三|sān}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}, with {个|gè} and {小时|xiǎo shí}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the right reply?
questions.explanation: "How do you get to school?" asks for the means: {我|wǒ}{坐|zuò}{出租车|chū zū chē}{去|qù}, by taxi. The others say what the school is like, where it is and when you arrive.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true?

audio.text: 我爸爸会开车，我妈妈不会。

questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{会|huì}{开车|kāi chē}，{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{不|bú}{会|huì}: Dad can drive, Mum can't. The second {会|huì} stands for {会|huì}{开车|kāi chē}: a short answer can be just the modal verb.

questions.stem: Read: "{高飞|Gāo Fēi}{明天|míng tiān}{去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}。{他|tā}{不|bú}{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}，{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}。{坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{要|yào}{六|liù}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。" Which is true?
choices: Gao Fei is flying to Beijing.
Gao Fei's journey takes six hours.
questions.explanation: {坐|zuò}{火车|huǒ chē}{要|yào}{六|liù}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}: the train takes six hours. He isn't flying ({不|bú}{坐|zuò}{飞机|fēi jī}), he goes tomorrow ({明天|míng tiān}), and nobody drives.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Mum is taking a taxi home.
