questions.explanation: {妈妈|mā ma}{坐|zuò}{出租车|chū zū chē}{回|huí}{家|jiā}。 The vehicle first ({坐|zuò}{出租车|chū zū chē}), then the going ({回|huí}{家|jiā}). {开|kāi} would make Mum the driver.

questions.stem: Type the word for "train" (pinyin with tone marks or characters): ___
questions.explanation: {火车|huǒ chē}, "fire vehicle", from the steam age: third tone, then first. A plane is {飞机|fēi jī} and a taxi {出租车|chū zū chē}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {火车|huǒ chē}, train: a third tone, said low before the first tone, then a high level first tone.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {坐|zuò}, to sit; to travel by: the fourth tone, falling. {做|zuò} and {作|zuò} have the same sound.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {我|wǒ} ___ {说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。 (I can speak Chinese: I've learned it.)
questions.explanation: A learned skill takes {会|huì}: {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}. {能|néng} is "be able (now, in this situation)", {可以|kě yǐ} "be allowed", and {想|xiǎng} "would like to".

questions.stem: Choose the word: {我|wǒ} ___ {坐|zuò}{这儿|zhèr}{吗|ma}？ (May I sit here?)
questions.explanation: Asking permission: {我|wǒ}{可以|kě yǐ}{坐|zuò}{这儿|zhèr}{吗|ma}？ ({能|néng} would work too, but it isn't offered.) {会|huì} would ask whether you know how to sit there, and {想|xiǎng} / {要|yào} talk about what you want.

questions.stem: Your friend asks you to come tomorrow, but you're busy. Choose the word: {我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{不|bù} ___ {来|lái}。
questions.explanation: Being busy means the situation doesn't allow it: {我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{不|bù}{能|néng}{来|lái}. {不|bú}{会|huì}{来|lái} would sound like "I won't come (that's unlikely)", {不|bù}{可以|kě yǐ} like a ban, and {是|shì} isn't a modal verb.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: A modal verb goes after the subject and before the main verb: {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}. It never follows the verb or comes before the subject.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I have Chinese class this afternoon."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{下午|xià wǔ}{上课|shàng kè}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
{我|wǒ}{上课|shàng kè}{下午|xià wǔ}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}。
questions.explanation: {上课|shàng kè} already has its object, {课|kè}, so the subject of the class goes in front of {课|kè}: {上|shàng}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{课|kè}. The time word {下午|xià wǔ} stays before the verb.

questions.stem: Which word means "classmate"?
questions.explanation: {同学|tóng xué}: {同|tóng} is "same", someone who studies with you. {学生|xué sheng} is any student, {大学生|dà xué shēng} a university student, and {老师|lǎo shī} a teacher.

questions.stem: "{你|nǐ}{会|huì}{开车|kāi chē}{吗|ma}？" How do you answer "yes" in one word?
questions.explanation: Chinese answers with the modal verb: {会|huì}, "(I) can". The negative is {不|bú}{会|huì}. {是|shì} is for {是|shì} questions and {有|yǒu} for {有|yǒu} questions.

questions.stem: 可以 is written kě yǐ, with two third tones. How is it said?
choices: kě yǐ, both full third tones
questions.explanation: Two third tones in a row: the first is said as a second tone, so {可以|kě yǐ} sounds like ké yǐ (just like {你好|nǐ hǎo}, said ní hǎo). The pinyin isn't changed.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {写|xiě}, to write: the third tone, low and dipping. Don't confuse it with {谢|xiè} in {谢谢|xiè xie}, a falling fourth tone.

questions.stem: {=Which character completes the word? {学|xué}___ (to study)=}
questions.explanation: {={学习|xué xí} ends in {习|xí}: a hooked stroke, a dot and a rising stroke. {刁|diāo} (not in this course) has no dot inside, {司|sī} is in {公司|gōng sī}, and {刀|dāo} is "knife".=}

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? ___ {学|xué} (classmate)
questions.explanation: {同学|tóng xué}: {同|tóng} is a frame open at the bottom with 一 and 口 inside. {问|wèn} and {间|jiān} are inside a door {门|mén}, and {用|yòng} (to use, HSK 3) has no 口.

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {课|kè} as in {上课|shàng kè}; {写|xiě} write; {同|tóng} same, in {同学|tóng xué}; {能|néng} be able; {习|xí} practise, in {学习|xué xí}. A word is {词|cí} (HSK 2).

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true about the speaker?

audio.text: 我会说汉语，不会写汉字。

choices: They can write characters but can't speak Chinese.
They can speak and write Chinese.
They can't speak or write Chinese.
They can speak Chinese but can't write characters.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}，{不|bú}{会|huì}{写|xiě}{汉字|hàn zì}: "I can speak Chinese but can't write characters." {不|bú}{会|huì} goes with the second part.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the student doing?

audio.text: 老师，我可以看一下书吗？

choices: Asking if they may look at the book
Saying they can read the book
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{可以|kě yǐ}{看|kàn}{一下|yí xià}{书|shū}{吗|ma}？: "May I have a look at the book?" {可以|kě yǐ} asks permission, and {一下|yí xià} makes it "a quick look".

questions.stem: Listen. What is the question?
choices: What time does our class start?
What time does our class finish?
How many classes do we have?
questions.explanation: {下课|xià kè} is "class ends": "What time do we finish class?" Starting is {上课|shàng kè}; "what time is it" is {现在|xiàn zài}{几|jǐ}{点|diǎn}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the right reply?
choices: {不|bù}{能|néng}，{我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{要|yào}{去|qù}{北京|Běi jīng}。
questions.explanation: "Can you come to class tomorrow?" is answered with {能|néng} or {不|bù}{能|néng}: "No, I'm going to Beijing tomorrow." {可以|kě yǐ}，{请|qǐng}{坐|zuò} answers a request to sit down.

questions.stem: Read the notice: "{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{课|kè}：{上午|shàng wǔ}{八|bā}{点|diǎn}{上课|shàng kè}，{十|shí}{点|diǎn}{下课|xià kè}。{下午|xià wǔ}{没有|méi yǒu}{课|kè}。" When does Chinese class end?
questions.explanation: {十|shí}{点|diǎn}{下课|xià kè}: class ends at ten. It starts at eight ({八|bā}{点|diǎn}{上课|shàng kè}), and there's no class in the afternoon ({下午|xià wǔ}{没有|méi yǒu}{课|kè}).

questions.stem: A sign in a classroom says: "{这儿|zhèr}{不|bù}{能|néng}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。" What does it mean?
choices: You can't make phone calls here.
You can make phone calls here.
questions.explanation: {不|bù}{能|néng} + verb on a sign is "you can't, not allowed": no phone calls here. "There's no phone" would be {这儿|zhèr}{没有|méi yǒu}{电话|diàn huà}.

questions.stem: Build the question in Chinese.
questions.prompt: May I sit here?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{可以|kě yǐ}{坐|zuò}{这儿|zhèr}{吗|ma}？ The modal verb comes before the main verb, and {吗|ma} ends the question. {会|huì} doesn't ask permission.

questions.stem: Type the modal verb (pinyin with tone marks or characters): {我|wǒ} ___ {开车|kāi chē}。 (I can drive: I learned last year.)
questions.explanation: Driving is a learned skill: {我|wǒ}{会|huì}{开车|kāi chē}. {能|néng} would be about whether you're able to right now, and {可以|kě yǐ} about being allowed.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {同学|tóng xué}, classmate: two rising second tones.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {汉字|hàn zì}, Chinese character: two falling fourth tones. The first is said a little higher and shorter, as in any 4 + 4 pair.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "It's started raining!"?
questions.explanation: {下雨|xià yǔ} is verb + object ("come-down rain"), and the change-of-state {了|le} goes at the end: {下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}！ {雨|yǔ}{下|xià} is English order, {了|le} never starts a sentence, and {很|hěn} goes before adjectives.

questions.stem: Choose the word: {今天|jīn tiān}{天气|tiān qì} ___ {冷|lěng}。 (It's cold today.)
questions.explanation: An adjective is the predicate by itself, usually with {很|hěn}: {今天|jīn tiān}{天气|tiān qì}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}. No {是|shì} before an adjective; {了|le} would go at the end; {有|yǒu} means "have".

questions.stem: You've changed your mind. How do you say "I'm not going any more."?
questions.explanation: {不|bù}…{了|le} is "not any more": {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}, with {了|le} at the end. {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù} means "I didn't go" (lesson 25), and {了|le} can't stand before or inside {不|bú}{去|qù}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Yesterday was cold."?
questions.explanation: {了|le} isn't a past tense: the time word {昨天|zuó tiān} already says it's past, so {昨天|zuó tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}. Adding {了|le} would announce a change. {是|shì} doesn't go before an adjective, and {很|hěn} comes before it.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I think this room is very nice."?
choices: {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{这个|zhè ge}{房间|fáng jiān}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。
{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{这个|zhè ge}{房间|fáng jiān}{是|shì}{好|hǎo}。
{我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}{这个|zhè ge}{房间|fáng jiān}。
{我|wǒ}{这个|zhè ge}{房间|fáng jiān}{觉得|jué de}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}。
questions.explanation: {觉得|jué de} + a normal sentence: {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de} + {这个|zhè ge}{房间|fáng jiān}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo}. Inside it, no {是|shì} before the adjective. The opinion is a whole sentence, so {这个|zhè ge}{房间|fáng jiān} comes before {很|hěn}{好|hǎo}, not after it, and {觉得|jué de} follows its subject {我|wǒ}.

questions.stem: What does "{他|tā}{是|shì}{大学生|dà xué shēng}{了|le}。" mean?
choices: He isn't a student any more.
questions.explanation: The {了|le} at the end marks a new situation: he has become a university student. It isn't a past tense ("was"), "not any more" would need {不|bù}…{了|le}, and a question would end in {吗|ma}.

questions.stem: What does "{不|bú}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}。" mean?
questions.explanation: {不|bù}…{了|le} is "not any more": it was raining, and now it isn't. "Not yet" and "again" need other words, and "going to rain" would be {要|yào}{下雨|xià yǔ} or {会|huì}{下雨|xià yǔ}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "It's snowing in Beijing now." ({北京|Běi jīng}: Beijing)
questions.explanation: {下雪|xià xuě} works like {下雨|xià yǔ}: verb first, then {雪|xuě}. The {了|le} says it has started. {北京|Běi jīng}{是|shì}{雪|xuě} says "Beijing is snow", and {有|yǒu} doesn't go before a verb here.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {热|rè}, hot: a falling fourth tone. Its opposite, {冷|lěng} (cold), is third tone.

questions.stem: How is 了 said at the end of "{下雨|xià yǔ}了！"?
questions.explanation: The particle {了|le} is always light: le. The same character is read liǎo in a few later words ({了解|liǎo jiě}, to understand), never at the end of a sentence.

questions.stem: Which character is the particle le?
questions.explanation: {了|le} has just two strokes: the top stroke across and down to the left, then a hooked vertical. 子 (the zi of {孩子|hái zi}) has a horizontal across the middle, and {予|yǔ} and {丁|dīng} are characters this course doesn't teach.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? {下|xià}___ (to snow)
questions.explanation: {下雪|xià xuě}: {雪|xuě} is the rain radical on top with 彐 underneath. {雨|yǔ} alone is rain ({下雨|xià yǔ}); {雷|léi} (thunder) and {需|xū} (to need, HSK 3) share the rain top.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word? {天|tiān}___ (weather)
questions.explanation: {天气|tiān qì}: {气|qì}, air. {汽|qì} (steam, with three-dot water) and {乞|qǐ} (to beg) are later or rarer characters, and {吃|chī} (to eat) has the mouth radical.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true?

audio.text: 外边下雨了，我们不去了。

choices: It's raining, but they're still going.
It's started raining, so they aren't going any more.
It's stopped raining, so they're going.
questions.explanation: {外边|wài bian}{下雨|xià yǔ}{了|le}: it has started raining outside. {我们|wǒ men}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}: "we're not going any more". Both {了|le} mark a change.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is the right reply?
questions.explanation: "What's the weather like today?" asks for an adjective: {今天|jīn tiān}{很|hěn}{热|rè}, it's hot today. {我|wǒ}{很|hěn}{好|hǎo} answers "how are you?", and {星期三|xīng qī sān} the day of the week.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?
choices: I don't think it's cold today.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{冷|lěng}: "I feel (that) today (is) not cold." {觉得|jué de} gives the speaker's opinion; the {不|bù} is inside it.

questions.stem: Listen. What do you learn about the speaker's daughter?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{女儿|nǚ ér}{五|wǔ}{岁|suì}{了|le}: "my daughter is five now". {了|le} marks the new age, not the past. Five daughters would be {五|wǔ}{个|gè}{女儿|nǚ ér}, and fifteen {十五|shí wǔ}.

questions.stem: Read the weather report (made up for practice): "{北京|Běi jīng}：{下雪|xià xuě}，{非常|fēi cháng}{冷|lěng}。{上海|Shàng hǎi}：{下雨|xià yǔ}，{不|bù}{冷|lěng}。" ({上海|Shàng hǎi}: Shanghai) Which is true?
choices: It's snowing and very cold in Beijing.
questions.explanation: {北京|Běi jīng}：{下雪|xià xuě}，{非常|fēi cháng}{冷|lěng}: snow and very cold in Beijing. In Shanghai it's raining ({下雨|xià yǔ}) and not cold ({不|bù}{冷|lěng}).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I think it's too hot.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{觉得|jué de}{太|tài}{热|rè}{了|le}。 {觉得|jué de} is followed by the opinion, here {太|tài}…{了|le} around the adjective. No {是|shì} before {热|rè}.

questions.stem: Type the word for "weather" (pinyin with tone marks or characters): ___
questions.explanation: {天气|tiān qì}: {天|tiān} (sky, day) + {气|qì} (air): first tone, then fourth. Ask about it with {天气|tiān qì}{怎么样|zěn me yàng}？

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {冷|lěng}, cold: the third tone, low and dipping. {热|rè} (hot) falls: fourth tone.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {下雪|xià xuě}, to snow: a falling fourth tone, then a third tone. {下雨|xià yǔ} has the same pattern.

questions.stem: Which is the longest river in China (and in Asia)?
choices: They are all about the same length.
questions.explanation: {长江|Cháng Jiāng}, about 6,300 km, is the longest river in Asia and the third longest in the world. The Yellow River, about 5,460 km, is China's second longest.

questions.stem: Why is the Yellow River called "yellow"?
choices: Its source is in yellow rocks.
Its water carries a lot of fine yellow-brown soil.
questions.explanation: The river carries huge amounts of fine yellow-brown soil (loess), which colours the water. {黄|huáng} is "yellow" and {河|hé} "river".

questions.stem: What does the name {长江|Cháng Jiāng} mean word for word?
questions.explanation: {长|cháng} is "long" and {江|jiāng} "river": the long river. The yellow river is {黄河|Huáng Hé}, and the north is {北方|běi fāng}.

questions.stem: Where is Mount Everest ({珠峰|Zhū Fēng})?
choices: in the middle of the North China Plain
at the mouth of the Yangtze
on the border of China and Nepal
questions.explanation: Everest, in the Himalayas, stands on the border of China and Nepal. The North China Plain is flat, and the Yangtze reaches the sea near Shanghai.

questions.stem: What height for Everest did China and Nepal announce together in 2020?
questions.explanation: The joint measurement announced in 2020 was 8,848.86 m. 6,300 and about 5,460 are the lengths of the Yangtze and the Yellow River in kilometres.

questions.stem: What is most of the Gobi ({戈壁|Gē bì}) made of?
questions.explanation: Much of the Gobi isn't sandy at all: it's bare rock and gravel, very dry, with bitterly cold winters.

questions.stem: Compared with the north, the land south of the Qinling–Huai River line is, broadly…
choices: colder and drier, and grows wheat
warmer and wetter, and grows rice
questions.explanation: The line roughly follows a January average of 0 °C and about 800 mm of rain a year. To the south it's warmer and wetter, with rice; to the north colder and drier, with wheat.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "There's snow on the mountain."? ({山|shān}: mountain)
questions.explanation: Place + {有|yǒu} + thing, with the locative after the noun: {山|shān}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{雪|xuě}. Usually no {在|zài} before the place, and {上|shàng} stays with {山|shān}.

questions.stem: Listen. What do you hear about the north in winter?
choices: It's cold and it can snow.
questions.explanation: {北方|běi fāng}{冬天|dōng tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{会|huì}{下雪|xià xuě}: in the north, winter is cold and it can snow.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true?

audio.text: 长江在南方，黄河在北方。

choices: Both rivers are in the north.
The Yangtze is in the south and the Yellow River in the north.
The Yangtze is in the north and the Yellow River in the south.
Both rivers are in the south.
questions.explanation: {长江|Cháng Jiāng}{在|zài}{南方|nán fāng}，{黄河|Huáng Hé}{在|zài}{北方|běi fāng}: the Yangtze is in the south, the Yellow River in the north. {南|nán} is south, {北|běi} north.

questions.stem: Read: "{中国|Zhōng guó}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{山|shān}。{珠峰|Zhū Fēng}{非常|fēi cháng}{高|gāo}，{山|shān}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{雪|xuě}。" ({山|shān}: mountain; {高|gāo}: high) What is on Everest?
questions.explanation: {山|shān}{上|shàng}{有|yǒu}{雪|xuě}: there's snow on the mountain. {非常|fēi cháng}{高|gāo} says it is extremely high.

questions.stem: Read: "{北京|Běi jīng}{在|zài}{北方|běi fāng}，{冬天|dōng tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}。{南方|nán fāng}{很|hěn}{热|rè}，{雨|yǔ}{很|hěn}{多|duō}。" ({冬天|dōng tiān}: winter) Which is true?
choices: It's hot in Beijing in winter.
It snows a lot in the south.
Beijing is in the north, and its winters are cold.
questions.explanation: {北京|Běi jīng}{在|zài}{北方|běi fāng}: Beijing is in the north, and {冬天|dōng tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}, winter is cold. The south is hot, with a lot of rain ({雨|yǔ}{很|hěn}{多|duō}); the text says nothing about snow there.

questions.stem: What does the name {北京|Běi jīng} mean?
questions.explanation: {北|běi} is north and {京|jīng} capital. {南京|Nán jīng} is "the southern capital", and {故宫|Gù gōng} "the former palace".

questions.stem: What do most Chinese speakers call the Forbidden City?
questions.explanation: {故宫|Gù gōng}, "the former palace". {天坛|Tiān tán} is the Temple of Heaven, a {胡同|hú tòng} is an alley, and {首都|shǒu dū} means "capital city".

questions.stem: When was the Forbidden City built?
questions.explanation: It was built from 1406 to 1420. In 1925 it became the Palace Museum, in 1987 a World Heritage site, and 1969 is the year Beijing's first subway line opened.

questions.stem: Why do almost all the roofs of the Forbidden City have yellow tiles?
choices: Yellow sand covers them in spring.
questions.explanation: Yellow was the colour of the emperor, so the palace roofs were covered in yellow glazed tiles.

questions.stem: What did the emperors do at the Temple of Heaven ({天坛|Tiān tán})?
choices: They prayed to Heaven for good harvests.
questions.explanation: Every year the emperors came to pray to Heaven for good harvests, above all at the round Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests. They lived in the Forbidden City.

questions.stem: What is a {胡同|hú tòng}?
choices: a narrow alley formed by rows of courtyard houses
a hall in the Forbidden City
questions.explanation: Hutongs are the narrow alleys of old Beijing, lined with courtyard houses ({四合院|sì hé yuàn}). The word probably comes from Mongolian.

questions.stem: When did Beijing's first subway line open?
questions.explanation: 1969: it was the first subway in China. 1420 is when the palace and the Temple of Heaven were finished, 1925 when the Palace Museum opened, and 1998 when the Temple of Heaven became a World Heritage site.

questions.stem: In which season does most of Beijing's rain fall?
questions.explanation: Summer ({夏天|xià tiān}) is hot and humid, with most of the year's rain. Winter is cold and dry, spring dry and sometimes dusty, and autumn short and crisp.

questions.stem: Listen. How is the speaker going to the Forbidden City?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{坐|zuò}{地铁|dì tiě}{去|qù}{故宫|Gù gōng}: by subway. A taxi is {出租车|chū zū chē}, a bus {公交车|gōng jiāo chē}, a bike {自行车|zì xíng chē}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true about Beijing?

audio.text: 北京冬天很冷，夏天很热。

choices: It's warm in winter and cool in summer.
It's cold in winter and hot in summer.
questions.explanation: {冬天|dōng tiān}{很|hěn}{冷|lěng}，{夏天|xià tiān}{很|hěn}{热|rè}: cold in winter, hot in summer.

questions.stem: Read the postcard: "{我|wǒ}{现在|xiàn zài}{在|zài}{一|yí}{个|gè}{胡同|hú tòng}{里|lǐ}。{明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{去|qù}{天坛|Tiān tán}。" Where is the writer now?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{现在|xiàn zài}{在|zài}{一|yí}{个|gè}{胡同|hú tòng}{里|lǐ}: "I'm in a hutong right now." The Temple of Heaven is where the writer wants to go tomorrow.

questions.stem: Read: "{早上|zǎo shang}{天坛|Tiān tán}{有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén}。" What does it say?
choices: The Temple of Heaven opens early.
Nobody goes to the Temple of Heaven in the morning.
Many people live in the Temple of Heaven.
In the morning there are lots of people at the Temple of Heaven.
questions.explanation: {早上|zǎo shang} (in the morning) + {天坛|Tiān tán} (the place) + {有|yǒu}{很|hěn}{多|duō}{人|rén} (there are many people): an existential sentence with a time word in front.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "It's a bit cold today"?
questions.explanation: {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr} goes before the adjective and takes the place of {很|hěn}. It never follows the adjective, {一点儿|yì diǎnr} can't stand before an adjective, and {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr} and {很|hěn} don't go together.

questions.stem: In a shop you want to ask for a lower price: "Could it be a bit cheaper?" Which do you say?
questions.explanation: Asking for "a bit more so" is adjective + {一点儿|yì diǎnr}: {便宜|pián yi}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}. {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr} only describes how something is (usually a complaint: {有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{贵|guì}), so it can't make a request.

questions.stem: You see this sign in a library: "{请|qǐng}{不要|bú yào}{在|zài}{这儿|zhèr}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。" What does it say?
choices: Please make your phone calls here.
Please don't make phone calls here.
questions.explanation: {请|qǐng}{不要|bú yào} + verb is "please don't …", the polite form on signs. {在|zài}{这儿|zhèr} (here) comes before the verb {打电话|dǎ diàn huà} (make a phone call).

questions.stem: Which one tells someone "Don't talk!"?
questions.explanation: {不要|bú yào} + verb tells someone not to do something. Plain {不|bù} only describes ("not talking"), {没|méi} is for things that didn't happen (lesson 25), and {不是|bú shì} is "isn't".

questions.stem: How do you say "I'm ill"?
questions.explanation: Being ill is a new situation, so it takes the change-of-state {了|le}: {我|wǒ}{病|bìng}{了|le} (or {我|wǒ}{生病|shēng bìng}{了|le}). {病|bìng} isn't an adjective like {忙|máng}, so ×{很|hěn}{病|bìng} doesn't work, and {是|shì} would make it "I am an illness".

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking you?
choices: How are you going to go?
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{怎么|zěn me}{了|le}？ is "What's wrong? What's happened to you?", what people ask someone who looks ill or upset. "How did you get here?" would need a verb ({怎么|zěn me}{来|lái}), and "What are you doing?" is {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{做|zuò}{什么|shén me}？

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct for "I sleep eight hours"?
choices: {我|wǒ}{睡觉|shuì jiào}{了|le}{八|bā}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}。
questions.explanation: A length of time follows the verb, and with {睡|shuì} it goes straight after it: {睡|shuì}{八|bā}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}. {睡觉|shuì jiào} is a separable verb, so nothing can follow the whole word ×{睡觉|shuì jiào}{八|bā}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}; and a length of time doesn't go before the verb.

questions.stem: Someone bumps into you and says "{对不起|duì bu qǐ}！" What is a natural reply?
questions.explanation: {没事|méi shì} ("it's nothing, no worries") answers an apology, like {没关系|méi guān xi}. {不要|bú yào} would be "don't!" or "I don't want it", and the other two don't answer anything.

questions.stem: What does "{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{没事|méi shì}。" mean when a friend asks you out?
questions.explanation: {没事|méi shì} is "there's no matter": I've got nothing on, I'm free. It's the opposite of {我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{很|hěn}{忙|máng} (I'm busy today).

questions.stem: Type 不要 (don't) in pinyin, with the tones as they are said: ___
questions.explanation: {不|bù} changes to the second tone before a fourth tone, and {要|yào} is fourth tone, so it's said and written {不要|bú yào} in this course.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word ___天 (daytime)?
questions.explanation: Daytime is {白天|bái tiān}, with {白|bái} (white): a short stroke on top of a box with one line inside. {日|rì} has no top stroke, {百|bǎi} (hundred) has a horizontal on top, and {自|zì} has two lines inside.

questions.stem: The radical 忄 on the left of 忙 (busy) is a form of which character?
questions.explanation: 忄 is the "upright heart", the form {心|xīn} (heart, mind) takes on the left of a character. {人|rén} becomes 亻, {手|shǒu} becomes 扌 and {水|shuǐ} becomes 氵 on the left.

questions.stem: Match each character to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {病|bìng} illness (with 疒, the sickness radical), {休|xiū} rest (a person by a tree), {白|bái} white, {忙|máng} busy (with 忄). Hospital is a word, {医院|yī yuàn}, and "to sleep" is {睡|shuì}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I'm going to the hospital to see a doctor.
questions.explanation: A serial verb sentence: first the going ({去|qù}{医院|yī yuàn}), then what for ({看病|kàn bìng}). English puts "to see a doctor" last too, but Chinese never puts the place after the purpose.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I sleep eight hours at night.
questions.explanation: The time word {晚上|wǎn shang} goes before the verb (before or after the subject); the length of time {八|bā}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí} goes after {睡|shuì}. {睡觉|shuì jiào} can't take the length after it.

questions.stem: Listen. When is the speaker free?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}，{明天|míng tiān}{没事|méi shì}。 — I'm busy today; tomorrow I'm free. {没事|méi shì} here is "to have nothing on".

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker tell you to do?

audio.text: 你病了，不要去上班，在家休息吧。

questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{病|bìng}{了|le}，{不要|bú yào}{去|qù}{上班|shàng bān}，{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}{吧|ba}。 — You're ill: don't go to work, rest at home. {不要|bú yào} rules out going to work; {吧|ba} makes the suggestion.

questions.stem: Read the note: "{王|Wáng}{老师|lǎo shī}：{我|wǒ}{今天|jīn tiān}{病|bìng}{了|le}，{不|bù}{能|néng}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}。{医生|yī shēng}{说|shuō}{我|wǒ}{要|yào}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}{两|liǎng}{天|tiān}。{李明|Lǐ Míng}" How long does Li Ming have to rest?
questions.explanation: {休息|xiū xi}{两|liǎng}{天|tiān}: rest for two days. The length comes after the verb. Two hours would be {两|liǎng}{个|gè}{小时|xiǎo shí}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {忙|máng}, busy: the second tone, rising, as in {没|méi}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {医院|yī yuàn}, hospital: tones 1 + 4, high and level, then falling. {医生|yī shēng} (doctor) starts the same way.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {生病|shēng bìng}, to fall ill: tones 1 + 4. {病|bìng} falls, like {看病|kàn bìng}s second syllable.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I like singing"?
questions.explanation: Singing as an activity is {唱|chàng}{歌|gē}, verb + general object: {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}. {唱|chàng} on its own sounds unfinished, {我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{歌|gē} is "I like songs", and {喜欢|xǐ huan} comes before the activity.

questions.stem: Complete: "{这个|zhè ge}{歌|gē}{很|hěn}___。" (This song is lovely.)
questions.explanation: You listen to a song, so it's {好听|hǎo tīng}, "good to listen to". {好看|hǎo kàn} is for what you watch or look at, {好吃|hǎo chī} for food and {好玩儿|hǎo wánr} for something fun to do.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "This film is really good"?
choices: {这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{很|hěn}{好听|hǎo tīng}。
{这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{是|shì}{好看|hǎo kàn}。
{这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{好看|hǎo kàn}{很|hěn}。
{这个|zhè ge}{电影|diàn yǐng}{很|hěn}{好看|hǎo kàn}。
questions.explanation: A film is watched: {好看|hǎo kàn}. Like other adjectives it takes {很|hěn} before it and no {是|shì}. {好听|hǎo tīng} is for things you hear.

questions.stem: The teacher wants you to read some characters out loud. What does the teacher say?
questions.explanation: {读|dú} is reading aloud. {看|kàn} would be "look at" (read silently), {写|xiě} "write" and {听|tīng} "listen".

questions.stem: What does "{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{读书|dú shū}。" mean?
choices: My older brother teaches at a university.
My older brother wants to go to university.
My older brother is studying at university.
My older brother reads books out loud at university.
questions.explanation: {读书|dú shū} is "to read books", and with a school it means "to study there, to be a student": {在|zài}{大学|dà xué}{读书|dú shū}.

questions.stem: How is 不爱 (doesn't like) said?
questions.explanation: {爱|ài} is fourth tone, and {不|bù} becomes second tone before a fourth tone: {不|bú}{爱|ài}. Before other tones it stays {不|bù}: {不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}.

questions.stem: Which character completes 唱___ (to sing songs)?
questions.explanation: Song is {歌|gē}: {哥|gē} (older brother), which gives the sound, plus 欠 (an open mouth) on the right. {哥|gē} alone is the brother, {欢|huān} is the {欢|huan} of {喜欢|xǐ huan}, and {可|kě} is half of {哥|gē}.

questions.stem: Which is the character for ài, "to love"?
questions.explanation: {={爱|ài}: 爫 (a hand) on top, then 冖, then a shape like {友|yǒu} below. {友|yǒu} (friend) is only its bottom part; {受|shòu} (to receive) has 又 at the bottom, and {觉|jué} (in {觉得|jué de}) has {见|jiàn}.=}

questions.stem: What does the character 院 add in 医院 (hospital) and 电影院 (cinema)?
choices: The idea of a place or institution
questions.explanation: {院|yuàn} was first a walled courtyard; now it makes words for institutions and places: {医院|yī yuàn}, {电影院|diàn yǐng yuàn}. The doctor is {医|yī}, the shadow {影|yǐng} and the electricity {电|diàn}.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {好|hǎo} + verb is "good to …": eat, look at, listen to, play. Busy is {忙|máng}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I love watching Chinese films.
questions.explanation: {爱|ài} + the activity: {爱|ài}{看|kàn}{中国|Zhōng guó}{电影|diàn yǐng}. The describing word {中国|Zhōng guó} goes before {电影|diàn yǐng}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Let's go to the cinema to see a film this evening.
questions.explanation: The time word goes before the verb (before or after {我们|wǒ men}); then the serial verbs: go to the place, then what you do there; {吧|ba} at the end makes it a suggestion.

questions.stem: A friend says "{你|nǐ}{来|lái}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{玩|wán}{吧|ba}！" What do they mean?
choices: Come and play with my toys!
questions.explanation: {玩|wán} for adults is "to have fun, to spend time": {来|lái}{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{玩|wán}{吧|ba} is a friendly invitation to visit. {来|lái} means coming here, to the speaker's home.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker's mother love doing?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{很|hěn}{爱|ài}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}。 — My mum loves singing.

questions.stem: Listen. Where does the speaker suggest going on Saturday?

audio.text: 星期六我们去电影院吧。

questions.explanation: {星期六|xīng qī liù}{我们|wǒ men}{去|qù}{电影院|diàn yǐng yuàn}{吧|ba}。 — Let's go to the cinema on Saturday. {电影院|diàn yǐng yuàn} ends in {院|yuàn} like {医院|yī yuàn} (hospital): listen for {电影|diàn yǐng} before it.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker love?

audio.text: 我不爱看电视，我爱看书。

questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{不|bú}{爱|ài}{看|kàn}{电视|diàn shì}，{我|wǒ}{爱|ài}{看|kàn}{书|shū}。 — I don't like watching TV; I love reading. {看|kàn}{书|shū} is reading.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{爱|ài}{看|kàn}{书|shū}，{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}，{我|wǒ}{哥哥|gē ge}{爱|ài}{看|kàn}{电影|diàn yǐng}。" Who likes singing?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}: the mother. The father reads and the brother watches films.

questions.stem: How do you say "fun" in Chinese? Type the pinyin with tone marks, or the characters: ___
questions.explanation: {好玩儿|hǎo wánr}: {好|hǎo} (good) + {玩|wán} (to play), often with erhua in the north. {好玩|hǎo wán} without 儿 is also heard.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {电影|diàn yǐng}, film: tones 4 + 3. {电|diàn} falls as in {电话|diàn huà}; {影|yǐng} dips low (before a pause you may hear it rise again).

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {唱|chàng}{歌|gē}, to sing: tones 4 + 1. {歌|gē} is high and level, like {哥|gē} in {哥哥|gē ge}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {读书|dú shū}, to read, to study: tones 2 + 1, rising, then high and level.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'll give you a book"?
questions.explanation: With two objects, the person comes first and the thing second: {给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}. With {给|gěi} the thing can't come first, so ×{给|gěi}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}{你|nǐ} is wrong.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'll call you this evening"?
choices: {我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}{你|nǐ}。
{我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{你|nǐ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。
{我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。
{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。
questions.explanation: Who you call goes in a {给|gěi} phrase before the verb: {给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}. {打电话|dǎ diàn huà} can't take the person straight after it, and the subject and time come first.

questions.stem: You've met Wang Fang. How do you say "I know Wang Fang"?
questions.explanation: Knowing a person you've met is {认识|rèn shi}. {知道|zhī dào} is for facts (you might know of her without having met her). {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng} and {我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{王芳|Wáng Fāng} say you are Wang Fang.

questions.stem: Complete: "{你|nǐ} ___ {他|tā}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}{名字|míng zi}{吗|ma}？" (Do you know what his name is?)
questions.explanation: His name is a piece of information, so it's {知道|zhī dào}. {认识|rèn shi} takes a person ({你|nǐ}{认识|rèn shi}{他|tā}{吗|ma}？), and {问|wèn} would make it "Are you asking what his name is?"

questions.stem: What does 小朋友 mean?
questions.explanation: {小朋友|xiǎo péng you} is a friendly word for a child, and how adults address children: {小朋友|xiǎo péng you}，{你|nǐ}{好|hǎo}！ It doesn't mean a friend who is small. A classmate is {同学|tóng xué}.

questions.stem: Li Ming says: "{这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{女朋友|nǚ péng you}。" What is he telling you?
choices: This is my friend (who is a woman).
questions.explanation: {女朋友|nǚ péng you} is a girlfriend. A friend who is a woman is just {朋友|péng you}; a daughter is {女儿|nǚ ér}.

questions.stem: Someone you've just met says "{认识|rèn shi}{你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。" What is a natural reply?
choices: {认识|rèn shi}{你|nǐ}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。
questions.explanation: "Nice to meet you" gets "nice to meet you too": {认识|rèn shi}{你|nǐ}，{我|wǒ}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}. {不客气|bú kè qi} answers thanks and {没事|méi shì} an apology.

questions.stem: Which character fits? {请|qǐng} ___ {说|shuō}{一下|yí xià}。 (Please say it again.)
questions.explanation: "Again" is {再|zài}. {在|zài} sounds the same but means "at, in" (or the progressive {在|zài}); the characters are what tell them apart.

questions.stem: Which character completes 认___ (to know a person)?
questions.explanation: {={认识|rèn shi}: both characters have 讠 (speech) on the left, and {识|shí} has {只|zhī} on the right. {只|zhī} alone is the measure word for animals (lesson 24); {话|huà} and {说|shuō} are the other 讠 characters you know.=}

questions.stem: The radical 纟 on the left of 给 (to give) first meant…
questions.explanation: 纟 is the "silk" radical, often in characters about thread, tying and cloth. Speech is 讠, water 氵 and a person 亻.

questions.stem: How do you say "again" (as in "come again tomorrow")? Type the pinyin with its tone, or the character: ___
questions.explanation: {再|zài}, fourth tone: {明天|míng tiān}{再|zài}{来|lái}. If you write the character, take care not to write {在|zài} (at), which sounds the same.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "To know (a fact)" is {知道|zhī dào}, and "again" is {再|zài}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Mum gives the child a little money.
questions.explanation: Verb, then the person, then the thing: {给|gěi}{孩子|hái zi}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{钱|qián}. {一点儿|yì diǎnr} describes the amount of money, so it goes right before {钱|qián}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I'd like to ask the teacher a question.
questions.explanation: {想|xiǎng} before the verb, then {问|wèn} + person + thing: {问|wèn}{老师|lǎo shī}{一个|yí gè}{问题|wèn tí}.

questions.stem: Listen. When would someone say this?
choices: When saying goodbye for a long time
When thanking someone for a present
When meeting someone for the first time
questions.explanation: {认识|rèn shi}{你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。 — Nice to meet you. {认识|rèn shi} is getting to know someone.

questions.stem: Listen. What will the speaker do this evening?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{晚上|wǎn shang}{给|gěi}{你|nǐ}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà}。 — I'll call you this evening. {给|gěi}{你|nǐ} before the verb says who the call is for; it doesn't mean giving you a phone.

questions.stem: Listen. Who is Zhang Wei?

audio.text: 这是我的朋友，他叫张伟。

questions.explanation: {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{朋友|péng you}，{他|tā}{叫|jiào}{张伟|Zhāng Wěi}。 — This is my friend; his name is Zhang Wei. A boyfriend would be {男朋友|nán péng you}.

questions.stem: Read: "{李明|Lǐ Míng}{是|shì}{王芳|Wáng Fāng}{的|de}{男朋友|nán péng you}，{他|tā}{很|hěn}{爱|ài}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}。{张伟|Zhāng Wěi}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}，{很|hěn}{忙|máng}。" Who works at a company?
questions.explanation: {张伟|Zhāng Wěi}{在|zài}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}: Zhang Wei works at a company. Li Ming is Wang Fang's boyfriend, who loves singing.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {朋友|péng you}, friend: a rising second tone, then a light neutral syllable. On its own {友|yǒu} is third tone.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {高兴|gāo xìng}, glad: tones 1 + 4, high and level, then falling.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {认识|rèn shi}, to know (a person): a falling fourth tone, then a neutral syllable. {识|shí} on its own is second tone.

questions.stem: How do you say "two cats"?
questions.explanation: Animals take the measure word {只|zhī}, and before a measure word "two" is {两|liǎng}: {两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}. {个|gè} sounds wrong with animals, {二|èr} is for counting and numbers, and {本|běn} is for books.

questions.stem: Complete: "{你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ} ___ {狗|gǒu}？" (How many dogs do you have?)
questions.explanation: {几|jǐ} + measure word + noun: {几|jǐ}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}. {件|jiàn} is for clothes and matters, {本|běn} for books.

questions.stem: All four are read tā or contain it. Which one means "it" (for an animal or a thing)?
questions.explanation: {它|tā} (with the roof 宀 on top) is "it". {他|tā} is "he" (亻 person) and {她|tā} "she" (女 woman); {们|men} is the plural ending.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Some people like cats; others like dogs"?
choices: {有的|yǒu de}{人|rén}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{猫|māo}，{有的|yǒu de}{人|rén}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{狗|gǒu}。
{人|rén}{有的|yǒu de}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{猫|māo}，{人|rén}{有的|yǒu de}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{狗|gǒu}。
{有的|yǒu de}{人|rén}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{猫|māo}，{还|hái}{人|rén}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{狗|gǒu}。
{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{有的|yǒu de}{猫|māo}，{有的|yǒu de}{狗|gǒu}。
questions.explanation: {有的|yǒu de} goes before the noun, at the start, and the pair {有的|yǒu de}…，{有的|yǒu de}… contrasts two groups. {还|hái} goes before a verb, not a noun, and {有的|yǒu de} isn't used after the verb as an object.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct for "I'm going to buy some fruit"?
questions.explanation: "Some" after the verb, as part of the object, is {一些|yì xiē}. {有的|yǒu de} and {有些|yǒu xiē} describe the subject at the start of a sentence: {有的|yǒu de}{水果|shuǐ guǒ}{很|hěn}{贵|guì} (some fruit is expensive).

questions.stem: You're looking for your cat. How do you ask "Have you seen my cat?"
questions.explanation: "See" with the result, actually catching sight of it, is {看见|kàn jiàn}. {看|kàn} is only looking; {你|nǐ}{在|zài}{看|kàn}…{吗|ma}？ is "Are you looking at …?" {见|jiàn} on its own is for meeting people.

questions.stem: Wang Fang has a cat. You have one too. Which do you say?
questions.explanation: A new subject doing the same thing takes {也|yě}, before the verb: {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{有|yǒu}{猫|māo}. {还|hái} adds another thing for the same subject ({我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{猫|māo}，{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{狗|gǒu}), and neither word goes after the verb.

questions.stem: Complete: "{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}，___ {有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}。" (I have a cat, and a dog as well.)
questions.explanation: {还|hái} before the verb adds one more thing for the same person: {还|hái}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}. {和|hé} joins nouns only ({一|yì}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}{和|hé}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}) and can't start a clause; {都|dōu} would mean "all".

questions.stem: In 一只猫 (a cat), how is 一 said?
questions.explanation: {只|zhī} is first tone, and {一|yī} becomes fourth tone before tones 1, 2 and 3: {一|yì}{只|zhī}. Before a fourth tone it's yí ({一个|yí gè}), and it stays yī when counting.

questions.stem: Which character completes ___有 (and also; there's also)?
questions.explanation: {={还|hái}{有|yǒu}: {还|hái} is {不|bù} inside 辶. {这|zhè} and {边|biān} share the 辶 but have different insides, and {不|bù} alone is "not".=}

questions.stem: Which radical do {=狗=} (dog) and {=猫=} (cat) share in simplified characters?
questions.explanation: 犭, the "dog side", is in many animal names. 亻 is the person side, 口 the mouth and 宀 the roof (as in {它|tā}). (Traditional {+猫+} has 豸 instead.)

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "He" is {他|tā}, which sounds like {它|tā}. {="Only" is {只|zhǐ} (HSK 3), the other reading of simplified {只|zhī}.=}

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I have a cat, and a dog as well.
questions.explanation: Same subject, one more thing: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{猫|māo}，{还|hái}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}. {还|hái} goes before the second {有|yǒu}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Some classmates can't write this character.
questions.explanation: {有些|yǒu xiē} describes the subject, so it comes first; then {不|bú}{会|huì} before the verb, and the object last.

questions.stem: Listen. How many dogs does the speaker have?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}。 — We have two dogs at home.

questions.stem: Listen. What can the speaker hear?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{听见|tīng jiàn}{有|yǒu}{人|rén}{在|zài}{说话|shuō huà}。 — I can hear someone talking. {有|yǒu}{人|rén} is "someone".

questions.stem: Listen. What is the cat doing?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{猫|māo}{还|hái}{在|zài}{睡觉|shuì jiào}{呢|ne}。 — My cat is still asleep. {还|hái} is "still", and {在|zài}…{呢|ne} is the progressive.

questions.stem: Read: "{小黑|Xiǎo hēi}{爱|ài}{玩|wán}，{白天|bái tiān}{它|tā}{在|zài}{外边|wài bian}{玩|wán}；{大白|Dà bái}{爱|ài}{睡觉|shuì jiào}，{白天|bái tiān}{它|tā}{在|zài}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{睡|shuì}。" Where is Xiaohei in the daytime?
questions.explanation: {白天|bái tiān}{它|tā}{在|zài}{外边|wài bian}{玩|wán}: in the daytime it plays outside. It's {大白|Dà bái} who sleeps in a room.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {猫|māo}, cat: the first tone, high and level, like the sound a cat makes.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {狗|gǒu}, dog: the third tone, low and dipping.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {看见|kàn jiàn}, to see: tones 4 + 4, two falling tones. The first falls only part of the way, so the second can fall from high again.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I bought a book"?
questions.explanation: The completed-action {了|le} goes straight after the verb: {买|mǎi}{了|le}{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}. Without {了|le} it's "I'll buy a book", {了|le} never goes before the verb, and {没|méi} and {了|le} can't be used together.

questions.stem: How do you say "I didn't buy it"?
questions.explanation: Something that didn't happen is {没|méi} + verb, and the {了|le} goes: {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{买|mǎi}. {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{买|mǎi} is "I won't buy it", and {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{买|mǎi}{了|le} "I'm not buying it after all" (change of state).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I didn't go to class yesterday"?
choices: {昨天|zuó tiān}{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}{了|le}。
{昨天|zuó tiān}{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{去|qù}{上课|shàng kè}{了|le}。
questions.explanation: {昨天|zuó tiān} says when; {没|méi}{去|qù} says it didn't happen, with no {了|le}. {不|bù} is for now, habits and the future, so it doesn't fit yesterday.

questions.stem: A friend asks "{你|nǐ}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{了|le}{吗|ma}？" You haven't eaten yet. What do you say?
questions.explanation: "Not yet" is {还|hái}{没|méi}({吃|chī}){呢|ne}. {吃|chī}{了|le} means you have eaten, {不|bù}{吃|chī} that you won't eat, and ×{没|méi}{吃|chī}{了|le} mixes {没|méi} with {了|le}.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT correct?
choices: {去年|qù nián}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{中学生|zhōng xué shēng}。
{去年|qù nián}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{了|le}{中学生|zhōng xué shēng}。
questions.explanation: {了|le} marks a completed action, not the past in general. Being a student is a state, so {是|shì} takes no {了|le}: {去年|qù nián}{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{中学生|zhōng xué shēng}. Going to Beijing is an action: {去|qù}{了|le}, or {没|méi}{去|qù}.

questions.stem: Which of these sounds unfinished if you say it on its own?
questions.explanation: Verb + {了|le} + a bare object sounds as if more is coming ("I bought books, and then…"). Give an amount ({两|liǎng}{本|běn}{书|shū}) or put {了|le} at the end ({我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{书|shū}{了|le}).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "When I was seven, we had a dog"?
choices: {我|wǒ}{七|qī}{岁|suì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}。
{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}，{我|wǒ}{七|qī}{岁|suì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}。
{我|wǒ}{七|qī}{岁|suì}{的|de}{时间|shí jiān}，{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}。
{我|wǒ}{七|qī}{岁|suì}{时候|shí hou}{的|de}，{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}{只|zhī}{狗|gǒu}。
questions.explanation: "When…" is phrase + {的|de}{时候|shí hou}, and it comes first, like a time word. {时间|shí jiān} is time as an amount, and {的|de} goes before {时候|shí hou}. Having a dog is a state, so no {了|le}.

questions.stem: Complete: "{我|wǒ}{没有|méi yǒu}___。" (I don't have time.)
questions.explanation: Time as something you have or don't have is {时间|shí jiān}. {时候|shí hou} is a point in time ("when"), and {小时|xiǎo shí} an hour.

questions.stem: What does "{我|wǒ}{不|bú}{去|qù}{了|le}。" mean?
questions.explanation: This is lesson 20's change-of-state {了|le} at the end: the plan has changed, so "I'm not going any more". "I didn't go" is {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}, with no {了|le}.

questions.stem: How do you say "last year" in Chinese? Type the pinyin with tone marks, or the characters: ___
questions.explanation: {去年|qù nián}, "the gone year". "Yesterday" uses another word, {昨天|zuó tiān}; this year is {今年|jīn nián} and next year {明年|míng nián}.

questions.stem: Which character completes 问___ (question; problem)?
questions.explanation: {题|tí} = {是|shì} (the sound part) + 页 (head). {是|shì} and 页 are only its parts; {提|tí} sounds the same but has 扌 (hand) and means "to lift" (HSK 3).

questions.stem: Which character completes 时___ (the time when)?
questions.explanation: {候|hòu} has a short vertical stroke between 亻 and the right side. {侯|hóu} (a surname) lacks it; 喉 (throat) and 猴 (monkey) have 口 and 犭 instead of 亻.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I bought two Chinese books.
questions.explanation: Verb + {了|le} + amount + noun: {买|mǎi}{了|le}{两|liǎng}{本|běn}{中文|Zhōng wén}{书|shū}.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I haven't eaten yet.
questions.explanation: "Not yet" is {还|hái}{没|méi} + verb, often with {呢|ne} at the end. There's no {了|le}: the eating hasn't happened.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the speaker do yesterday?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{没|méi}{去|qù}{上班|shàng bān}。 — I didn't go to work yesterday. Listen for {没|méi} before the verb.

questions.stem: Listen. How old was the speaker when they started primary school?

audio.text: 我七岁的时候上了小学。

questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{七|qī}{岁|suì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{上|shàng}{了|le}{小学|xiǎo xué}。 — I started primary school when I was seven.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking?
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{吃|chī}{饭|fàn}{了|le}{没有|méi yǒu}？ — Have you eaten (or not)? …{了|le}{没有|méi yǒu}？ asks whether something has happened. It's also a friendly greeting around mealtimes.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{七|qī}{岁|suì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}{上|shàng}{了|le}{小学|xiǎo xué}。{十三|shí sān}{岁|suì}{的|de}{时候|shí hou}，{我|wǒ}{上|shàng}{了|le}{中学|zhōng xué}。{去年|qù nián}{我|wǒ}{上|shàng}{了|le}{大学|dà xué}。" When did the writer start university?
questions.explanation: {去年|qù nián}{我|wǒ}{上|shàng}{了|le}{大学|dà xué}: last year I started university. {上|shàng} + a school is "to start (going to) it".

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {问题|wèn tí}, question, problem: tones 4 + 2, falling, then rising. {没|méi}{问题|wèn tí}: no problem.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {小学|xiǎo xué}, primary school: tones 3 + 2. Before another tone, the third tone stays low (a "half third").

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {时候|shí hou}, (the) time when: a rising second tone, then a neutral syllable. On its own {候|hòu} is fourth tone.

questions.stem: What is {太极拳|tài jí quán}?
choices: A slow, flowing exercise that is also a martial art
A board game played at stone tables
questions.explanation: {太极拳|tài jí quán} (tai chi) combines relaxed, circular movements with calm breathing. "To do tai chi" is {打|dǎ}{太极拳|tài jí quán}.

questions.stem: According to UNESCO, where and when did tai chi begin?
choices: In Wenxian County, Henan, in the mid-seventeenth century
In Shanghai, in the twentieth century
questions.explanation: UNESCO's 2020 listing of Taijiquan says it began in the mid-1600s in Wenxian County ({温县|Wēn Xiàn}), Henan. Weifang and 1984 are the kite festival; the 1990s are when water calligraphy spread.

questions.stem: Who mostly takes part in {广场舞|guǎng chǎng wǔ} (square dancing)?
questions.explanation: Square dancing is above all a pastime of middle-aged and retired women, who dance in rows in squares and parks, in the early morning and in the evening.

questions.stem: How do you say "to fly a kite"?
questions.explanation: {放|fàng}{风筝|fēng zheng}: {放|fàng} is "to let go, release". {打|dǎ} goes with tai chi ({打|dǎ}{太极拳|tài jí quán}) and {踢|tī} with the shuttlecock ({踢|tī}{毽子|jiàn zi}).

questions.stem: What is {地书|dì shū}?
choices: Writing characters on the ground with a brush and water
Reading a map in the park
questions.explanation: {地书|dì shū}, "ground writing": large characters written in water on the paving stones, which dry and disappear after a few minutes.

questions.stem: Which city calls itself the kite capital of the world and holds a kite festival in April?
questions.explanation: {潍坊|Wéi fāng} (Weifang) in Shandong has held its international kite festival since 1984.

questions.stem: What does {遛|liù}{鸟|niǎo} describe?
choices: Taking a caged songbird out for a walk
questions.explanation: Bird owners, often older men in Beijing, carry their songbirds to the park in cages, swing them gently as they walk and hang them in the trees so the birds can sing together.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the park like at six in the morning?

audio.text: 早上六点，公园里人很多。

questions.explanation: {早上|zǎo shang}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}，{公园|gōng yuán}{里|lǐ}{人|rén}{很|hěn}{多|duō}。 — At six in the morning there are lots of people in the park.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker's father do every morning?

audio.text: 我爸爸每天早上打太极拳。

questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{每天|měi tiān}{早上|zǎo shang}{打|dǎ}{太极拳|tài jí quán}。 — My dad does tai chi every morning.

questions.stem: A notice in the park says: "{太极拳|tài jí quán}：{星期一|xīng qī yī}{到|dào}{星期五|xīng qī wǔ}，{早上|zǎo shang}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}". When is tai chi?
questions.explanation: {星期一|xīng qī yī}{到|dào}{星期五|xīng qī wǔ}: Monday to Friday; {早上|zǎo shang}{六|liù}{点|diǎn}{半|bàn}: half past six in the morning.

questions.stem: Read: "{昨天|zuó tiān}{爷爷|yé ye}{没|méi}{去|qù}{公园|gōng yuán}，{他|tā}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{冷|lěng}，{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}{了|le}{一|yì}{天|tiān}。" Why didn't Grandpa go to the park yesterday?
questions.explanation: {他|tā}{有点儿|yǒu diǎnr}{冷|lěng}: he felt a bit cold, so he rested at home for the day. {没|méi}{去|qù} says he didn't go.

questions.stem: Complete: "{有的|yǒu de}{人|rén}{唱|chàng}{歌|gē}，___ {人|rén}{跳舞|tiào wǔ}。" (Some people sing, others dance.)
questions.explanation: {有的|yǒu de}…，{有的|yǒu de}… contrasts two groups: some…, others…. {还|hái}, {也|yě} and {都|dōu} go before a verb, not a noun.

questions.stem: What does a character's radical usually give you?
questions.explanation: The radical is usually the meaning part ({说|shuō} has 讠, speech); the sound part is the other component. It's a hint, not a rule: {很|hěn} has 彳 "step", which has nothing to do with "very".

questions.stem: Which character has the "speech" radical 讠?
questions.explanation: {说|shuō} (to speak) has 讠. {吃|chī} has 口 (mouth), {你|nǐ} has 亻 (person) and {她|tā} has 女 (woman).

questions.stem: 茶 (tea), 菜 (vegetables) and 苹 (in 苹果, apple) all have 艹 on top. What does it suggest?
questions.explanation: 艹 is the grass radical, found in many words for plants: {茶|chá}, {菜|cài}, {苹果|píng guǒ}.

questions.stem: How many Kangxi radicals are there?
questions.explanation: 214, the system of the Zihui (1615) kept by the Kangxi Dictionary (1716). 540 is the Shuowen Jiezi's number, and 201 main radicals with 100 side forms is the 2009 mainland table.

questions.stem: What does the mainland Table of Chinese Character Radicals of 2009 (GF 0011-2009) contain?
questions.explanation: {汉字部首表|Hàn zì bù shǒu biǎo}: 201 main radicals, with 100 side forms such as 亻 and 氵 listed under their main radicals 人 and 水.

questions.stem: {=You're looking up simplified 课 in a paper dictionary. Its radical 讠 has 2 strokes; the rest, 果, has 8. Where do you look in the character index?=}
choices: Under 10 strokes in the pinyin index
questions.explanation: {=Find the radical, then count the strokes outside it: 讠 + 8. The total (10) is what a stroke-count index uses, not the radical index.=}

questions.stem: 忙 has 6 strokes, and its radical 忄 has 3. How many strokes are outside the radical? ___
questions.explanation: 6 − 3 = 3: the right side, {亡|wáng}, has three strokes. In the dictionary, {忙|máng} is under 忄 + 3.

questions.stem: Which statement about mainland and Taiwan stroke order is true?
choices: Taiwan writes every character from right to left.
The mainland has no official stroke order.
They differ in some characters and parts, such as 必 and 忄.
questions.explanation: Both have official standards, which agree on most characters but differ in some: the last two strokes of {必|bì}, the order of 忄, the strokes of 艹 (3 or 4) and the start of 馬.

questions.stem: Which stroke order do this course and its tracing pads use?
choices: Mainland order, also when traditional characters are shown
questions.explanation: The stroke data (Make Me a Hanzi) follows mainland order, and the course uses it for both scripts.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker want to buy?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{买|mǎi}{一|yì}{本|běn}{字典|zì diǎn}。 — I'd like to buy a dictionary. {字典|zì diǎn}: a dictionary of characters.

questions.stem: Listen. Which radical is the speaker talking about?
questions.explanation: {这|zhè}{个|gè}{字|zì}{的|de}{部首|bù shǒu}{是|shì}{口|kǒu}。 — This character's radical is 口 (mouth). {部首|bù shǒu} is "radical".

questions.stem: Read: "{书店|shū diàn}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{两|liǎng}{本|běn}{字典|zì diǎn}：{一|yì}{本|běn}{很|hěn}{大|dà}，{很|hěn}{贵|guì}；{一|yì}{本|běn}{很|hěn}{小|xiǎo}，{很|hěn}{便宜|pián yi}。{我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{小|xiǎo}{的|de}。" Which dictionary did the writer buy?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{小|xiǎo}{的|de}: I bought the small one ({小|xiǎo}{的|de}, "the small one"), which was cheap.

questions.stem: Read: "{我|wǒ}{查|chá}{了|le}{字典|zì diǎn}：{它|tā}{的|de}{部首|bù shǒu}{是|shì}“{三点水|sān diǎn shuǐ}”，{是|shì}{水|shuǐ}{的|de}{意思|yì si}。" ({查|chá}: to look up; {三点水|sān diǎn shuǐ}: "three-dot water", the name of 氵; {意思|yì si}: meaning) What does the radical mean?
questions.explanation: {是|shì}{水|shuǐ}{的|de}{意思|yì si}: it means water. 氵 is the side form of {水|shuǐ}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Where are you going?"
questions.explanation: A question word stays where the answer goes: {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{商店|shāng diàn} → {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}？ It never moves to the front as in English, and it never takes {吗|ma}: {你|nǐ}{去|qù}{哪儿|nǎr}{吗|ma}？ would mean "Are you going anywhere?"

questions.stem: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{美国人|Měi guó rén}，{你|nǐ}___？ Choose the word for the blank (I'm American. And you?).
questions.explanation: {呢|ne} after a pronoun asks the same question about someone else: {你|nǐ}{呢|ne}？ (and you?). {你|nǐ}{吗|ma}？ isn't a sentence, {你|nǐ}{吧|ba}？ would guess something, and {了|le} marks a change or a completed action.

questions.stem: {这|zhè}{本|běn}{书|shū}___ {钱|qián}？ Choose the word for the blank (How much is this book?).
questions.explanation: Prices are asked with {多少|duō shao}{钱|qián}. {几|jǐ} needs a measure word after it ({几块|jǐ kuài}{钱|qián} is possible, {几|jǐ}{钱|qián} is not), {什么|shén me}{钱|qián} means "what kind of money", and {怎么|zěn me} asks how to do something.

questions.stem: Which question is correct?
questions.explanation: An A-not-A question is the adjective, {不|bù}, then the adjective again: {忙不忙|máng bu máng}. It takes no {很|hěn} and no {吗|ma}: the A-not-A pair already makes it a question.

questions.stem: “{你|nǐ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}{吗|ma}？” Which is the natural short answer for "yes"?
questions.explanation: Chinese answers "yes" by repeating the verb of the question: {喜欢|xǐ huan}。 ("no" would be {不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}。). {是|shì} only answers questions with {是|shì} in them, {有|yǒu} answers {有|yǒu} questions, and {对不起|duì bu qǐ} is "sorry".

questions.stem: “{你|nǐ}{不|bù}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}{吗|ma}？” You don't drink tea. Which answer says so?
questions.explanation: {对|duì} agrees with the sentence that was said ("you don't drink tea"): {对|duì}，{我|wǒ}{不|bù}{喝|hē}。 — Right, I don't. English says "No, I don't" here, but {对|duì}，{我|wǒ}{喝|hē} contradicts itself, {吗|ma} doesn't end an answer, and {没有|méi yǒu} denies having or a completed action.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker want to know?
questions.explanation: The speaker said {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{哪国人|nǎ guó rén}？ — Where are you from? (literally "you are which-country person?"). Your name would be {你|nǐ}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}{名字|míng zi}？, your age {你|nǐ}{多大|duō dà}？

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{呢|ne}？ — {呢|ne} after a noun on its own asks where it is. "Is this my phone?" would be {这|zhè}{是|shì}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{吗|ma}？, and "whose" is {谁|shéi}{的|de}.

questions.stem: Listen to the question. Which reply fits?
questions.explanation: The question was {你|nǐ}{明天|míng tiān}{来不来|lái bu lái}？ — Are you coming tomorrow? An A-not-A question is answered with the verb: {来|lái} (yes) or {不来|bù lái} (no). {是|shì} answers only {是|shì} questions; the other two answer other questions.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker think?
choices: The listener is probably Teacher Wang.
questions.explanation: The speaker said {您|nín}{是|shì}{王老师|Wáng lǎo shī}{吧|ba}？ — You're Teacher Wang, aren't you? {吧|ba} checks a guess the speaker thinks is right. With {吗|ma} it would be an open question.

questions.stem: Which is the pinyin of 哪儿 (where?)?
questions.explanation: {哪儿|nǎr} has the third tone, like {哪|nǎ} (which). nàr, with the fourth tone, is {那儿|nàr} (there): the tone is the only difference in sound between "where?" and "there".

questions.stem: In the question 你去不去？ (Are you going?), how is the 不 in the middle said?
questions.explanation: In an A-not-A question the {不|bu} in the middle is said lightly, with the neutral tone: {去不去|qù bu qù}. On its own before a fourth tone it would be bú ({不去|bú qù}), but inside the A-not-A pair it loses its tone.

questions.stem: Which character makes the word "where?": ___儿
questions.explanation: {哪儿|nǎr} (where?) is written with 哪, which has the "mouth" radical 口 on the left, like other question and particle characters ({吗|ma}, {呢|ne}, {吧|ba}). 那 without 口 is {那儿|nàr} (there). 都 ({都|dōu}, all) has 阝 on the right.

questions.stem: Which character means "who"?
questions.explanation: 谁 is {谁|shéi}, who. All four have the speech radical {=讠=} (言 in traditional characters) on the left: 话 is in {电话|diàn huà} (phone), 说 is {说|shuō} (to speak) and 请 is {请|qǐng} (please).

questions.stem: Build the question in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Where does your older sister work?
questions.explanation: Start from the statement {我|wǒ}{姐姐|jiě jie}{在|zài}{医院|yī yuàn}{工作|gōng zuò} and put {哪儿|nǎr} in the place of the answer: {你|nǐ}{姐姐|jiě jie}{在|zài}{哪儿|nǎr}{工作|gōng zuò}？ The place with {在|zài} comes before the verb, and a question word never takes {吗|ma}.

questions.stem: Build the question in Chinese, without {吗|ma}.
questions.prompt: Are you coming tomorrow?
questions.explanation: The A-not-A pair {来不来|lái bu lái} makes the question, so there is no {吗|ma}. The time word goes before the verb, after the subject or before it: {你|nǐ}{明天|míng tiān}{来不来|lái bu lái}？ or {明天|míng tiān}{你|nǐ}{来不来|lái bu lái}？

{你|nǐ}{几点|jǐ diǎn}{有|yǒu}{时间|shí jiān}？ — What time do you have time (are you free)? Li Ming already says tomorrow is Saturday, and {怎么样|zěn me yàng}？ after the suggestion asks "how about it?", not which film.

questions.stem:
Read the conversation.

A: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{大卫|Dà wèi}{吧|ba}？
B: {不是|bú shì}，{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{他|tā}{弟弟|dì di}。{大卫|Dà wèi}{在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}。

Which is true?
questions.explanation: A guesses with {吧|ba} ("You're David, aren't you?"), and the guess is wrong: {不是|bú shì}，{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{他|tā}{弟弟|dì di} — No, I'm his younger brother. David is {在|zài}{学校|xué xiào}, at school.

questions.stem: Type the missing word, in characters or pinyin: {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng}___？ (Are you a student?)
questions.explanation: {吗|ma} at the end turns the statement {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{学生|xué sheng} (you're a student) into a yes/no question. It has the neutral tone, so its pinyin has no tone mark.

questions.stem: Match each question word to what it asks about.
questions.explanation: {谁|shéi} who, {什么|shén me} what, {哪儿|nǎr} where, {几|jǐ} how many (a small number, with a measure word), {怎么|zěn me} how. "Why" is {为什么|wèi shén me}, an HSK 2 word.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {什么|shén me}, what: a rising second tone, then a light neutral syllable. In a question it carries the stress, but its tones don't change.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {手机|shǒu jī}, mobile phone: a low third tone, then a high level first tone (3+1), as in {我|wǒ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{呢|ne}？

questions.stem: You see this sign over a door: {出口|chū kǒu}. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: {出口|chū kǒu} is {出|chū} (out) + {口|kǒu} (mouth, opening): the way out. The entrance is {入口|rù kǒu}, toilets are {洗手间|xǐ shǒu jiān}, and a taxi rank says {出租车|chū zū chē}.

The shop is open from 9 a.m. ({上午|shàng wǔ}9:00) to 6 p.m. ({下午|xià wǔ}6:00), and {星期一|xīng qī yī}{休息|xiū xi} means it's closed on Mondays. Tuesday at 10 is the only time inside the opening hours on an open day.

The price of dumplings is for ten (10{个|gè}): twenty dumplings are 2 × 18 = 36 yuan, and two cups of tea 2 × 5 = 10 yuan, so 46 yuan ({四十六块|sì shí liù kuài}). 23 is one plate and one tea; 36 forgets the tea.

choices: He Ping is a teacher at a school.
He Ping is a doctor at a hospital.
He Ping works at a company called He Ping.
He Ping is a patient at a hospital.
questions.explanation: The first line is the workplace, {大明|Dà míng}{医院|yī yuàn} (Daming Hospital, a made-up name), the biggest line is the name, {何平|Hé Píng}, and the next is the job: {医生|yī shēng}, doctor. A teacher would be {老师|lǎo shī}.

questions.stem:
Read the timetable.

{车次|chē cì}  {开车|kāi chē}  {到|dào}
G123  07:00  11:30
G456  08:00  12:40
G789  10:00  14:30

You must arrive by 12:00. Which train can you take?
questions.explanation: On a train timetable {开车|kāi chē} is the departure time and {到|dào} the arrival. Only G123 arrives ({到|dào}) before 12:00, at 11:30; G456 arrives at 12:40 and G789 at 14:30.

questions.stem:
Read the note.

{李明|Lǐ Míng}：
{我|wǒ}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}{了|le}，{下午|xià wǔ}{三点|sān diǎn}{回来|huí lái}。 {大卫|Dà wèi}

Where is David now?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{去|qù}{超市|chāo shì}{买|mǎi}{东西|dōng xi}{了|le} — I've gone to the supermarket to buy some things. He'll be back at three in the afternoon. A note starts with the reader's name and a colon and ends with the writer's. ({回来|huí lái}, to come back, is an HSK 2 word.)

questions.stem: A menu says 15.50{元|yuán}. How do you say the price?
choices: {十五元五十|shí wǔ yuán wǔ shí}
{十五点五块|shí wǔ diǎn wǔ kuài}
questions.explanation: Prices are written in {元|yuán} but said with {块|kuài}, and the tenths after the point follow {块|kuài}: {十五块五|shí wǔ kuài wǔ}. Digits are read one by one only in phone and room numbers, and {点|diǎn} isn't used inside a price.

questions.stem: On a name card, the mobile number starts with 1: 139…. How is the 1 said?
questions.explanation: In phone numbers, room numbers and other strings of digits, 1 is said yāo, so it can't be confused with 7 ({七|qī}): 139 is yāo sān jiǔ. In counting it's yī.

questions.stem: Which character is on the door of the women's toilets?
questions.explanation: 女 is {女|nǚ}, female. 男 ({男|nán}, male: "field" 田 + "strength" 力) is on the men's door. 好 and 妈 contain 女 but are other words: {好|hǎo} good, {妈妈|mā ma} mum.

questions.stem: Which character completes the sign for "exit": ___口
questions.explanation: {出口|chū kǒu}, exit, uses 出 (out), the character in {出租车|chū zū chē}. 去 is {去|qù} (to go); 山 (mountain) and 土 (earth) look a little like parts of 出 but aren't it.

questions.stem: Which character completes the sign for "entrance": ___口
questions.explanation: {入口|rù kǒu}, entrance, uses 入 (to enter): its long stroke goes down to the right, with the short left stroke leaning on it. 人 ({人|rén}, person) has the long stroke on the left; 八 ({八|bā}, eight) has two separate strokes.

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement. What are people asked not to do?
questions.explanation: {请不要|qǐng bú yào}{在|zài}{这儿|zhèr}{打电话|dǎ diàn huà} — Please don't make phone calls here. {请不要|qǐng bú yào} + verb is the polite "please don't" of signs and announcements.

questions.stem: Listen. How much is it?
questions.explanation: {饺子|jiǎo zi}{十个|shí gè}{十八块|shí bā kuài} — dumplings: ten for eighteen kuai. The number with {个|gè} is how many; the number with {块|kuài} is the price.

questions.stem: Listen. When does the train leave?
questions.explanation: {火车|huǒ chē}{早上|zǎo shang}{七点|qī diǎn}{开车|kāi chē} — The train leaves at seven in the morning. On trains and buses {开车|kāi chē} means "to depart". {早上|zǎo shang} is early morning; 7 p.m. would be {晚上|wǎn shang}{七点|qī diǎn}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true?
choices: The bookshop is closed on Mondays.
The bookshop opens at one o'clock.
The bookshop closes at one o'clock.
questions.explanation: {这个|zhè ge}{书店|shū diàn}{星期一|xīng qī yī}{休息|xiū xi} — This bookshop is closed on Mondays. {休息|xiū xi} (to rest) on a shop means "closed". {星期一|xīng qī yī} is Monday, not one o'clock ({一点|yī diǎn}).

questions.stem: Which is the pinyin of 元 (yuan, the word for money on menus and labels)?
questions.explanation: {元|yuán} has the second tone. yuàn is the second syllable of {医院|yī yuàn} (hospital), a different character with the fourth tone.

questions.stem: Build the sign in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Please don't eat here.
questions.explanation: {请|qǐng} comes first, then {不要|bú yào} (don't), then the place with {在|zài} before the verb, then the verb and its object: {请不要|qǐng bú yào}{在|zài}{这儿|zhèr}{吃|chī}{东西|dōng xi}。 {没|méi} denies the past, not a request.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: The bookshop is closed on Mondays.
questions.explanation: A time word goes before the verb, either after the subject or at the very start: {书店|shū diàn}{星期一|xīng qī yī}{休息|xiū xi}。 or {星期一|xīng qī yī}{书店|shū diàn}{休息|xiū xi}。 Never at the end, as in English.

questions.stem: A label says 20{元|yuán}. Type the number as you'd say it, in characters or pinyin: ___ {块|kuài}
questions.explanation: 20{元|yuán} is said {二十块|èr shí kuài}. {二|èr} is right inside a number such as 20; {两|liǎng} is for a single "two" before a measure word ({两块|liǎng kuài}, 2 yuan).

questions.stem: Match each sign to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {出口|chū kǒu} exit ("out-opening"), {入口|rù kǒu} entrance, {男|nán} men, {女|nǚ} women, {推|tuī} push. "Pull" would be {拉|lā}; both have the hand radical 扌.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {元|yuán}, the written word for yuan on menus and labels: the second tone, rising.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {超市|chāo shì}, supermarket: a high level first tone, then a falling fourth tone (1+4).

questions.stem: Listen to the question. Which reply fits?
questions.explanation: The question was {你|nǐ}{今年|jīn nián}{多大|duō dà}？ — How old are you (this year)? An age with {岁|suì} answers it. A name answers {你|nǐ}{叫|jiào}{什么|shén me}{名字|míng zi}？, a country {你|nǐ}{是|shì}{哪国人|nǎ guó rén}？, and {两点|liǎng diǎn} {几点|jǐ diǎn}？

questions.stem: Listen to the question. Which reply fits?
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{做|zuò}{什么|shén me}{工作|gōng zuò}？ — What do you do (for work)? Answer with your job: {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}。 The others answer "where are you?", "what do you like doing?" and "can you…?".

questions.stem: Listen to the question. Which reply fits?
questions.explanation: {你|nǐ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{几口人|jǐ kǒu rén}？ — How many people are there in your family? The answer repeats the measure word {口|kǒu}: {五口人|wǔ kǒu rén}。 {三个|sān gè} drops the right measure word, and {在|zài}{北京|Běi jīng} answers "where?".

questions.stem: Listen. When does the speaker's class finish?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{四点|sì diǎn}{下课|xià kè} — My class finishes at four. {四|sì} (4) has a falling fourth tone; {十|shí} (10) rises and starts with the curled-back sh. Listen for the tone and the start of the syllable.

questions.stem: Listen. What time is he coming tomorrow?
questions.explanation: {他|tā}{明天|míng tiān}{十点|shí diǎn}{来|lái} — He's coming at ten tomorrow. {十|shí} rises (second tone); {四|sì} (4) would fall. The time goes before the verb.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true?

audio.text: 我不喜欢喝茶，我喜欢喝水。

choices: The speaker likes tea and water.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}，{我|wǒ}{喜欢|xǐ huan}{喝|hē}{水|shuǐ} — I don't like tea; I like water. The short {不|bù} before {喜欢|xǐ huan} turns the first half round: always listen for it.

questions.stem: Listen to the short conversation. Where is the second speaker from?

audio.text: 你是美国人吗？不是，我是英国人。

questions.explanation: "{你|nǐ}{是|shì}{美国人|Měi guó rén}{吗|ma}？" "{不是|bú shì}，{我|wǒ}{是|shì}{英国人|Yīng guó rén}。" — Are you American? No, I'm British. The answer starts with {不是|bú shì}, so the guess in the question is wrong.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker want?
questions.explanation: {请|qǐng}{再说|zài shuō}{一下|yí xià} — Please say it again. {再|zài} (again) comes before the verb {说|shuō}. "More slowly" would be {请|qǐng}{慢|màn}{一点儿|yì diǎnr}{说|shuō}, and goodbye is {再见|zài jiàn}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which reply fits?
questions.explanation: {认识|rèn shi}{你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng} — Nice to meet you. The reply is {我|wǒ}{也|yě}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng} (me too). {没关系|méi guān xi} answers an apology and {不客气|bú kè qi} answers thanks.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker want to do?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{想|xiǎng}{卖|mài}{我|wǒ}{的|de}{车|chē} — I'd like to sell my car. {卖|mài} (sell) has the falling fourth tone; {买|mǎi} (buy) dips with the third tone. {我|wǒ}{的|de}{车|chē} (my car) is a clue too: you sell your own car.

questions.stem: How do you ask "What's your mobile number?"
choices: {你|nǐ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{号|hào}{是|shì}{什么|shén me}？
{你|nǐ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{号|hào}{是|shì}{多少|duō shao}？
questions.explanation: Numbers, including phone numbers, are asked with {多少|duō shao}: {你|nǐ}{的|de}{手机|shǒu jī}{号|hào}{是|shì}{多少|duō shao}？ {什么|shén me} sounds wrong to Chinese ears here, {几|jǐ} needs a measure word, and the last question only asks whether you have a phone.

questions.stem: Someone asks {你|nǐ}{会|huì}{说|shuō}{汉语|Hàn yǔ}{吗|ma}？ Which is the natural, modest answer?
questions.explanation: {会|huì}{一点儿|yì diǎnr} — I can a little. Answer a {会|huì} question with {会|huì}. {是|shì} doesn't answer it, {很|hěn} can't go before a noun, and {我|wǒ}{是|shì}{汉语|Hàn yǔ} says "I am Chinese (the language)".

questions.stem: Someone says {对不起|duì bu qǐ} to you. What do you answer?
questions.explanation: {对不起|duì bu qǐ} (sorry) is answered with {没关系|méi guān xi} (it doesn't matter). {不客气|bú kè qi} answers {谢谢|xiè xie} (thanks).

questions.stem: You didn't catch what someone said. What do you say?
choices: {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听见|tīng jiàn}。
questions.explanation: {对不起|duì bu qǐ}，{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{听见|tīng jiàn} — Sorry, I didn't catch (hear) that. {听见|tīng jiàn} is hearing something, and {没|méi} denies that it happened. {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{听|tīng} would mean "I won't listen".

questions.stem: Which is the pinyin of 不客气 (you're welcome), as this course writes it?
questions.explanation: {不|bú} changes to the second tone before a fourth tone (kè), so it's bú kè qi; {气|qi} is neutral in this word. kě (third tone) is the syllable of {可以|kě yǐ}.

questions.stem: Which character completes the word 认___ (to know a person)?
questions.explanation: {认识|rèn shi} is written 认识: both characters have the speech radical {=讠=} (言 in traditional characters). 只 ({只|zhī}), 是 ({是|shì}) and 时 (in {时间|shí jiān}) sound similar but mean other things.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Chinese.
questions.prompt: I'm twenty-five this year.
questions.explanation: An age is a noun predicate: no {是|shì} is needed. The time word {今年|jīn nián} goes after the subject or at the start: {我|wǒ}{今年|jīn nián}{二十五岁|èr shí wǔ suì}。

questions.stem: Build the request in Chinese.
questions.prompt: Please say it again.
questions.explanation: {再|zài} (again) goes before the verb, and {一下|yí xià} after it softens the request: {请|qǐng}{再说|zài shuō}{一下|yí xià}。 {在|zài} sounds the same but means "at".

questions.stem:
Read the introduction.

{大家好|dà jiā hǎo}！{我|wǒ}{叫|jiào}{李明|Lǐ Míng}，{是|shì}{中国人|Zhōng guó rén}。{我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{三口人|sān kǒu rén}：{爸爸|bà ba}、{妈妈|mā ma}{和|hé}{我|wǒ}。{我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{是|shì}{医生|yī shēng}，{我|wǒ}{妈妈|mā ma}{在|zài}{一家|yì jiā}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}。

Who is a doctor?
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{爸爸|bà ba}{是|shì}{医生|yī shēng} — My dad is a doctor. His mum works at a company ({在|zài}{一家|yì jiā}{公司|gōng sī}{工作|gōng zuò}), and there are three in the family.

questions.stem: Someone says {谢谢|xiè xie} to you. Type the usual reply, in characters or pinyin: ___
questions.explanation: {不客气|bú kè qi} — you're welcome (literally "don't be polite"). It's written bú kè qi in this course, because {不|bù} is said with the second tone before a fourth tone.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {卖|mài}, to sell: the fourth tone, falling. {买|mǎi}, to buy, has the third tone: listen for the fall.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tone is it?
questions.explanation: {买|mǎi}, to buy: the third tone, low and dipping. {卖|mài}, to sell, falls with the fourth tone.

questions.stem: Listen. Which tones are the two syllables?
questions.explanation: {高兴|gāo xìng}, glad: a high level first tone, then a falling fourth tone (1+4), as in {认识|rèn shi}{你|nǐ}{很|hěn}{高兴|gāo xìng}。

questions.stem: Which sentence means "She's busy."?
questions.explanation: An adjective is a predicate by itself, with a plain {很|hěn} before it: {她|tā}{很|hěn}{忙|máng}。 English "is" tempts learners to add {是|shì}, but {是|shì} links two nouns ({她|tā}{是|shì}{老师|lǎo shī}).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Today isn't Monday."?
choices: {今天|jīn tiān}{不|bù}{星期一|xīng qī yī}。
{今天|jīn tiān}{不是|bú shì}{星期一|xīng qī yī}。
{今天|jīn tiān}{没|méi}{星期一|xīng qī yī}。
{今天|jīn tiān}{星期一|xīng qī yī}{不|bù}。
questions.explanation: {今天|jīn tiān}{星期一|xīng qī yī} (today is Monday) needs no {是|shì}, but its negative does: {今天|jīn tiān}{不是|bú shì}{星期一|xīng qī yī}。 {不|bù} can't go straight before a noun, and {没|méi} is for {有|yǒu} and the past.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm resting at home tomorrow."?
questions.explanation: Time and place both come before the verb, time first: {我|wǒ}{明天|míng tiān}{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi}。 ({明天|míng tiān} could also open the sentence.) Putting {在|zài}{家|jiā} or {明天|míng tiān} after the verb copies English word order.

questions.stem: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{三|sān}___ {书|shū}。 Choose the measure word (I have three books).
questions.explanation: Books take {本|běn}: {三本|sān běn}{书|shū}. {个|gè} is the general measure word, but not for books; {件|jiàn} is for clothes and matters, {只|zhī} for animals.

questions.stem: {我|wǒ}{家|jiā}{有|yǒu}{一|yì}___ {猫|māo}。 Choose the measure word (We have a cat at home).
questions.explanation: Animals take {只|zhī}: {一只|yì zhī}{猫|māo}, {两只|liǎng zhī}{狗|gǒu}. {口|kǒu} counts the people in a family, {本|běn} books and {块|kuài} money or pieces.

questions.stem: {我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}___ {个|gè}{弟弟|dì di}。 Choose the word for "two".
questions.explanation: Before a measure word, "two" is {两|liǎng}: {两个|liǎng gè}{弟弟|dì di}. {二|èr} is for counting and inside numbers ({十二|shí èr}, {二十|èr shí}), and {第二|dì èr} means "second".

questions.stem: {昨天|zuó tiān}{我|wǒ}___ {去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}。 Choose the word (I didn't go to school yesterday).
questions.explanation: An action that didn't happen takes {没|méi}: {昨天|zuó tiān}{我|wǒ}{没|méi}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}。 {不|bù} is for now, habits and the future ({明天|míng tiān}{我|wǒ}{不去|bú qù}), and a {没|méi} sentence has no {了|le}.

questions.stem: Listen. Which is true?

audio.text: 我昨天没去学校，在家休息。

choices: The speaker went to school yesterday.
The speaker will rest at home tomorrow.
The speaker rested at school yesterday.
The speaker stayed at home yesterday.
questions.explanation: {我|wǒ}{昨天|zuó tiān}{没|méi}{去|qù}{学校|xué xiào}，{在|zài}{家|jiā}{休息|xiū xi} — I didn't go to school yesterday; I rested at home. {昨天|zuó tiān} (yesterday) comes early, and {没|méi} says it didn't happen.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I bought a book."?
questions.explanation: The completed-action {了|le} goes right after the verb, before an object with a number: {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{了|le}{一本|yì běn}{书|shū}。 It never goes before the verb or inside the object, and {没|méi} and {了|le} don't go together.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I didn't buy it."?
questions.explanation: The negative of a completed action is {没|méi} + verb, without {了|le}: {我|wǒ}{没|méi}{买|mǎi}。 {我|wǒ}{不|bù}{买|mǎi}{了|le} is a change of plan: "I'm not buying it any more".

questions.stem: Which sentence means "There's a cat in the room."?
questions.explanation: "There is" is place + {有|yǒu} + thing: {房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ}{有|yǒu}{一只|yì zhī}{猫|māo}。 {在|zài} works the other way round, for where a known thing is: {猫|māo}{在|zài}{房间|fáng jiān}{里|lǐ} (the cat is in the room).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "He gave me a book."?
questions.explanation: With two objects, the person comes first and the thing second: {给|gěi}{我|wǒ}{一本|yì běn}{书|shū}. ({了|le} after {给|gěi} would make it clearly completed: {他|tā}{给|gěi}{了|le}{我|wǒ}{一本|yì běn}{书|shū}。)
